Nationwide plays the long game in women’s soccer
article_text:
Nationwide Insurance has scored a multi-year extension of its deal to be the official insurance sponsor of the National Women’s Soccer League.

Nationwide held on to its position as presenting sponsor of the Lauren Holiday Impact Award, which honors NWSL players for outstanding community service and character off the pitch.

Nationwide will kick in a $50,000 donation to a charitable organization of the winner’s choice once announced, which will air Thursday on ESPN2 at 6:30 p.m. Eastern time, the insurer said in a statement.

To date, Nationwide has already passed on more than $600,000 to nonprofits selected by clubs and players through the Nationwide Community Impact Award and the Lauren Holiday Impact Award.

Columbus, Ohio-based Nationwide has been a league partner since 2021.

Several NWSL athletes will also get a chance to trade their cleats for office shoes when Nationwide hosts its annual “Experience Nationwide” professional development event at its Columbus headquarters beginning Nov. 30. The event is aimed at helping players score career opportunities beyond the pitch.

title: ISPS HANDA Expands Support for Golf as G4D Open Partner - Asia-Pacific Golf Confederation
article_text:
St Andrews, Scotland: ISPS HANDA is expanding its support for golf as the first-ever title partner of The G4D Open, the international championship for golfers with disabilities.

Established in 2023, The G4D Open – held annually in partnership by The R&A and the DP World Tour – is one of the most inclusive championships, featuring 80 male and female amateur and professional golfers.

The Championship will now be known as the ISPS HANDA G4D Open. In addition to being title partner, ISPS HANDA will introduce two new initiatives to the Championship to encourage and support participation from players worldwide:

· ISPS HANDA will cover the full entry fee of each G4D Open competitor, an initiative that will reduce the financial burden to compete and help create an environment in which more golfers with disabilities can perform on the international stage.

· The ISPS HANDA Inspiration Award will be an annual, monetary award which recognises an individual who has made a significant contribution to the promotion and development of golf for people with disabilities beyond competition itself. It will also expand the possibilities of golf for people with disabilities and look to inspire others into the sport.

The ISPS HANDA G4D Open extends the organisation’s commitment to golf at various levels of the sport, including title sponsorship of the Senior Open and support of the Women’s Amateur Asia-Pacific.

Dr Haruhisa Handa, ISPS HANDA Founder and Chairman, said: “Nearly four decades ago, a blind golfer’s joy in playing the game inspired me to champion the power of sport.

“I am proud that ISPS HANDA is becoming the first title partner of The G4D Open, building on the outstanding efforts of The R&A and DP World Tour to make golf more inclusive, break down barriers and create opportunities for golfers with disabilities around the world.”

Mark Darbon, Chief Executive of The R&A, said: “We thank ISPS HANDA for becoming the first title partner of The G4D Open and extending their significant contribution to golf.

“Our purpose at The R&A is to open golf to the world, inspiring people through our championships and leading golf’s future through working with our partners. The G4D Open is an important platform in demonstrating that golf is accessible and welcoming to all while encouraging more people with a disability to take up the sport.

“We greatly value the relationship between The R&A and ISPS HANDA and look forward to continuing the development of the Championship in the years ahead.”

Guy Kinnings, Chief Executive Officer of the European Tour Group, said: “We are delighted to welcome ISPS HANDA as the first-ever title partner of The G4D Open. They have been a tremendous supporter of golf for many years and have a genuine passion for using golf as a force for good, so they are a natural fit for this Championship.

“The DP World Tour has provided G4D golfers with high profile playing opportunities for several years and The G4D Open has quickly established itself as a world class event that showcases their extraordinary talent on a global stage. This commitment from ISPS HANDA, alongside our continued partnership with The R&A, will help us further elevate the Championship and inspire more people to see golf as a game for everyone.”

The world’s most talented golfers with disabilities play in The G4D Open, which was staged in Wales for the first time this year after three previous editions at Woburn. Simon Lee Seung-min from Korea and Germany’s Jennifer Sräga enjoyed memorable first victories in the respective men’s and women’s events at Celtic Manor Resort in May.

The Championship continues to be supported by EDGA (formally the European Disabled Golf Association) in an advisory role.

Irishman Brendan Lawlor, a two-time G4D Open Champion and an ISPS HANDA ambassador, added: “I’m delighted ISPS HANDA is becoming title partner of The G4D Open to expand their support of golf across various levels of the sport.

“The R&A, DP World Tour and EDGA put in so much work to stage the Championship and the support of ISPS HANDA will now further elevate its profile. As an ambassador, I know their passion for the power of sport and their dedication to inspire, break down barriers and create opportunities.

“Having competed in all four years of The G4D Open and winning the men’s event in 2023 and 2025, it’s a Championship that is very special to me and I look forward to its continued success.”

title: SA top sprinter Akani Simbine joins forces with Sibanye-Stillwater MyGold road race
article_text:
Sibanye-Stillwater and the Simbine Classic have announced a three-year sponsorship that will introduce the Sibanye-Stillwater MyGold 5km and 10km road races at the 2027 World Athletics Continental Tour event, providing recreational runners and walkers with the opportunity to participate in one of the country’s premier athletics showcases.

The MyGold races will make their debut in Pretoria on 17 April 2027, with mining company Sibanye-Stillwater holding the naming rights to both mass participation races, which form part of an expanded festival of athletics designed to bring communities, families, aspiring athletes and elite performers together through the power of sport.

All individuals who purchase a ticket to the Simbine Classic and make a R50 donation to the Akani Simbine Foundation will automatically receive an entry into the road race. Participants who complete the Sibanye-Stillwater MyGold 10km in under 60 minutes will also receive a commemorative medal, while all runners and walkers will have up to 80 minutes to complete the course.

The day’s programme will feature development sprint races for emerging young athletes, competitions showcasing South Africa’s rising track and field stars, and a world-class elite programme featuring local and international athletics icons. Spectators attending the event and audiences watching from home can also look forward to a vibrant entertainment offering throughout the day. Ticket sales and entry details for the road race will be announced in the coming weeks.

“We were very pleased with the success of the 2026 Simbine Classic, and we want to go even bigger and better in 2027,” said Akani Simbine, founder of the Simbine Classic.

“The introduction of the Sibanye-Stillwater MyGold road races allows us to create a platform where everyone can participate, whether they are chasing a personal best, taking their first steps into athletics, supporting a loved one, or competing on the world stage. Our vision is to make the Simbine Classic a true festival of athletics that inspires participation at every level.”

Sibanye-Stillwater’s sponsorship of the MyGold road races reflects its wider commitment to sport development, healthy lifestyles and the communities in which it operates. The partnership advances the company’s focus on inclusion and opportunity, while extending its support for youth development. As part of its commitment, the company will donate R1 million to the Akani Simbine Foundation, a non-profit organisation dedicated to empowering underserved youth through sports, education, and community welfare projects.

“The launch of the Sibanye-Stillwater MyGold 5km and 10km reinforces our commitment to creating opportunities that bring people together, promoting healthy lifestyles and inspiring the next generation of athletes. Our partnership with the Simbine Classic extends these opportunities beyond elite competition to one that encourages broad community participation and fosters social cohesion,” said Charl Keyter, Chief Financial Officer of Sibanye-Stillwater.

“Akani Simbine’s exceptional achievement in 2026 as the only athlete to run 100 metres in under 10 seconds for 12 consecutive years aligns with our own commitment to performance excellence. Our support of the Akani Simbine Foundation also complements our broader investments in education and sports development in our host communities.”

The addition of the MyGold mass participation race further strengthens the Simbine Classic’s ambition of becoming one of Africa’s premier athletics events, ensuring that the excitement and inspiration of the day can be experienced by athletes and supporters alike.

title: Zee’s Unite8 Sports secures broadcast rights for DP World ILT20 Season 5
article_text:
MUMBAI: The UAE is getting ready for a month of cricketing fireworks, and Indian viewers will have a front-row seat without leaving their sofas. Zee Entertainment Enterprises’ sports network Unite8 Sports will broadcast the fifth season of the DP World International League T20 (ILT20), bringing all 34 matches to television and streaming platforms from 21 November to 20 December 2026.

The tournament will be played across three UAE venues – Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah – with the grand final scheduled in Dubai. Every match will be telecast live on Unite8 Sports 1 in standard definition (SD) and high definition (HD), while digital viewers can stream the action on Hindi Zee5. Zee Zest, available in SD and HD, will carry the English-language television coverage.

The season begins on Saturday, 21 November, with defending champions Desert Vipers taking on MI Emirates at 8 pm IST. The opening fixture is a repeat of last season’s final, giving the tournament an early rematch between the two sides that finished Season 4 at the top.

Six franchises will compete for the Season 5 trophy, five of them backed by prominent Indian business groups. The line-up comprises:

Desert Vipers enter the season as defending champions after claiming their maiden ILT20 title in Season 4. They defeated MI Emirates by 46 runs in the final at Dubai International Stadium, setting up an immediate opportunity for their opponents to seek revenge in the new campaign.

With the same two teams opening the tournament, the first match offers more than just the start of the season: it brings last year’s final back into focus.

The fifth edition will also introduce significant changes to playing conditions, with a new ‘Batter Zone’ definition for wides and an expanded 60-second stop-clock rule.

Under the Batter Zone rule, a delivery will be called wide if the entire ball passes outside the batter zone at the popping crease, whether on the off side or the leg side. The change is intended to discourage negative bowling and create a fairer contest between bat and ball.

The stop clock, meanwhile, will now apply to batters as well as bowlers and fielding teams. Both batters must be ready for the next over to begin within 60 seconds of the previous over ending.

Teams will receive two warnings per innings for violations. From the third offence onwards, the fielding side will be penalised five runs. The rule also applies to glove changes, meaning these cannot be used to sidestep the time limit.

The changes bring greater emphasis on keeping the game moving while tightening the rules around deliveries that move too far away from the batter’s reach. For broadcasters and viewers, they could also make the pace of the contest a talking point throughout the season.

The ILT20 coverage adds another cricket property to Unite8 Sports’ growing portfolio. Bavesh Janavlekar, chief business officer of Unite8 Sports at Zee Entertainment Enterprises, said the network had expanded its live sports offering since its launch earlier this year.

Its existing portfolio includes India’s T20I tour of Zimbabwe, the FIFA World Cup 2026, Bundesliga, Serie A, the Indian Football League (IFL), Wrestling Xtreme Mania (WXM) and the Professional Golf Tour of India (PGTI).

Janavlekar said the addition of ILT20 Season 5 strengthened the network’s cricket offering and reflected Zee’s focus on building a multi-sport destination for Indian audiences. He also pointed to the new playing-condition changes and the availability of coverage in Hindi and English across television and Zee5 as ways to bring viewers closer to the action.

With 34 matches spread across three UAE venues, six franchises and new rules designed to keep the game sharper, the fifth season offers plenty of talking points. For Indian viewers, the broadcast schedule is straightforward: Unite8 Sports 1 and Zee Zest for television, and Hindi Zee5 for streaming, starting with Desert Vipers against MI Emirates at 8 pm IST on 21 November.

title: News: ESPN-NFLN studio, Phillies RSN, PGA Tour and more
article_text:
ESPN is consolidating its West Coast production to the NFL Network facility in Inglewood; the Philadelphia Phillies have reportedly done groundwork on what would be required to launch their own network; and select PGA Tour events will air on the ESPN linear network next month. Plus news on the Emirates NBA Cup, Elle Duncan, Jonathan Jones and ESPN.

ESPN shuttering L.A. Live studio, moving West Coast production to NFL Network building

ESPN will close its current Los Angeles studio space at L.A. Live and consolidate its West Coast production within the NFL Network facility in nearby Inglewood, as first reported by Austin Karp of Sports Business Journal. The approximately 160 employees who still worked at the L.A. Live facility will shift to new locations without planned layoffs. The move is expected to take place by early September.

“We are announcing the creation of a consolidated West Coast production center at Hollywood Park in Inglewood,” ESPN said in a statement provided to Sports Media Watch. “Featuring state-of-the-art technology, this facility will continue to serve as the home of NFL Network and NFL RedZone while also adding NBA Today and WNBA Countdown. As part of this process, we are closing our LA Production Center at L.A. Live, relocating production employees to Hollywood Park. We look forward to all of ESPN’s LA-based studio content originating from a single location, further enhancing creativity and collaboration, with expansion possible in the future.”

ESPN first started airing shows out of the L.A. Live space in April 2009, including a Los Angeles edition of “SportsCenter” with anchors such as Stan Verrett, Linda Cohn and Neil Everett. The network ended that edition of the show last year, opting to centralize most editions of the studio program to its Bristol, Conn. studios. Verrett and Cohn have since left ESPN.

The facility has also served as the home for a majority of NBA studio programming, such as “NBA Today” and the “NBA/WNBA Countdown” franchises. The shift does not directly impact ESPN LA 710, which will continue to broadcast from the Good Karma Brands offices in the area. Good Karma Brands purchased the radio station from ESPN as part of a larger transaction announced in December 2021.

The Philadelphia Phillies have done groundwork on trying to create their own television network, according to a report by Matt Gelb of The Athletic. The organization is in the midst of a deal with Comcast-owned NBC Sports Philadelphia under a reported 25-year agreement that gives them a 25% minority stake in the network. Gelb cited sources who said there are “legitimate doubts” as to “how much longer [the network] will last as NBCUniversal divests from its RSN business.”

The network, which like all other NBCUniversal properties will be spun off from Comcast in the next year, is facing an “uncertain financial future,” according to Gelb. NBC Sports currently owns four regional sports networks that air live game broadcasts for nine professional teams across the four major sports leagues. The company formerly owned a Chicago-based RSN that ceased operations in 2024 (prior to the launch of Chicago Sports Network) and the prior year sold its equity stake in the D.C. RSN now known as Monumental Sports Network. Prior to these divestitures, the company also shuttered NBC Sports Northwest, which broadcast Portland Trail Blazers games prior to Root Sports.

The RSN business has been in a state of flux for the last several years, headlined by bankruptcy and eventual collapse of Main Street Sports Group. Warner Bros. Discovery exited the RSN business a few years ago, including the sales of AT&T SportsNet Southwest, Root Sports and AT&T SportsNet Pittsburgh.

MLB commissioner Rob Manfred has indicated that MLB plans to centralize local media rights in 2028. The league has also tied media-related concerns, particularly equal revenue sharing, to the economic system it is proposing as part of ongoing CBA negotiations.

ESPN will carry coverage of the PGA Tour FedExCup Playoffs on its flagship linear network for the first time this year, airing a total of 12 hours across six days during the FedEx St. Jude Championship, BMW Championship and Tour Championship. The telecasts will air in two-hour windows, primarily on Friday and Saturday mornings.

ESPN acquired a PGA Tour media rights package in 2020 that has almost exclusively consisted of streaming coverage on ESPN+. One exception came earlier this year, when ESPN simulcast coverage of the Farmers Insurance Open — featuring Brooks Koepka‘s return to the PGA Tour from LIV Golf — on its flagship network.

The PGA Tour is in a state of transition under CEO and future commissioner Brian Rolapp, who previously worked for the NFL as its chief media and business officer. Since joining the PGA Tour last year, Rolapp has introduced several changes, including forthcoming alterations to its competitive structure that includes a two-tiered system with promotion and relegation. The PGA Tour also introduced a limited-time returning member program under Rolapp that permitted golfers who departed for LIV Golf to come back, albeit with some limitations.

The primary PGA Tour media rights deals with CBS and NBC do not expire until 2030, but John Ourand of Puck reported earlier this year that Rolapp had told the incumbents he is open to negotiating “in the next year or two.”

Plus: NBA, Elle Duncan, ESPN.com, Jonathan Jones

- The National Basketball Association laid off some employees on Wednesday as the league seeks to prioritize “key growth areas,” including local media, the WNBA and the looming NBA Europe league, NBA commissioner Adam Silver said in an internal memo obtained by Tom Friend of Sports Business Journal. The league recently hired former NESN GM Matt Volk to lead its local media department, a move that comes ahead of the NBA reportedly looking to launch a streaming hub for local broadcasts. Silver said that the investments “will best position us to achieve our key objectives, including a better understanding of our fans, improving the game and viewership, and driving global growth across our leagues.”

title: Shohei Ohtani Secures Career-Long Sponsorship With New Balance
article_text:
[Sports Chosun Reporter Na Yu-ri] Shohei Ohtani has been promised sponsorship until the day he retires from his playing career.

On November 20 (Korean time), the U.S. fashion magazine 'GQ' reported, "Ohtani has signed a historic extension with New Balance."

According to the report, Ohtani agreed to extend his sponsorship contract with long-time partner New Balance, a sports brand, until his retirement from active play. 'GQ' reported, "Japanese baseball icon Ohtani has made a groundbreaking deal, extending his sponsorship with a long-time partner until the end of his baseball career, adding a new chapter to his achievements. While only a handful of athletes, such as LeBron James and Cristiano Ronaldo (both Nike), and Damian Lillard (Adidas), have secured lifetime sponsorships, Ohtani’s deal is the first to cover an entire playing career and the first such case in Major League Baseball."

In an interview with 'GQ', Ohtani said, "I have great trust in the brand. Of course, we’ve built a good relationship. They’ve listened well to my requests, which requires significant trust. Our relationship has been really good and smooth so far. There was no hesitation in extending the contract."

New Balance, which will sponsor Ohtani until his retirement, has decided to rename its in-house research lab. Originally named the "Sports Research Lab," it will now be called the "Shohei Ohtani Sports Research Lab."

Ohtani recently visited the Boston headquarters to analyze spikes for the next season. Ohtani recorded a disappointing performance this season due to injuries to his left knee and right biceps. He revealed, "There were moments this year when my heel slipped upon landing during pitching." Consequently, the spikes he will wear next season are expected to address these issues.

As the only two-way player in Major League Baseball, Ohtani does not change his shoes when switching between pitching and batting, wearing the same spikes for both.

In the 'GQ' interview, when asked what advice and encouragement he would give to children who want to be like him, Ohtani said, "If you want to succeed, baseball is a sport that requires a lot of repetitive practice. You must consistently build on the fundamentals. Once you reach a certain level, baseball becomes really, really difficult. At that point, you should reconsider why you play baseball. Is it because you love the sport? If you have that passion and love, you can overcome tough times."

Reporter Na Yu-ri youll@sportschosun.com

title: Frontier Airlines & BarkleyOKRP ink the world’s first-ever official sports NIL butt sponsorship
article_text:
November, 2026.- Most airlines launch premium seats with typical luxury marketing and visuals. Not Frontier Airlines. They decided to pen the world’s first-ever official sports NIL butt sponsorship, literally sponsoring the actual rear ends of college football’s heaviest players.

Frontier and BarkleyOKRP partnered with two #2-ranked University of Georgia offensive linemen, Jahzare Jackson (6’10”, 350 lbs) and Juan Gaston (6’7”, 360 lbs), for what they’re calling the world’s “biggest” NIL deal. And they took the signing quite literally. The 710-pound duo made their endorsements official by dipping their backsides in paint and stamping their contracts with their butts.

The campaign comes as Frontier works to reshape perceptions of the airline, introducing a series of cabin enhancements that include First Class seating, more extra-legroom options, in-seat power and Starlink Wi-Fi. Rather than relying on traditional premium airline advertising, BarkleyOKRP turned an NIL partnership into an unexpected demonstration of one of those upgrades: If Frontier’s new First Class seats can comfortably accommodate two SEC offensive linemen, they can accommodate just about anyone.

The campaign launches November 18 across social and digital channels, bringing an unexpected twist to both airline advertising and the increasingly crowded world of NIL deals.

title: Fox, Netflix Lead As Rivals Exit World Cup Media Rights Race
article_text:
FIFA’s sought-after frenzy for the U.S. media rights to the 2030 men’s World Cup is turning into a far quieter affair after several major networks have removed themselves from bidding.

NBCUniversal is not pursuing the rights, either for its English-language NBC broadcast network or for the Spanish-language Telemundo, according to industry sources and multiple reports. That follows similar retreats in recent days by ESPN, CBS Sports and TNT Sports parent company Skydance, Apple, and YouTube.

That leaves Fox, which aired this year’s World Cup to record-setting levels, and Netflix, the U.S. rights holder for next year’s Women’s World Cup, as the top candidates for the English-language rights in 2030.

Univision is likely to be a key player for Spanish-language rights in the U.S., as that broadcast network has far greater reach than the cable-based Fox Deportes, and is now said to be working in direct cooperation with Fox.

Amazon has also tendered a separate bid.

The relatively low amount of jockeying for the World Cup rights is due to a tough combination of internal and external factors. FIFA, buoyed by this year’s historic television audiences, is said to be seeking more than $1.5 billion for rights to the 2030 event, and a similar amount for the 2034 tournament. Fox and Telemundo combined to pay $1.285 billion for the 2026 World Cup rights in the U.S.

This year’s North America-based event, however, provided convenient broadcast windows for American viewers. That will not be nearly as readily available in 2030, as that event is split between Morocco, Portugal, and Spain, after a set of initial matches in Uruguay, Argentina, and Paraguay. The bulk of the tournament will be happening five time zones ahead of the U.S. East Coast, and eight ahead of the U.S. West Coast. Live matches airing in U.S. primetime will be impossible.

That means it’s highly likely, if not altogether certain, that the 2030 World Cup will fail to match the 2026 viewership figures in the U.S. Fox averaged 7.74 million viewers per match for the English-language coverage this year, while Telemundo averaged 6.3 million. The figures for both networks doubled the comparable averages from the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

The 2034 men’s World Cup doesn’t get any easier, relative to U.S. viewership, as that event will be held in Saudi Arabia, creating an even greater time difference. It’s also possible that the event shifts to a fall window, as the one in 2022 did, which is far more crowded on the sports calendar.

The 2030 World Cup rights bidding, set to finish by the end of the year, also is happening as nearly every major U.S. media company is in the midst of large-scale corporate change that is bringing heavy financial costs and job losses—regardless of what happens in the FIFA negotiations.

NBCUniversal is in the process of separating from parent company Comcast, a move that will carry a restructuring charge of at least $1 billion. Skydance just completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, and now carries a debt load of about $80 billion. ESPN and its parent company Disney are shedding thousands of jobs and are seeking annual operating savings of at least $3 billion.

Even Fox, now seen as a strong favorite to retain World Cup rights, has talked about the need to potentially “rebalance” its sports rights in the wake of likely fee hikes to keep NFL programming.

As these and other media outlets have held quarterly earnings calls with analysts in recent weeks, a consistent theme has been “financial discipline” when evaluating any potential sports rights acquisition.

“The thing I would tell you is we always look at deals with discipline and an eye towards driving value for the shareholders, as well as our fans,” Disney CFO Hugh Johnston said on an earnings call this week.

Fox executive chairman and CEO Lachlan Murdoch echoed a similar refrain earlier this month, saying, “We obviously were happy with the performance of the World Cup this past year, and we will be looking at the rights for 2030 and 2034 in a disciplined manner, as we would with all sports rights.”

title: ATP Ventures unveiled, men’s top tour significantly increasing prize money
article_text:
The board of men's tennis' top-tier ATP has given the green light to launch ATP Ventures, a new vehicle set to manage the body's commercial and media rights.

This comes as part of a wider sweep of changes to the structure of men's top-tier tennis that will also see the total prize money available to players increase to over $350 million by 2028. That figure is currently set at $270 million.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

It also forms the latest chapter in OneVision, the long-term campaign to increase the ATP's revenue and commercial appeal that began in 2023 (having been in development since 2020).

The creation of ATP Ventures will bring all of the media and sponsorship rights for the ATP Tour under one roof for the first time.

It comes with plans to create a joint commercial venture between the ATP and women's tennis' WTA, which had fallen through earlier this year.

The launch of this new vehicle has been unanimously approved by the ATP's board, alongside the shareholders of the ATP Media wing.

It comes as the end-of-year ATP Finals take place currently in Turin, Italy.

The rights combined will cover those held by the ATP Tour itself, ATP Media, as well as those held by the Tennis Data Innovations vehicle.

The Florida-based ATP has said that work on the agreement will begin next year, and that the venture will become operational from the start of 2028.

Andrea Gaudenzi, chair of the ATP, commented: "The next phase of OneVision strengthens our product, while ATP Ventures will transform how we take it to market. Bringing ATP Media, TDI and our central sponsorship business together under one aligned commercial strategy gives us a huge opportunity to grow the Tour, tell a stronger story around our players and bring fans closer to the sport.”

Regarding the financial element of this news, the increased player prize money will include an increase in the bonus pool figure to $50 million, a bonus of $25 million covering end-of-year rankings, and $26 million in player pension funding.

As a contrast, the 2026 bonus pool for ATP professionals only comes to $21 million.

The ATP Tour announced earlier this month that central partnership revenues had increased 49% year-on-year in 2026, to more than $100 million, for the first time.

This came on the back of new agreements and expanded investments from long-standing partners including flag carrier airline Emirates, tech company Infosys, parts manufacturer Nitto, luxury carmaker Lexus, home appliances corporation Haier, and tyre manufacturer Yokohama.

Overall, OneVision represents the organization's long-term strategic plan to reform professional tennis, align interests between players and tournaments, and grow the sport’s commercial digital footprint.

Earlier this year, the tour re-elected Gaudenzi as chairman for a third term until 2028, meanwhile.

Recent growth has also been driven by the launch of the ATP’s dedicated Licensing and Retail team within its central business division in 2025, which has opened the door to new licensing agreements, including K-Swiss’ agreement to create a collection of five ATP-branded tennis shoes.

title: Apple doubles down on Formula 1 with F1 Academy rights in US
article_text:
Technology giant Apple, rights holder of motor racing’s Formula 1 (F1) in the US, has expanded its partnership with the major property by adding rights in the country to F1 Academy, the all-female racing series.

The deal, starting in 2027, will see Apple TV provide coverage of every F1 Academy qualifying session and race throughout each season.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

F1 Academy acts as a support series for F1 and in 2027 will feature at seven Grands Prix, including Jeddah (Saudi Arabia), Shanghai (China), Montreal (Canada), Silverstone (UK), and Budapest (Hungary), before the two final US rounds in Austin and Las Vegas.

Apple TV's live coverage will be complemented with in-depth programming and exclusive original content surrounding the championship, while its platform will offer customizable features for following drivers and the progress of the competition.

The new rights consolidate Apple TV’s F1 coverage in the US, having secured a five-year agreement to become the series’ exclusive US broadcast partner from 2026 as part of a deal valued at around $140 million.

For F1 Academy, the rights deal comes as the series enters its fifth season, having launched in 2022 as a development series. Since then, it has expanded its calendar internationally and increased the profiles of young drivers including Alba Hurup Larsen, Alisha Palmowski, and Emma Felbermayr.

The agreement also expands the series’ global visibility, having secured several high-profile broadcasters as rightsholders, including Sky (UK), ESPN (Latin America), BeIN (MENA and Southeast Asia), SuperSport (Pan-regional Africa), Fox Sports (Australia), Sky New Zealand, DAZN (Spain, Portugal), FanCode (India), and Televisa (Mexico).

Sky Italia (Italy) and Globo (Brazil) hold highlights rights in their respective markets.

Susie Wolff, F1 Academy’s managing director, said: “We have built incredible momentum in the U.S., with a growing and increasingly engaged audience following our drivers and their journeys.

“To have a global brand like Apple recognize the potential of our sport and commit its platform and resources to helping us reach new audiences is a powerful statement of how far we have come and where we are heading. Visibility remains fundamental to our mission.”

The new deal adds to F1 Academy’s growing portfolio of partners, which most recently saw sports apparel giant Nike and banking firm Standard Chartered added as official sponsors starting from 2027.

Earlier this year, F1 Academy added US beauty retailer Sephora to its growing sponsorship stable, which also includes TAG Heuer, American Express, Gatorade, Lego, Puma, Salesforce, Standard Chartered, TeamViewer, Wella, Pirelli, and Aramco.

During its inaugural season airing F1, Apple has looked to capitalize on F1’s growing fan base to capture more subscribers for its platform. Earlier this year, the tech giant announced a partnership with streaming giant Netflix to showcase the Canadian Grand Prix between May 22 and 24 on its platform.

Last year, it also released an F1- based movie starring Hollywood star Brad Pitt and F1 driver Lewis Hamilton.

It also dropped its paywall for the three-day Austrian GP weekend from June 26 to 28, with the free coverage spanning practices, qualifying sessions, and the race itself.

title: CANADA’S WOMEN’S SEVENS TEAM CONFIRMS ROSTER FOR FIRST TWO STOPS OF 2027 HSBC SVNS SERIES
article_text:
The squad for Canada’s Women’s Sevens Team has been named for the first two tournaments of the 2027 HSBC SVNS Series, with Canada set to play in Dubai on November 28-29 and Cape Town on December 5-6.

November 19, 2026 (Langford, BC) — The squad for Canada’s Women’s Sevens Team has been named for the first two tournaments of the 2027 HSBC SVNS Series, with Canada set to play in Dubai on November 28-29 and Cape Town on December 5-6.

The 2027 HSBC SVNS Series brings an added level of excitement and intrigue, with qualification for the 2028 LA Olympics on the line. The top four teams in the standings following the final tournament in New York, prior to the start of the HSBC SVNS World Championships, will secure Olympic qualification. That number increases to five if the USA finishes among the top four teams.

With Olympic qualification at stake, the 2027 HSBC SVNS Series marks the beginning of Canada’s journey to the LA Olympics in 2028, following the team’s historic performance at the Paris 2024 Olympics, where Canada captured a silver medal.

"The road to LA 2028 is well under way, and our focus is on the opening leg of the 2027 series in Dubai and Cape Town," said Jocelyn Barrieau, Head Coach of Canada's Women's Sevens Team. "This roster reflects both experienced Sevens players that led us to success in the 2025/26 season and some new faces which will continue to build depth across this program in this Olympic qualification season."

Several Canadian players were unavailable for selection as they are competing in the Premiership Women’s Rugby (PWR) league in England. Breanne Nicholas, Adia Pye and Larah Wright are the three returning players from the Canadian squad that captured bronze at the final stop of the 2026 HSBC SVNS World Championship in Bordeaux, France. That tournament marked the last time Canada’s Women’s Sevens Team took the field together.

Set to make their international sevens debuts for Canada are Lizzie Gibson, Aurora Bowie, Ava Van Saten and Olivia Newsome. Gibson and Bowie both featured regularly for Canada’s Women’s 15s Team throughout 2026, while Van Saten was named MVP at the 2026 FISU World University Championships, helping Canada capture gold. Van Saten scored all four of Canada’s tries in a 20-0 victory over France in the final. Newsome recently helped the University of Victoria win gold at the 2026 U SPORTS National Rugby Championship.

Next year, the 2027 HSBC SVNS Series returns to BC Place Stadium in Vancouver on March 6-7. Canadian rugby fans will have the opportunity to watch both Canada’s Men’s and Women’s Sevens Teams compete on home soil. Tickets are available now at vansevens.com.

title: Blitzboks include two uncapped players in Dubai squad as SVNS series returns
article_text:
Blitzbok head coach Philip Snyman has named a 13-man squad for the opening tournament of the season, where Selvyn Davids will also earn his 50th tournament cap.

Former Junior Springbok wing JC Mars has been selected as an outside back, while FNB UP-Tuks centre Van Reenen Kruger has been included among the forwards.

Siviwe Soyizwapi will captain the side in the absence of Impi Visser, having previously led the Blitzboks in Singapore and Perth last season.

Davids is one of six players who featured in last year's Dubai tournament, where South Africa finished fifth. The team bounced back in impressive fashion, winning four tournaments on their way to claiming the overall series title before securing a second successive HSBC SVNS World Championship crown.

The 31-year-old Davids made his international sevens debut in Hong Kong during the 2016/17 season and has since scored 793 points, including 107 tries, for South Africa. Meanwhile, Zain Davids and Ryan Oosthuizen are set to feature in their ninth Dubai tournaments, having each been part of six Blitzbok title-winning campaigns there.

Snyman said selection was based on current form in training, while also taking into account the need to build depth within the squad.

"JC has been in the SA Rugby pathway since his school days, while 'Van' had a brilliant Varsity Cup campaign and once we brought them into the wider group, they quickly rose to the challenge."

Snyman saluted Selvyn Davids, who has also captained the Blitzboks, on his half century: "He is just such an awesome team player and playmaker and to have him fit and ready is just great. The same with Siviwe, who will take the reins with Impi not quite fit and available for this tournament. One of our strengths is a strong leadership group, which makes my life much easier as a coach."

The Dubai tournament takes place on 28 and 29 November and South Africa have been drawn in Pool A with Australia, the USA and Argentina. The series then moves to the DHL Stadium for the HSBC SVNS Cape Town on 5 and 6 December.

title: Verizon renews LaLiga sponsorship amid World Cup years
article_text:
Seven years after first signing on as a regional sponsor of LaLiga in the US and Canada, Verizon is renewing the deal under another multiyear agreement, the Spanish pro soccer league shared exclusively with Marketing Brew.

It’s the second time Verizon has re-upped its LaLiga sponsorship that began in the 2019-20 season, after first renewing it in 2023. The announcement comes sandwiched between two World Cups, with the men’s tournament held this past summer in North America, and the women’s coming up in Brazil next year.

With soccer fandom making strides in the US following the World Cup, Verizon has looked to stake its claim in the sport in a way that could help the brand stand out among other sponsors. In addition to serving as the official wireless telecommunications partner of LaLiga in the US and Canada, Verizon is hosting sweepstakes that provide fans access to the league, a sponsorship strategy the brand has carried over from its NFL and World Cup work.

For LaLiga, brands that want to activate experientially as opposed to just through official marks or media buys can help support the mission of growing fandom around the world, Nicolás García Hemme, managing director of LaLiga North America, told Marketing Brew.

“We go to market together, and the fans feel that the brand is very much there with LaLiga,” Hemme said. “It’s not just LaLiga delivering a logo.”

The latest deal focuses on the brand’s Verizon Shine loyalty program, which offers sweepstakes and merch drops through its app that include experiences with LaLiga like trips to Spain and meet and greets with legends from the league.

“Extending our long-standing partnership with LaLiga allows us to meaningfully fuel soccer fandom as momentum continues to surge,” Justin Toman, Verizon’s VP of partnerships, said in an email.

One complication to growing fandom is that soccer is a fragmented sport, Hemme said, and not just in terms of media rights.

“When you talk about basketball, you have the NBA,” he said. “When you talk about American football, you have the NFL. Then you talk soccer, and you have local soccer with MLS and the NWSL, then you have Liga MX, a huge deal here in the US due to the Hispanic population, and you have all the European soccer competition coming to the market.”

To stand out to sponsors in the US—which also include Walmart and Lowe’s—Hemme said his team leans into a few selling points of LaLiga, including some of its teams with rabid global fandom like Real Madrid and FC Barcelona, as well as the league’s connection with various Hispanic communities.

LaLiga’s growing audience in the US certainly doesn’t hurt among brands, either. The league had record US viewership across ESPN platforms for its 2025-26 season with more than 20 million viewers, up 10% YoY.

After the World Cup, Barcelona and Elche CF opened the 2026-27 season with 1 million viewers on ESPN platforms, making it the most-watched English-language match for LaLiga on the network. El Clásico, the iconic matchup between Barcelona and Real Madrid, averaged 2.4 million viewers on ABC and ESPN Deportes last month, up more than 50% from last season to become the most-watched LaLiga match for ESPN.

The involvement of sponsors like Verizon help support LaLiga’s efforts to grow that fandom even further, especially as the league looks to build its reputation among people outside of its core audience of Hispanic fans, Hemme said.

“For these [new] audiences,” he said, “you have to find other angles” to build affinity, including the more lifestyle-oriented experiences.

title: F1 swaps Puma for Nike as apparel partner, expands Standard Chartered deal
Bossjob lands Leicester City front-of-shirt deal
article_text:
Leicester City have signed AI-powered recruitment platform Bossjob as their new principal partner, with its branding appearing on the front of the men’s first-team shirt for the rest of the 2026/27 season.

Bossjob’s logo will debut on Saturday, 21st November, when the Foxes travel to Huddersfield Town in Sky Bet League One.

Headquartered in Singapore, Bossjob connects candidates directly with employers and hiring managers. It has offices in Singapore, the Philippines, Indonesia and Japan, and is now expanding across Europe, North America and the Middle East. The deal also opens a new sponsorship category for the club as it looks to diversify its commercial interests.

Russell Jones, Commercial Director at Leicester City, said, “We welcome Bossjob as our new Principal Partner for the remainder of the season and look forward to building a strong relationship over the coming months.

“Through the partnership, we look forward to introducing Bossjob to our supporters and wider audiences, while supporting the company’s ambitions to develop its international profile. The agreement also provides an opportunity to work with an international partner operating in a new sponsorship category for the Club – an important step as we look to diversify our commercial interests and open up new markets in the future.”

title: Nike signs Formula 1 apparel deal
article_text:
The long-term partnership will see Nike become F1’s apparel and uniform supplier from 2027, extending its push into elite European sport later this month.

Under the deal, Nike will create co-branded uniforms worn by staff at F1 events worldwide. It will also release Formula 1 x Nike capsule collections spanning footwear, apparel and accessories, alongside performance innovations and race-weekend experiences for fans.

The first collection, a limited Las Vegas Grand Prix x Nike capsule, launches today at the F1 Hub and Nike’s Las Vegas stores ahead of this year’s Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Nike will also support F1 ACADEMY, the all-female driver series, as its sporting apparel partner, working with the next generation of drivers on performance innovation, design and technology.

The agreement comes days after Nike secured a four-year deal to supply the match ball for UEFA’s Champions League, Europa League and Conference League from the 2027-28 season, ending Adidas’ 26-year hold on European club football’s top competition.

Stefano Domenicali, President and CEO of Formula 1, said, “Formula 1 and Nike are two of the world’s most iconic brands, united by a relentless drive to innovate, perform at the highest level, and inspire people to push beyond what is possible. Formula 1 is experiencing unprecedented global growth, reaching hundreds of millions of fans and engaging one of the most passionate, diverse and dynamic communities in sport. Nike’s unique ability to sit at the intersection of sport, culture and inspiration makes them the ideal partner as we enter our next chapter.“

Elliott Hill, President and CEO of Nike, said, “Formula 1 is driven by competition, speed and a constant push to innovate. That’s an athlete mindset, and it’s one we share at Nike. Together, we have an incredible opportunity to bring new energy to the sport, serve its athletes and inspire fans around the world.”

title: The great US rights freeze: dancing to the NFL’s tune
SailGP brings in MassMutual as title sponsor for San Francisco return
article_text:
International sailing series SailGP has unveiled MassMutual, the US-based insurance company, as the title sponsor of its San Francisco Sail Grand Prix next year.

After a one-season hiatus, SailGP will be returning to the Bay Area for the sixth time from April 3-4, 2027.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

As well as its title partner designation, MassMutual will serve as the exclusive life insurance, official wealth management, and official annuities partner of the event.

The firm will benefit from prominent branding and global broadcast visibility, as well as an interactive race stadium footprint and exclusive waterfront hospitality.

Russell Coutts, SailGP co-founder and CEO, said: “San Francisco is known for an incredible combination of strong winds, dynamic race conditions, and a natural amphitheater that is tailor-made for SailGP’s stadium racing.

“Add in passionate fans, world-class athletes and a premier title partner like MassMutual, and it is guaranteed to be a standout event on our calendar next season.”

SailGP claims to have generated a $12.2 million economic impact from the 2025 event in San Francisco.

Last month, the series also announced global payments giant American Express as the title sponsor of its upcoming inaugural Hong Kong Sail Grand Prix.

The American Express Hong Kong Sail Grand Prix will take place on January 23 and 24, opening the campaign in the Victoria Harbor area.

Hong Kong is one of two new locations added to the SailGP calendar for the 2027 campaign, the other being Italy, Rome, specifically, unveiled in late May.

The Far East country is SailGP’s first race in the East Asian market since Singapore hosted in the 2022-23 campaign, though the series has held multiple events in the Middle East and Oceania in the interim period.

The 2027 schedule will feature 13 races across the season, with the season-opening Hong Kong Sail Grand Prix to be followed by the return of the Australia Sail Grand Prix in Perth (which opened the 2026 season) on an as-yet-unconfirmed date in February.

After Perth will be the North American swing of events, starting with San Francisco, then Bermuda (May 1 and 2), Halifax, Canada (May 15 and16), and New York, US (June 5 and 6).

The tour will then embark on a European swing, featuring the return of sail Grand Prix races in Portsmouth, UK (July 24 and 25), Sassnitz, Germany (August 14 and15), Valencia, Spain (September 4 and 5), and Rome, on September 11 and 12.

There will be two more regular-season races after this, in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil (October 9 and 10) and Dubai, UAE (November 20 and 21), before the season-ending 2027 SailGP Championship Grand Final, which will take place in either November or December at a to-be-confirmed location.

title: ILT20 in multi-year Decimal Data deal ahead of fifth season
article_text:
Cricket data and odds specialist Decimal Data has struck a deal to partner with the International League T20 (ILT20), the UAE-based men's Twenty20 franchise competition.

Through a deal unveiled yesterday, described as a long-term agreement, Decimal Data now becomes the official data and video partner for the six-team competition.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The agreement has been made public ahead of the 2026 edition of the franchise league, taking place between November 22 (this coming Sunday) and December 20.

The deal was brokered through the Sportfive agency, which has a long-running commercial rights relationship in place with the ILT20.

It entails Decimal Data collecting fast data from "dedicated official positions" inside the ILT20 venues, and then supplying that data to licensed sportsbook partners of the league.

Andrew Ashenden, Decimal Data's chief executive, commented: "Our dedicated official positions inside the venues will allow us to deliver the speed, precision and depth of data that our customers rely on, direct from the action. This long-term partnership expands our extensive official cricket rights portfolio and reflects our commitment to investing in the sport.”

Late September saw Decimal Data unveil a deal with the Cricket Australia governing body. The arrangement covers marquee cricket events until 2031, including the men’s and women’s editions of the Big Bash League, domestic cricket and Australian men’s and women’s home internationals.

Through this collaboration, the firm will utilize its dedicated team of over 120 cricket analysts and trading technology to manage official data distribution and modeling across all match formats.

Data rights deals, and those covering the provision of such licenses to betting brands and sportsbooks, have become a growing part of cricket properties' portfolios over recent years.

The 2026 ILT20 will be the fifth season of the franchise tournament, which launched in 2023. Since then, it has attracted a significant number of top-tier players from the world's strongest cricketing nations.

Dubai-based logistics and shipping heavyweight DP World has held title rights since the competition's inception.

title: Apollo scraps $2bn loan to Man City owners; Hull partner with Corpay
article_text:
The Apollo Sports Capital investment firm has reportedly pulled the plug on a potential $2 billion loan to City Football Group (CFG), the parent company of English soccer giants Manchester City and 12 other clubs, despite the two parties reaching the final stages of negotiations.

According to the Financial Times (FT), the financing was intended to provide additional liquidity for the ownership group and to refinance its existing credit facilities, but Apollo ended the talks after Manchester City were recently found guilty of significant financial breaches.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The FT report stated that Companies House filings show that club owner Sheikh Mansour instead injected £100 million of equity into CFG through his Newton Investment and Development vehicle in the month after an independent commission published its findings in September.

The commission found Manchester City guilty of 114 of 115 financial breach charges laid by the top-flight Premier League and revealed that the club artificially inflated its organic revenue by over £900 million ($1.19 billion) across nine years.

A 40-page report contains details of how the Manchester club – which won three Premier League titles during the nine years these financial breaches took place, between 2009 and 2018 – concocted 'sham' sponsorship deals with commercial partners to inflate its organic revenue and thus not fall foul of the league's Financial Fair Play (FFP) rules.

City filed inaccurate accounts for every single season during this time period – if these had been filed properly, the club would have broken league spending limits significantly, as well as those set down by European soccer's governing body UEFA.

Essentially, City used owner funding from its Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) ownership vehicle to top up and boost the value of sponsorship deals signed with Abu Dhabi-based partners between 2009 and 2018. As the commission put it, the club was "relying on sham agreements to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs."

In total, the club recorded £949.9 million in sponsorship income across the nine seasons in question – the commission found that only £119.2 million of this actually came from sponsors, with the other £830.6 million simply provided by the club owners instead.

Man City continues to protest its innocence and lodged an appeal in early October, which will be heard in mid-December.

A rule introduced by the Premier League in the summer requires appeal hearings to conclude within 12 weeks and decisions to follow within 30 days, although that timeframe can be set aside if necessary.

Should City's appeal fail, the commission has wide-ranging powers to impose sanctions ranging from fines and points deductions to expulsion from the league.

The collapse of the loan deal with Apollo reflects the uncertainty surrounding the outcome of City's appeal and the sanctions that could follow should it prove unsuccessful when a judgment is delivered in the new year.

The private equity group launched its Apollo Sports Capital branch in 2025 and has already acquired a major sports team in the European market, taking a majority stake in Spanish soccer's Atletico Madrid last year.

Recently, the firm also agreed a major $2.6 billion financing deal with the New York Yankees, the iconic Major League Baseball (MLB) franchise, that includes an equity stake in the team.

Earlier this year, Apollo also led a $225 million investment into Major League Pickleball and the PPA Tour, the two largest professional organizations for the US-based racket sport.

Through a multi-year agreement, the company will become the club’s official foreign exchange (FX) partner.

As part of the deal, Corpay Cross Border will deliver FX risk management solutions to support Hull’s day-to-day business operations. In addition, its platform will enable the club to manage global payments through a single point of access.

The partnership comes just a month after Corpay announced a deal with Newcastle United.

Over the past few years, Corpay has become a prominent sports sponsor across several major markets, with a particularly strong presence in soccer.

The US-based company has tie-ups with fellow English Premier League sides Manchester City and Everton, Spanish giants Real Madrid, Italian Serie A heavyweights AC Milan, US outfit Atlanta United, and Major League Soccer.

In its return to the Premier League for the first time since the 2016-17 season, Hull is currently 13th with 11 points.

title: Leicester City terminate shirt sponsorship after adult film star backlash
article_text:
There was a time when Leicester City could do no wrong.

The Foxes went from one of the greatest underdog stories in sporting history to FA Cup winners, capturing the imagination of football supporters around the world. Today, however, the club find themselves fighting a very different battle, with financial troubles, successive relegations and a series of controversies threatening to tarnish their remarkable legacy.

Their latest scandal, involving a betting sponsor and an adult film performer, is perhaps another indication of just how difficult it has been for the club to find stability.

Few will ever forget their remarkable and awe-inspiring English Premier League championship run that had the entire world rooting for them during the 2015/16 season. As recently as 2021, the Foxes lifted the FA Cup.

Since those heady days, though, the club has been mired in controversy and a fall from grace that will be noted in the history books for years to come, with that cup triumph one of the few bright spots.

In 2025, the club was relegated from the elite division to the Championship, and a year later they dropped down again to League One. Currently, they are 11th in the third tier, having won only five of their 14 matches thus far.

Financial mismanagement, a carousel of managers and breaches of league financial rules have plagued the club since their famous title-winning campaign. But their latest controversy has further undermined their standing.

As reported by several media outlets, including the BBC, Leicester's main shirt sponsor, BC.GAME, parted ways with the club this week following a backlash over the betting company's appointment of Russian adult film performer Eva Elfie as their brand ambassador. Setting aside Elfie's appointment, with the company justifying her appointment due to her reach within the eSports and gaming communities, the BC.GAME sponsorship had been heavily questioned since its announcement in 2024, given that the company is an unlicensed gambling company in the UK.

In response to the Elfie announcement, the Foxes Trust — who are the official supporters' club of the team — said in a statement this week: "Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people's lives, in particular young people.

"Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?"

In response, the club issued a statement on Wednesday confirming that the sponsorship had been terminated by "mutual consent" with immediate effect. They also announced a returns policy for supporters who had bought shirts bearing the BC.GAME branding through official club channels within the previous 28 days.

"Since the partnership was announced in 2024, the trust has consistently made clear that BC Game, for numerous reasons, does not reflect the values of our club or its supporters," the Foxes Trust said, after the sponsorship was terminated.

"That view has been shared by the great majority of fans who responded to our surveys. The recent partnership with an adult content creator only deepened those concerns and the trust felt the need to once again speak out publicly.

"This statement gained strong traction, emphasising the weight of feeling on this matter. Although we believe that the club should never have gone into partnership with BC Game, we nevertheless welcome this decision to part ways."

title: Sports: 12-player Lady Cranes squad heads to Dubai for HSBC
article_text:
Uganda's women's rugby team, the Lady Cranes, have left for Dubai to compete in the HSBC SVNS 3 tournament next week. They qualified after winning the African championship in Kenya earlier this month.

The team of 12 players and three officials was seen off at the National Council of Sports offices in Lugogo on Wednesday morning.

Uganda Rugby Union CEO Isaac Lutwama confirmed the team will get UAE visas despite travel restrictions on Uganda and other East African countries due to the Ebola outbreak. He said an agreement was reached between the government, URU, UAE authorities, Asia Rugby, and World Rugby to allow Uganda to take part. The tournament starts Friday, November 27.

"However, they have allowed us only 12 players and a management team of three — the head coach, strength and conditioning coach, and team manager," Lutwama noted.

"We are expecting the visas any time from now. We shall travel with all the necessary documentation," Lutwama said. "It is only fair that a team that has finally stepped up to win should be given the chance to compete."

In the six-nation tournament, Uganda will face China, Colombia, Poland, Samoa, and Mexico on the opening day. The competition is round-robin, with the top two teams advancing.

Head coach Charles Onen said the target is to finish in the top two and qualify for the three-leg HSBC SVNS 2 competition in Kenya, Brazil, and Uruguay, as they seek promotion.

He revealed the team will miss Katesa, who is sitting her final exams. Sarah Kirabo will replace her.

Onen added that the team will build on its experience from the recent continental championship in Nairobi and Uganda's appearance at the Dubai event in 2024.

Captain Peace Lekuru said the team is well prepared, citing the coaches' input and the players' previous Dubai experience.

NCS sports officer James Kasumba represented the General Secretary, Dr Bernard Ogwel, at the ceremony. "Winning the continental accolade indicates that you can go further. The government will support you financially and logistically," Kasumba said. He urged the players to remain united and compete as one team.

title: Equiti reveals official sports event partnership with Rolex SailGP 2026
article_text:
Equiti Group, a global fintech, has partnered with the 2026 Rolex SailGP Championship. The event partnership unites the two brands, Equiti and SailGP, around a shared belief that ambitious ideas, new technology and world-class experiences should reach more people.

Equiti will bring its brand to life across SailGP’s global platform, starting with the Emirates Dubai Sail Grand Prix, presented by DP World, on 21–22 November and at the season’s grande finale: the Mubadala Abu Dhabi Sail Grand Prix, presented by Abu Dhabi Sports Council, on 28–29 November.

Across both race weekends, Equiti will bring the partnership to life through bespoke brand and digital activations.

Equiti joins a strong SailGP partner line-up that includes Rolex, DP World, Emirates, Mubadala, Oracle, Apex Group, Accor, KPMG and Red Bull.

Founded by Larry Ellison and Sir Russell Coutts, and title-sponsored by Rolex, the championship combines elite athleticism, cutting-edge technology and real-time data to deliver fast, close racing. National teams race identical F50 hydrofoiling catamarans, at speeds sometimes exceeding 100kmph.

The SailGP 2025 Season reached a cumulative global broadcast audience of nearly 215 million viewers, averaging 18 million viewers per event, while SailGP content generated more than 1.65 billion social media views. More than 112,000 fans attended events across the season, underscoring the league’s growing appeal both in venues and on screen.

Chantelle Johnson, Chief Marketing Officer, Equiti Group, said, “SailGP is one of the fastest-growing sports in the world. Not just because it brings ambitious people together, but because it refuses to settle for what has been done before. Equiti is proud to join that shared platform. We both believe in challenging the status quo, raising the bar and creating experiences that bring more people into the action.”

SailGP is built around innovative technology and a refusal to accept limits, bringing world-class racing to a broad audience while its teams, owners and investors keep redefining what is possible on the water. Equiti shares that drive, using technology to open up access without diluting quality, and help people build better money habits.

Charlie Dewhurst, Chief Commercial Officer, SailGP, said, “We’re very pleased to partner with Equiti on two of our biggest races of the season in the UAE, in Dubai and our Grand Final in Abu Dhabi.

Dewhurst added, “We share their commitment to innovation and have a real alignment in our approach to data and precision across both our worlds of trading and sail racing. They are committed to elevating the fan experience across both events and we look forward to evolving this partnership in what is a very important region for SailGP.”

title: Fiji names seven debutants for opening SVNS rounds
article_text:
Seven new faces have been included in the Fiji Airways Fijian men’s and Fijiana 7s squads for the opening two legs of the HSBC SVNS Series in Dubai and Cape Town.

The squads feature a blend of experienced campaigners and emerging talent, with debutants marked by an asterisk in the official team announcement.

title: Formula 1 Signs with Nike Across F1 and F1 ACADEMY
article_text:
Formula 1 has entered a long-term global partnership with Nike, uniting motorsport’s premier championship with the world’s largest athletic footwear and apparel brand across both Formula 1 and F1 ACADEMY.

Ahead of the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix, the agreement establishes Nike as an Official Partner and the Official Apparel and Uniform Supplier of Formula 1 beginning in the 2027 season, while also naming Nike an Official Partner and Official Sporting Apparel Partner of F1 ACADEMY.

Formula 1 president and CEO, Stefano Domenicali, emphasised the cultural reach and global momentum driving the alliance across both series.

“Formula 1 and Nike are two of the world’s most iconic brands, united by a relentless drive to innovate, perform at the highest level, and inspire people to push beyond what is possible.”

“Formula 1 is experiencing unprecedented global growth, reaching hundreds of millions of fans and engaging one of the most passionate, diverse and dynamic communities in sport.

“Nike’s unique ability to sit at the intersection of sport, culture and inspiration makes them the ideal partner as we enter our next chapter,” Domenicali said.

Nike president and CEO, Elliott Hill, highlighted the shared performance ethos connecting motorsport with Nike’s global athlete mandate.

“Formula 1 is driven by competition, speed and a constant push to innovate.”

“That’s an athlete mindset, and it’s one we share at Nike.

“Together, we have an incredible opportunity to bring new energy to the sport, serve its athletes and inspire fans around the world,” Hill said.

From 2027, Nike will supply co-branded uniforms for Formula 1 staff at events worldwide while rolling out performance innovations, footwear, apparel, accessories, and race-weekend fan experiences across the global calendar. Ahead of the full commercial rollout, an early preview arrives on 20 November 2026 with a limited-edition Las Vegas Grand Prix x Nike capsule collection launching at the F1 Hub and Nike retail locations in Las Vegas.

title: USA Names 1st Roster of HSBC SVNS Season
article_text:
The USA Women’s Eagles have named their roster for the opening leg of the 2026-2027 HSBC SVSN season in Dubai. The tournament kicks off Saturday, Nov. 28, and the Americans will do work in Pool A against Spain, Australia and France. All action will be broadcast live on Paramount+. [lead photo: Alex Ho @hoiho_photo]

“We’ve framed the whole cycle as building our house,” head coach Emilie Bydwell looked at the four years between Olympics. “2025 was about forming and foundation building, identifying our new group, and building depth while Paris Olympians took extended breaks or recovered. Last year was about framing our house; getting stability in our squad profile and game model for LA.

“This year is about storm-proofing that performance and building the squad,” the coach continued. “If we have injuries to experienced players, or teams start to figure out how we’re playing, we want to be able to adapt by deploying different roles and combinations. Our goal is to be a really adaptable and anti-fragile team through these first four tournaments and build squad capabilities regardless of the mix of experienced to less experienced players.”

A warm-up tournament in New Zealand punctuated the Eagles’ eight-week pre-season. Since returning home the team has focused on refining systems, testing players and combinations, and elevating standards.

“We’ve come back into these two weeks of training hitting the ground running,” head coach Emilie Bydwell said. “We still have stuff that we need to clean up and can still be better. Our preseason was a long eight weeks before we were in New Zealand, and no matter how well it’s planned, it’s just not the same as playing.”

Kristi Kirshe resumes the role of team captain and oversees a Dubai squad that includes Olympian Ilona Maher.

“Beyond who she is as a player, she’s such a professional,” Bydwell said. “She takes what she does here very seriously, and she’s such a competitor. It’s been really great to have her back in — ready to compete, ready to drive the standards that we have as a team, and ready to empower the young athletes that she’s playing alongside.”

On the opposite end of the experience spectrum, Utahan teenager Fane Tausinga is traveling to the UAE in hopes of earning a first USA 7s cap.

The Dubai SVNS kicks off on Saturday, Nov. 28, and USA will compete in Pool A start against Spain (1 a.m. EST), followed by fellow New Zealand invitational attendees Australia (4:22 a.m.) and France (8:46 a.m.). Knockouts follow on Sunday, and all of the action will livestream on Paramount+.

title: MLB’s Local Media Rights Emerge As Focus in Labor Fight
article_text:
The future of MLB’s local media business has become a central element in the sport’s labor battle, providing yet another substantial layer to the already fractious situation.

For the last six months, MLB club owners have proposed to pool the local media revenue of all 30 clubs as part of a sought-after economic system that would implement a hard salary cap and floor. Most recently, management has updated its cap offer to the MLB Players Association to a 2028 implementation, and vows there will be “no compromise” on the pursuit of a cap as the Dec. 1 expiration of the current labor deal and an expected lockout thereafter approach.

The pooling of local media revenues, and a promise to end regional blackouts that have long frustrated fans, were also part of a video recently distributed by MLB to fans.

Throughout the entrenched negotiations, though, two key questions have persisted: Why are the local media and salary cap issues so deeply linked, and why couldn’t owners just agree on their own to pool that revenue, similar to how the NFL operates?

The beginning of the answer lies in the accelerating economic divide between the local media revenue of well-heeled teams such as the Dodgers, Yankees, and Mets, and half the league that has lost traditional regional sports network rights deal entirely and now has its local games produced and distributed by MLB—often at less lucrative terms than what they had before.

That split, exacerbated by existential disruption across the media business, has been the key driver in a $446 million spending difference this year between the Dodgers’ total luxury-tax payroll and projected taxes, and the comparable figure for the Guardians.

The total pool of local media income in MLB has also fallen, with the roughly $2.4 billion in annual revenues earlier this decade now standing at about $1.8 billion. With a cap-based system, MLB believes it can both narrow the economic spread and enlarge the overall pie of local media revenue.

“We are trying to make changes to the game that fans want and will improve the value of our media rights,” MLB EVP of baseball operations Morgan Sword said in a presentation this week to reporters.

One of the teams whose games are produced by the league, the Brewers, won this year’s World Series, something Sword called out of step with the industry’s prevailing trends.

“It is truly aberrational in baseball for small markets to be successful,” he said. “It’s not impossible, but it is much, much more difficult in our sports than it is in any of the other sports.”

The second part of the question is more complicated. Pooling local media revenue has a direct connection to MLB’s revenue-sharing system, which is collectively bargained between the league and MLBPA due to its link to player compensation. In the current labor deal, teams currently pay 48% of their local revenue into a central pool. So the league says it cannot simply restructure this part of its economics without involving the union.

While that is indeed true, the blackouts remain a separate issue from a salary cap. A complete pooling of local media revenue, and an end to regional blackouts, could be negotiated with the union absent a salary cap, though that likely would create disruption in the current rights deals—something the league is reluctant to face.

Instead, management is seeking to achieve the local media pooling with a hard cap that players have long resisted. The league is also proposing several other sweeping changes in conjunction with the cap-and-floor system, including significant restrictions on free agency, a retooled draft, and a 154-game regular season.

“We’re not saying it’s the players’ fault there are blackouts. We’re also not saying a salary cap in isolation fixes blackouts,” Sword said. “What we are saying is that this economic system, which is a big series of trade-offs, for the clubs, for the players, enables us to do it.”

MLB additionally is looking to mimic the NBA’s recent strategy and pursue a much more nationalized strategy when its current rights deals expire after the 2028 season. The NBA did that to great success, nearly tripling its national deals to about $6.9 billion annually.

Amid all of that, the MLBPA has consistently argued that caps reduce overall player compensation, pit player against player in a zero-sum game, and erode contract covenants.

“There can be no clearer example of the league’s lack of seriousness than their insistence that they will not negotiate over the economics outside of a radical change to the system that would dramatically reduce overall player compensation for all categories of players and strip fundamental rights from players like the ability to have truly guaranteed contracts,” MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer said in a statement. “There should be no illusions about the owners’ true motivation in pushing for this system. They want to make more money in profits and franchise values by artificially suppressing player salaries.”
