title: MLR Player of the Year among players selected for Canada's SVNS 3 squad
article_text:
Major League Rugby Player of the Year Brock Webster has been included in the Canada Men’s Sevens squad selected for the HSBC SVNS 3 opener in Dubai.

The full-back starred for the Chicago Hounds as they claimed the MLR title in an unbeaten season. He is a two-time MLR champion and was the first Canadian to be named the competition’s best player. The 26-year-old was Canada’s top points-scorer at the 2022 Rugby Sevens World Cup in Cape Town, South Africa.

Webster is one of several players with Test rugby experience that has been selected by Canada Men’s Sevens head coach Craig Dods for the tournament that takes place next week.

Kyle Tremblay, Sion Parry, Isaac Olsen, Jesse Kilgour, Takoda McMullin and Demetri Patterson have been part of Stephen Meehan’s World Rugby Nations Cup squad this autumn, while Noah Flesch, Lockie Kratz and Cody Nhanala have all spent time in the Test setup this year.

Craig Dods, Canada’s Men’s Sevens head coach, said: “Kicking off the 2026-27 season in Dubai marks a new chapter in this program, which has been reflective in the energy and excitement in training camp the past few weeks.

“Right now, we’re focused on building our identity with some new pieces in place and taking the first step toward earning our way back up the HSBC SVNS Series. Dubai will be our first collective test as a new unit, and I look forward to the upcoming challenge.”

Canada will play Zimbabwe, Chile, Italy, Hong Kong China and Samoa in the two day round robin competition.

Both the winners and runners-up next week in Dubai will gain promotion to HSBC SVNS 2. The second tier competition starts in Nairobi in January before legs in Montevideo and Sao Paulo in February.

Finishing in the top four of that competition will secure a place at the HSBC SVNS World Championship and an opportunity to gain HSBC SVNS Series status.

title: Glos-Hartpury aim to name new head coach in January
article_text:
Gloucester-Hartpury will not have a new head coach until next year, says the club's commercial sales director James Forrester.

Head of rugby Dan Murphy's departure from the Premiership Women's Rugby club was confirmed on Thursday, less than 48 hours before the start of the new season.

Forrester said the team will be led by the remainder of the existing coaching team for the first block of the campaign.

"We will be advertising in the next week or so and looking to get someone in place late January," he told BBC Radio Gloucestershire.

Murphy was in charge of the three-time PWR champions for just one season, having taken over the reigns from Sean Lynn, who departed for the Wales head coach role.

Under Lynn's tenure, the team won three consecutive titles.

Last season, they won their first 14 matches of the campaign, but a dip in form at a crucial time during spring culminated in losing the play-off semi-final to Trailfinders to miss out on a spot in the PWR final for the first time in four years.

At the same time as Murphy's departure was announced, it was confirmed former Gloucester captain Luke Narraway was joining the Gloucester-Hartpury coaching team as a consultant coach on a short-term basis, while Richie Williams also was appointed earlier this summer as an assistant coach.

"Club favourite Lewis Ludlow [Gloucester number eight] is supporting with some of the line-out work and he's been, as you can imagine, a massive hit with the players," Forrester added.

"Lewis Arnold's also helping the line-outs and then former captain Luke Narraway has come into the team and he'll be supporting the team with defence largely.

"We think we've got a really good team together."

Gloucester-Hartpury begin the new season away at Sale Sharks on Saturday, with their first home game of the season on Saturday, 28 November at Kingsholm against Loughborough Lightning.

"We want to being continue to be one of the best programme female programmes in the world and we felt this the right decision at this time to continue to do that."

title: 'No-one is going to break us'
article_text:
Already circled as one of the must-see fixtures in a packed November schedule, interest in the meeting between Ireland and South Africa has intensified following their contrasting disciplinary fortunes in recent days.

Not for the first time, Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus landed himself in hot water with the powers-that-be for criticising match officials.

After receiving a six-match ban for questioning the integrity of referee Andrea Piardi and television match official Matteo Liperini in South Africa's defeat by France last week, Erasmus has been defended and condemned.

Any doubt about where his players stand, however, was cleared up by captain Siya Kolisi, who bristled at a suggestion Erasmus was being "dramatic".

"It might sound dramatic to you, but to us it means so much more," Kolisi said during his pre-match news conference.

"Rugby has done a lot for our country, and it's done a lot for many of us who come from South Africa.

"We know how happy people are and what the mood is like when we win, and when we lose, it gets tough. People care a lot about it.

"When we play, we think about the people back home. We don't take representing the country lightly because we represent every single person in South Africa when we put on that jersey."

While Erasmus has dominated headlines this week, he will not be in attendance at Aviva Stadium on Saturday.

Instead, in a bizarre twist, the two-time World Cup winner will host a watchalong of the game from the team's Dublin hotel, with the conditions of his suspension prohibiting him from matchday contact with players and management.

"He's been hands-on with our team [in the build-up], and we're in a good space," assistant coach Mzwandile Stick said of Erasmus.

"Irrespective of what has happened, we love him, we appreciate him, and no-one is going to break us. I can tell you that for sure."

Whether or not Jasper Wiese joins Erasmus' stream remains to be seen. The back row was hit with a four-match ban for a dangerous ruck clearout against France.

While Wiese's fate did not attract the same level of scrutiny, South Africa's sense of injustice will perhaps be fuelled by the sight of Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast on Saturday.

As predicted by Erasmus, Prendergast was cleared to face the world champions after being cited for an alleged hip-drop tackle on Fiji back row Peceli Yato.

"I will tell you now for free, if that was a Fijian player tackling an Irish player with that hip-drop, that player would be in Fiji now," said Stick.

"If that was a Fijian player, he would be sitting in Fiji now doing some extra lessons of how to tackle."

Focused on erasing the pain of last year's 24-13 loss to the Springboks in Dublin, Ireland have sidestepped questions about Erasmus this week, with head coach Andy Farrell opting not to comment on his opposite number's suspension.

Irish captain Dan Sheehan said the commotion has not "affected the squad at all".

"Obviously it's a big media story for fans to get behind, but in terms of us playing the match it has zero impact," he said.

While there may be added scrutiny on referee Christophe Ridley, Sheehan said he plans to leave the official alone unless compelled to bring something "major" to his attention.

The Irish skipper has enough on his plate anyway. In addition to leading his side against the back-to-back world champions, Sheehan has been thrust into the number eight role.

The 28-year-old has won all 42 of his previous caps at hooker but moves to the back row with Caelan Doris, Jack Conan, Sean Jansen and James McNabney all ruled out.

Ireland hope Sheehan's inclusion in the back row will facilitate his powerful ball-carrying capabilities, but he insists he is not going to "overthink" it.

"I just get on with stuff. Like, eight on my back, just pick the ball up and go," said Sheehan, whose only previous start in the position was in Leinster's win over Munster last month.

"It can't be that complicated. That's my approach to it, to be honest."

Had it not been for the furore surrounding Erasmus, chances are the pre-match talk would have been dominated by scrums.

Last year, Ireland were shown five cards and conceded six penalties and a penalty try during a chastening night against the Springbok scrum.

That set-piece shellacking may have given the Irish pack nightmares over the past 12 months, and while South Africa won nine scrum penalties against France, Kolisi expects a closer contest in Dublin this time.

"Their scrum is much better than it was a year ago," he said.

"You can see they're getting penalties. But our focus is not on what they're going to do. It's about making sure we stick to our plans and do what we need to do in the scrum."

The Springboks have been boosted by the return of record cap holder Eben Etzebeth, but his second-row partner Ruan Nortje was ruled out through injury on Friday. He has been replaced by Franco Mostert, who was not originally in the matchday squad.

Ireland - who have lost their past six contests against New Zealand, France and South Africa, the three teams above them in the world rankings, by double-digit margins - have also been forced into a late change, with Thomas Clarkson replacing Sam Illo as the replacement tight-head prop.

title: Springboks demand World Rugby action as Ireland accusation made on eve of game
article_text:
Mzwandile Stick, South Africa's assistant coach, has demanded clarity from World Rugby over the new hip-drop tackle law, claiming Ireland's Sam Prendergast would have been banned for the tackle he was cited for last weekend were he a Fijian.

The Irish fly-half was summoned over an alleged hip-drop tackle on Fiji captain Peceli Yato last weekend but escaped punishment, being cleared of the charge after he contested it earlier this week.

He is now free to face the Springboks this weekend, something which South Africa have taken umbrage with.

Their head coach, Rassie Erasmus, is already serving a six-match ban for comments he made in the aftermath of South Africa's defeat to France last weekend, where he questioned whether referees were involved in "match-fixing" and accused officials of missing 17 on-field infringements in Paris, among other things.

Now Stick has issued a defiant statement to World Rugby, saying the squad is united and that Erasmus' suspension won't split the camp.

“Rassie might not be in that coaching box, but he’s with us,” he said. “His energy will be there. And whatever we’re going to be doing tomorrow, we’ll do it for him. No one is going to break us.”

Moving on to Prendergast, Stick suggested the No.10 should have been banned and would have been, had he been a Fiji player.

“You know what they call a traditional drink in Fiji?" he said.

"Is it kava? If that was a Fijian player, he would be sitting in Fiji now doing some extra lessons of how to tackle. But it’s an Irish player, it’s free to play."

He added they as coaches needed clarity from law makers in order to instruct their players, who he claims are in the dark right now.

“When there are laws and new rules, people need to explain,” he said. “The players look up to us as coaches. They also don’t know what’s right or wrong.”

He added: “We want to play the game clean and make sure players know how to tackle. But other parties aren’t coming to the party, and then we’re getting punished.”

Stick implied that suspensions were becoming "a trend" when visiting the Emerald Isle, with Jasper Wiese hit with a ban following his red card against Les Bleus and therefore unavailable for the match tomorrow.

“Last year in this boardroom, we were talking about [players] who were also suspended. It’s becoming a trend now when you come to Ireland,” he said.

“It’s always crazy now. If I think about last year in this boardroom, we were talking about who was also suspended.

“So it’s becoming a trend now when you come to Ireland, players will be suspended. So I think by the time we come here, we must always be prepared for that.

“But once again, don’t worry, it’s part of the game. I know I’m excited to see a guy like (Cameron) Hanekom also getting an opportunity (in place of Wiese).”

title: Lizzie Gibson among new faces in Canada squad for SVNS Series opener
article_text:
Lizzie Gibson has been named in the Canada Women’s Sevens squad a day after she signed for JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby side Trailfinders Women.

The back-row forward made her Test debut earlier this year against the Black Ferns in the Pacific Four Series and started all five of Canada’s WXV Global Series 2026 fixtures, including the back-to-back wins against the Red Roses.

With a number of other Canada Women’s Sevens players unavailable due to PWR and Élite 1 commitments for the opening tournaments of the HSBC SVNS Series in Dubai and Cape Town, Aurora Bowie is also in line for her sevens debut.

This season will be hugely influential on qualification for the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles. A top four finish after three HSBC SVNS World Championship events will give teams an automatic slot at the Games.

Jocelyn Barrieau, Head Coach of Canada’s Women’s Sevens, said: “The road to LA 2028 is well under way, and our focus is on the opening leg of the 2027 Series in Dubai and Cape Town.

“This roster reflects both experienced sevens players that led us to success in the 2025/26 season and some new faces which will continue to build depth across this program in this Olympic qualification season.”

Along with Gibson and Bowie, Ava van Saten and Olivia Newsome are both in line for their debuts. Van Saten was named MVP at the 2026 FISU World University Championships earlier this year as Canada claimed gold with victory over France in the final.

There are also returns to Barrieau’s squad for Breanne Nicholas, Adia Pye and Larah Wright, who helped Canada claim bronze at the final leg of the HSBC SVNS World Championship in Bordeaux.

The North Americans have been placed in Pool B alongside Fiji, the Black Ferns Sevens and Japan for the season opener in Dubai.

title: 2026/27 JAECOO PWR: Every team's squad confirmed for Round 1
article_text:
Tonight the 2026/27 JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby season will get underway when Loughborough Lightning host Trailfinders Women in Northampton.

This season promises to be the most competitive and exhilarating yet. There have also never been so many verifiable stars of women’s Test rugby present in the English top flight.

Every weekend is essential viewing on the way to a June finale at the Twickenham Stoop.

To take on last season’s runners-up Trailfinders Women, Loughborough Lightning boss Nathan Smith has included all five of his team’s Canadian recruits in his matchday 23.

Flo Symonds and Rachel Smith both start in the Friday night clash, while Kiki Idowu, Brooke Rempel and Pamphinette Buisa are all named among the replacements. Daisy Hibbert-Jones captains the team from the back-row, alongside Sadia Kabeya and Haineala Lutui.

England internationals Lilli Ives Campion and Helena Rowland also get starts, while Ellie Tromans gets her first minute in the league since October 2024 on the wing. USA Women’s Eagles pair Alev Kelter and Mae Sagapolu are also starters.

Barney Maddison’s Trailfinders have gone strong for their first game of the season. This includes starts for summer arrivals Helen Nelson, Laetitia Royer, Ruby Tui and Bo Westcombe-Evans.

Scotland playmaker Nelson starts at inside centre – as Canada’s Claire Gallagher is preferred at fly-half – and partners England captain Meg Jones. Rachel Malcolm captains the team from flanker, where she combines with Abi Burton and Annabel Meta.

Jade Betsen, daughter of former France Men international Serge, is named among the replacements after she impressed in the club’s JAECOO PWR Next Gen Cup success.

Tatyana Heard and Kelsey Jones will want to make an impression for new club side Sale Sharks this weekend when they face former employers, Gloucester Hartpury, on Saturday. Heard starts at inside centre and Jones is named as a replacement, with Amy Cokayne captaining the side as starting hooker.

It is a Sale team dripping with international quality. Holly Aitchison starts at fly-half, Scotland’s Rhona Lloyd and Shona Campbell are on the wings, Beatrice Rigoni starts at centre, Red Roses lock Morwenna Talling is at lock and Brittany Hogan starts at No.8.

USA co-captain Erica Jarrell-Searcy is on the bench, alongside Wales’ Gwen Pyrs and Courtney Keight. Sophie Hopkins will make her first league appearance for the club in over a year after she spent last season in Élite 1 in France.

Less than 24 hours after the club confirmed that Dan Murphy left his post as head coach, Gloucester Hartpury named their first matchday squad of the 2026/27 season.

Gloucester Hartpury’s coaching staff have included three debutants in the matchday squad for their season opener against Sharks. Italy hooker Vittoria Vecchini and Eagles lock Emerson Allen are included in the starting XV, while Bridie O’Gorman is among the replacements.

Hot on the heels of their involvement with England’s WXV Global Series campaign, Emma Sing, Mia Venner, Natasha ‘Mo’ Hunt, Maud Muir and Alex Matthews are included from the start. Wales’ Hannah Dallavalle, Nel Metcalfe, Lleucu George and Kate Williams are also starters. Jorja Aiono and Sian Jones are on the bench.

Sydney Gregson will make her 100th Saracens appearance when the PWR champions host Leicester Tigers on Sunday afternoon. The 30-year-old partners Emma Hardy in the midfield.

Canada scrum-half Olivia Apps combines with fly-half Amelia MacDougall, while Lotte Sharp, Alysha Corrigan and Sophie Bridger form the back three. May Campbell captains the team at hooker, as Liz Crake and Kelsey Clifford complete the front three.

Sophie de Goede is named at lock and her Canada teammate Julia Omokhuale is named in the back-row. A day after her signing was announced, USA back-row Freda Tafuna is included among the replacements. England internationals Bryony Field, Zoe Harrison and Jess Breach are also on the bench.

Leicester Tigers have included a host of new signings in the squad for their season opener. Wallaroos trio Caitlyn Halse, Ashley Fernandez and Tabua Tuinakauvadra will make their debuts, while former Australia international Jemima McCalman is named captain.

After she missed out on a Wallaroos debut in WXV Global Series with injury, Grace Freeman is named at fly-half and will partner Eneka Labeyrie. Former England international Lagi Tuima gets the nod at inside centre.

USA lock Rachel Ehrecke and Wales’ Abbie Fleming start in the back. Ex-France prop Coco Lindelauf starts in the front-row, where she will combine with Springbok Women hooker Micke Günter and tighthead prop Nadine Vincent.

Ellie Kildunne will make an instant return to the Twickenham Stoop with new side Bristol Bears this Sunday afternoon. She is one of 18 internationals included in Scott Lawson’s squad that will travel to West London.

There are also inclusions for Women’s Rugby World Cup winners Lark Atkin-Davies and Abbie Ward, who both recently made returns to the pitch after giving birth. Atkin-Davies co-captains the team alongside tighthead prop Sarah Bern. England’s Hannah Botterman completes the front-row.

Scotland’s Evie Gallagher, Hollie Cunningham and Meryl Smith all have starting roles this weekend. Lana Skeldon is named on the bench, as are Wales internationals Bethan Lewis and Keira Bevan.

Marlie Packer captains Harlequins in her first league appearance for the club. The 37-year-old England international leads the team in the absence of the injured Aoife Wafer. Packer starts in the back-row with Alex Callender and Grace Keel.

South Africa’s Danelle Lochner and Scotland’s Sarah Bonar are the lock partnership. In the front-row Sisilia Tuipulotu makes her first appearance for the West London club, where she combines with Abby Middlebrooke and Maja Meuller.

title: Ireland prop stood down with immediate effect ahead of Springboks match
article_text:
Ireland have been dealt a late injury blow ahead of tomorrow’s Nations Championship showdown against South Africa, with Sam Illo ruled out of the clash.

The Connacht prop had initially been named in Andy Farrell’s matchday 23, taking the number 18 shirt, but has now been withdrawn after failing to complete the return-to-play protocols.

Illo suffered a concussion during the second half of last weekend’s victory over Fiji at the Aviva Stadium and has not recovered in time to face the world champions.

Leinster prop Thomas Clarkson has been drafted into the squad as his replacement, while Connacht’s Finlay Bealham has also joined the Ireland camp as emergency cover.

Clarkson is in line to make his first appearance of the month and could find himself facing either Gerhard Steenekamp or Ox Nche in the South African front row, depending on the Springboks' substitutions.

Illo’s absence is a setback for Ireland, particularly given the strength of the Springboks scrum. The late change also means Farrell will have to adjust his front-row options just a day before kick-off.

However, Clarkson is no stranger to the international set-up. The Leinster tighthead was selected as injury cover for the 2025 British and Irish Lions tour of Australia and is listed at 3kg heavier than Illo.

Saturday’s encounter is effectively a must-win for both sides as they look to finish top of their respective hemisphere tables and secure the best possible position heading into next weekend’s finals at Allianz Stadium.

Both Ireland and South Africa currently sit one point behind the leaders in their respective tables.

The Springboks will know exactly what is required when they take to the pitch, with New Zealand facing England earlier in the day.

Ireland, meanwhile, will have to wait until France’s later meeting with Argentina to discover the full picture in their race for top spot.

title: Five things Rassie Erasmus is banned from doing against Ireland
article_text:
Springboks boss Rassie Erasmus will be forced to watch Saturday's blockbuster clash against Ireland from afar as he begins his six-match suspension.

The South Africa head coach was hit with the lengthy ban following his controversial comments about the officiating during last Friday's defeat to France.

Ireland legend Brian O’Driscoll has admitted Erasmus has a point, while Eddie Jones has also delivered his verdict on the suspension. SA Rugby has requested a full misconduct hearing following the suspension.

However, Erasmus has found a unique way to remain involved by announcing his own live watchalong.

Here, RUCK looks at five things the Springboks boss is banned from doing.

Erasmus cannot even enter the Aviva Stadium as a spectator.

That rules out watching from the stands, a hospitality box or his usual position alongside the coaching team.

Instead, the 54-year-old will watch the fixture from his hotel.

The Springboks boss is prohibited from coaching on matchday.

That means no motivational pre-match speeches, half-time team talks or tactical instructions in the changing room.

Captain Siya Kolisi, who has publicly backed Erasmus following his ban, will have an even greater leadership role.

Perhaps the most significant restriction is the ban on communicating with players and team management on matchday.

Erasmus cannot recommend substitutions, send tactical instructions or use a third party to pass on messages.

Ironically, Christophe Ridley, who was involved in last weekend's controversial defeat to France, will referee Saturday's showdown.

Erasmus cannot contact the match officials on matchday or take part in the formal referee feedback process.

The two-time Rugby World Cup-winning coach is also barred from carrying out media duties during his suspension.

That means no official pre-match interviews or post-match press conferences.

Could Rassie Erasmus land himself in more trouble?

According to Sky Sports, Erasmus could risk breaching his suspension if members of the Springboks coaching staff tune into his planned live stream and receive tactical guidance.

The South African has stressed that the watchalong is a personal event rather than an official Springboks broadcast.

- Honorary doctorate: Awarded by North-West University in 2024.

- National honour: Received South Africa’s Order of Ikhamanga in Gold in 2026.

title: McDowall goes from farm hand to Scotland captain as Darge injured
article_text:
Stafford McDowall was working on his dad's farm when he got the call to play for Scotland against Australia on Sunday - and six days later will be captain against Japan after Rory Darge suffered a late injury blow.

It is the second change of captain head coach Gregor Townsend has had to make in a week after Sione Tuipulotu was ruled out of the Nations Championship matches against Australia and Japan.

Darge produced a man-of-the-match performance against the Wallabies in his place and the Glasgow Warriors forward was initially named again in the starting line-up despite a shoulder injury.

But, following further assessment and discussion within the Scotland camp, it has been decided he will sit out the game against Japan at Murrayfield.

Club-mate Matt Fagerson will start instead at number eight, with his place on the bench filled by Edinburgh flanker Freddy Douglas and Newcastle Red Bulls' Ollie Leatherbarrow moving forward in the back row.

Glasgow centre McDowall takes over as captain and revealed that he had returned to help out on his father's farm in Dumfries not expecting to come off the bench against the Wallabies as a second-half substitute.

"Originally I was not involved at the weekend, not travelling reserve, so I took the opportunity to go home and help dad out," he said.

"I got there for about 12 hours, got some work done on the Saturday morning, then got the call at about 11 o'clock in the morning. Quick shower, then up the road.

"Dad wasn't too happy. I phoned him at four o'clock and asked what he was doing and he said he was doing all the jobs he had lined up for me.

"But it was awesome. Dad came up for the game the next day, so he said it worked out better than me doing jobs on the farm anyway.

"It was class. It was a bit of a whirlwind weekend."

Townsend had already made 10 changes for Japan's visit with several top players, including fly-half Finn Russell, rested before deciding not to risk Darge.

Darge will remain in the squad with the aim of being involved next week, when the Nations Championship comes to a conclusion.

Scotland are fourth in the Northern Hemisphere group and could yet be involved in a play-off for third, fifth, seventh or ninth places depending on this weekend's results.

Starting XV: Ollie Smith; Darcy Graham, Stafford McDowall (capt), Rory Hutchinson, Kyle Rowe; Tom Jordan, Jamie Dobie; Nathan McBeth, Gregor Hiddleston, Zander Fagerson, Jonny Gray, Max Williamson, Liam McConnell, Ollie Leatherbarrow, Matt Fagerson.

Replacements: Seb Stephen, Rory Sutherland, Will Hurd, Gregor Brown, Magnus Bradbury, Freddy Douglas, George Horne, Blair Kinghorn.

title: USA confirm Ilona Maher's return for start of new SVNS campaign
article_text:
Ilona Maher will make her return to HSBC SVNS Series action in Dubai and Cape Town at the start of the 2026/27 season.

The 30-year-old did not play for the USA Women’s Eagles Sevens last season after her involvement at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025. She is the third-most experienced player named in Emilie Bydwell’s squad for the first tournaments of the new campaign.

Emilie Bydwell, USA Women’s Eagles Sevens head coach, said: “Beyond who she is as a player, she’s such a professional. She takes what she does here very seriously, and she’s such a competitor.

“It’s been really great to have her back in – ready to compete, ready to drive the standards that we have as a team, and ready to empower the young athletes that she’s playing alongside.”

Maher’s return adds to an otherwise settled squad, with travelling reserve Fane Tausinga the only player named without any tournament caps.

Last season, the Eagles finished fourth after three HSBC SVNS World Championship tournaments. While other teams are looking to book their place at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles, as host nation the Eagles can focus on development hot on the heels of a positive campaign.

Bydwell said: “We want a storm-proof performance this year. We want to be really consistent, regardless of what lineup we put on the field, who we’re playing, or what game we’re playing in.

“We’ve come back into these two weeks of training hitting the ground running. We still have stuff that we need to clean up and can still be better. Our preseason was a long eight weeks before we were in New Zealand, and no matter how well it’s planned, it’s just not the same as playing.”

For Dubai, the USA have been named in Pool A alongside Spain, France and Australia.

title: Ireland vs South Africa referee involved in Rassie Erasmus controversy
article_text:
One of the match officials involved in the Springboks' controversial defeat to France will take charge of Saturday's blockbuster clash between Ireland and South Africa.

England's Christophe Ridley was an assistant referee during South Africa's 21-19 defeat in Paris last Friday.

The performance of the officials sparked an explosive response from Rassie Erasmus, who questioned whether match-fixing could have occurred.

The Springboks boss highlighted several alleged knee-drop tackles that went unpunished before being handed a six-match ban by World Rugby.

Ridley will now swap the touchline for the whistle when South Africa face Ireland at the Aviva Stadium.

Erasmus did not single out Ridley personally, with World Rugby's disciplinary statement specifically highlighting comments concerning the TMO.

Ridley has previously refereed four Springboks Tests, with South Africa winning three and losing one.

That solitary defeat came against Argentina in September 2024, when the Springboks lost 29-28.

The spotlight on the officials will be particularly intense this weekend, with Erasmus set to watch the match from his hotel.

Christophe Ridley is an English rugby union referee who has established himself as one of the leading officials in the international game.

- Background: A former Leicester Tigers academy player who turned to officiating at a young age.

Ridley has risen rapidly through the refereeing ranks, earning appointments at the highest level of both club and international rugby.

Nations Championship predictor: Who will reach the Grand Final?

Five nations remain in contention to reach the inaugural Nations Championship Grand Final at Twickenham.

Remarkably, the Springboks could lose to Ireland and still qualify, while England could beat the All Blacks and miss out.

Predict all six fixtures below and discover how the finals weekend will shape up.

title: PWR title, England recall, Lions tour - ambitious Atkin-Davies returns
article_text:
Winning a World Cup on home soil is up there among the pinnacle of things an athlete can achieve in their career.

Lark Atkin-Davies was part of the England Red Roses team that did just that in September 2025, clinching the World Cup at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham.

That match was also the hooker's final game until last month, when she returned to the pitch with Bristol following the birth of her daughter.

After achieving a goal so monumental, it would be understandable if it took some athletes a little while to find new motivation and targets going forward in their sporting career.

But for Atkin-Davies, who describes herself as a "naturally very driven and motivated person", it did not prove tricky after a year away from the sport to come back and aim for even more.

"I'd love to win a PWR (Premiership Women's Rugby) title with Bears. I've said it since being here that I think we've got everything we need to be able to do that," she told BBC Sport.

"And I truly believe that we can go and do that this season.

"Then personally, I'd love to put my hand up for selection for the Six Nations. To get back into an England shirt is a real goal of mine. And then obviously next year looking at the [British and Irish] Lions as well, I'd love to put myself in contention for that."

Atkin-Davies is one of the most experienced front-row players in England.

The 31-year-old has 74 caps and has been a mainstay of the Red Roses since making her debut in 2015.

She has also played across the PWR, starting her career at Worcester before joining Loughborough and then Bristol in 2022.

But Atkin-Davies says that before she dreamt of being a professional rugby player, she wanted to be a mother and since welcoming her daughter Olive this summer her perspective on her career has changed.

"Going through pregnancy and then having a daughter especially, has just brought this new motivation and new drive," she said.

Atkin-Davies is one of four Red Roses players who were away from the sport last season through pregnancy, with Abbie Ward, Zoe Stratford and Rosie Gallagher also welcoming children in recent months.

She has previously cited her Bristol team-mate Ward as being a huge part in showing her that rugby and motherhood can co-exist.

Lock Ward became the first centrally contracted England player to return to the sport and use the Rugby Football Union's maternity policy following the birth of her first child in 2024.

"I always speak about how much of an inspiration Abbie is and was with having Hallie (her first daughter) and then going on to win a World Cup," Atkin-Davies said.

"Seeing her with Hallie at that final whistle, carrying the World Cup around, I'd love to potentially have a moment like that.

"If Olive can grow up seeing me in an environment where I'm being challenged but where I'm doing something I love, that's a really big motivator."

Such is the regard Atkin-Davies is held in at Bristol, she has been named co-captain along with England team-mate Sarah Bern, for the new season.

After a disappointing campaign in 2025-26 when the Bears finished eighth in the table, they start away at Harlequins on Sunday, 22 November boosted further by the signing of England star Ellie Kildunne.

The Bears were beaten PWR finalists in 2024 and reached the semi-finals in 2025 but have never won the title.

Atkin-Davies believes with the squad they have, that could change this season.

"I've always truly believed that we could win the PWR title," she added.

"I said that at the beginning of the season last year - but we've got so many incredible individuals and, as a group, I just think we've always had that potential."

As for her own performances, Atkin-Davies believes the best is still to come and motherhood is to thank for that.

"Post-World Cup, as soon as I found out I was pregnant, it was like, 'OK, first and foremost, I want to make sure that I'm doing everything I can to have a really healthy pregnancy and to have Olive'," she said.

"Then also 'what can I be doing whilst I'm out of the game that can continue to keep pushing me forward?'"

She continued: "I said early on coming back to training at Bears that there's almost this new level that's been unlocked for me.

"I find that a really exciting place to be in because I think I'll be a better player for it.

"We're just at the start of the journey in terms of that return and being better than I was before."

title: World Rugby make Malcolm Marx ban decision after footage emerges
article_text:
Under World Rugby Law 9.12, striking an opponent is an act of foul play.

In my opinion, there was more than enough evidence to warrant a disciplinary hearing.

Instead, rugby’s disciplinary system looks like a courtroom that has locked its doors before the evidence has arrived.

World Rugby regularly talks about its commitment to player safety. Allowing potential foul play to go unexamined because of an administrative deadline hardly reinforces that message.

Remarkably, Jasper Wiese and Rassie Erasmus have both been banned following events surrounding the defeat in Paris, yet Marx remains available.

title: Wales v Australia moved off ITV1 as Nations Championship TV schedule changes
article_text:
Wales' Nations Championship clash with Australia will not be shown on ITV1 this weekend, with a packed international rugby schedule and a busy Saturday night television line-up seeing the match broadcast on ITV4 instead.

Steve Tandy's side host the Wallabies at the Principality Stadium on Saturday, November 21, with kick-off scheduled for the unusually late time of 8.10pm.

However, supporters thinking the match will be on ITV1 will need to switch channels, with the broadcaster instead showing The 1% Club and I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here!

It is a different arrangement for the final round of Nations Championship fixtures, with all six matches taking place on Saturday and three pairs of games kicking off simultaneously.

England's clash with New Zealand, fresh from their defeat in Cardiff last weekend, at Twickenham will be shown on ITV1 at 2.10pm, while Scotland's meeting with Japan takes place at the same time on ITV4.

Ireland then face world champions South Africa at 4.40pm on ITV1, with Italy hosting Fiji simultaneously on ITV4.

The evening sees Wales take on Australia at 8.10pm, at exactly the same time as France host Argentina in Paris. The latter fixture has been allocated ITV2, leaving Wales' encounter with the Wallabies on ITV4.

ITV1's evening schedule includes Celebrity Catchphrase at 7.15pm, The 1% Club at 8.10pm and I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! at 9.15pm.

The scheduling means ITV1 will broadcast two Nations Championship matches during the afternoon before switching away from live rugby for its primetime entertainment programmes.

Despite the change, Wales supporters will still be able to watch the match free-to-air, with ITV4 and ITVX providing English-language coverage.

Welsh-language coverage will also be available on S4C, with streaming available on S4C Clic and BBC iPlayer.

The weekend marks the final round of the inaugural Nations Championship before the competition's finals weekend at Twickenham from November 27 to 29.

- 2.10pm: England v New Zealand – ITV1, ITVX

- 4.40pm: Ireland v South Africa – ITV1, ITVX

- 8.10pm: France v Argentina – ITV2, ITVX

- 8.10pm: Wales v Australia – ITV4, ITVX, S4C, BBC iPlayer

title: Wallabies make 5 changes to avoid 5th straight loss
Unbeaten World Rugby Nations Cup winners name teams for final bout
article_text:
The winners of Pools A and B in the World Rugby Nations Cup will meet in Tbilisi this weekend for bragging rights as the tournament’s best.

The USA enjoyed a blowout win over Romania in round 5 to secure their Pool A crown after four tight wins to begin the inaugural competition, while Georgia’s supremacy in Pool B has never been challenged, and they’ve emerged with a competition-best points differential of +124 through five rounds of action.

There is no further silverware on offer for the teams, but there’s an air of serendipity in the matchup coming in the final round of the competition.

USA head coach Scott Lawrence has made just one change to the starting XV that put 53 points on Romania last weekend, with Mitch Wilson replacing Perry Mayo at fullback. And Georgia’s Pierre-Henry Broncan has also opted for as much continuity as possible, only promoting loosehead prop Sergo Abramishvili and halfback Gela Aprasidzeto to the starting team.

title: Scotland injury update as Dempsey undergoes surgery but good news on Tuipulotu
article_text:
Jack Dempsey has undergone surgery on the foot injury he suffered against Australia, but there is better news concerning the fitness of captain Sione Tuipulotu.

The pair were ruled out of Scotland's final two Nations Championship fixtures this week after suffering foot and knee injuries, respectively.

Tuipulotu was a late withdrawal from the side to face Australia last weekend after aggravating the problem the day before the game.

On Tuesday, assistant coach Pieter de Villiers suggested Dempsey may need surgery on his foot problem.

And after naming his side to face Japan, Gregor Townsend confirmed the 32-year-old had gone under the knife.

"Jack got operated today so obviously he will be working with his club on that," said the Scotland coach.

"It's great that he's been able to have the surgery in Scotland and also very good that he's been operated so quickly and that he can make a quicker recovery."

Dempsey's injury is a significant setback to Dempsey, who will now miss a significant portion of the Top League season Toshiba Brave Lupus Tokyo.

But the prognosis for Tuipulotu is more encouraging, Townsend revealed, while also stating none of the other players who are injured are expected to miss the Six Nations.

"He flew down to see a specialist on Monday in London, so [he will be out for] three or four weeks.

"We're thinking Ben White's about the same time scale. Scott Cummings might be slightly longer and Fergus Burke is similar. Alex Craig had a hip issue and he didn't train fully leading up to New Zealand."

title: 'Clearer' approach has lifted England mood
article_text:
Captain Maro Itoje says a clearer sense of purpose and unity has coincided with improved performances from England this autumn.

They have won their last four games, racking up victories over Fiji, Argentina, Australia and Japan in the Nations Championship.

Prior to that run, England had lost five successive Tests - a streak that included their worst ever Six Nations campaign.

They host New Zealand on Saturday, with the All Blacks stung by their first defeat by Wales in 73 years last time out.

"It feels a lot more cohesive," Itoje told BBC Rugby Union Weekly.

"It feels, from a player's point of view, that our understanding of what we're trying to do is a lot clearer.

"The level of understanding has grown from campaign to campaign and we have a very clear sense of what we're doing, what we're trying to do and we're getting into those positions a lot more effectively now."

A Times report earlier this month, external claimed senior players had sought a summit meeting with head coach Steve Borthwick after their July Nations Championship campaign due to differences of opinion over the team's direction.

Itoje was rested for that tour and Jamie George, who had reassumed the captaincy in his absence, said parts of the article were untrue and the squad were "incredibly disappointed" by its publication.

"As senior players part of our job is to challenge Steve," said George at the time. "Steve is so open to us giving feedback and having challenge."

In turn, Borthwick has credited his senior players with leading a drive on discipline that has helped England's results turn a corner.

Across their first eight Tests in 2026, England were shown 14 yellow cards and a red.

It was highlighted as a key area to improve before the autumn and they have responded with no cards and only 15 penalties conceded across their two November Tests so far.

"It's never just one thing, but I will talk about one matter," added Borthwick of the reasons behind the improvement.

"A number of weeks ago, the senior players led the players in groups. It was a big discussion topic and coming out it was a series of commitments that the players made about what they need to do.

"They've backed up those commitments in this first couple weeks. Now we know that's going be tested even more this weekend."

Itoje admitted the arrival of New Zealand brought a different atmosphere to training.

"There are weeks...and then there are weeks," he said.

"The step-up often first starts with the mind, then goes down to behaviours and actions.

"There's a sharpness needed when playing against a team like New Zealand that for other games you may not need to get to.

"Without any disrespect, when you play in New Zealand your mind has to be sharper than when you play a team like Japan."

Before the final round of matches and Nations Championship finals weekend, New Zealand lead the southern hemisphere standings, putting them on course for the title decider at Allianz Stadium on 29 November.

South Africa, who are a point behind in the table and could overtake the All Blacks if they slip up at Twickenham on Saturday, visit Ireland later in the day.

The build-up in Dublin has been dominated by Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus' criticism of match officials and subsequent six-Test ban.

While Borthwick would not be drawn on Erasmus' situation or comments, he stressed the importance of respect for referees and their colleagues.

"When I first picked up a rugby ball aged 11, my schoolteacher told me, 'you call the referee sir'," he added.

"For so many years I still called the referees sir, because it's just so well ingrained. For this brilliant sport we're involved in, respect is integral. It is different to other sports and it's one of the reasons I love it."

title: Dates Confirmed for Rugby World Cup 2031
article_text:
World Rugby has confirmed the tournament dates for Men’s Rugby World Cup 2031. The event will kick off on the weekend of October 3-5, 2031 with the final taking place on the weekend of November 14-16, 2031.

The announcement comes with attention firmly on Australia 2027 which is now well under a year away. The USA will compete at that tournament after missing out on France 2003 with losses to Chile and Portugal seeing a changing-up of competitors.

World Rugby’s move to expand the Men’s Rugby World Cup from 20 to 24 teams has come as a safeguard against the 2031 hosts not being involved in the 2027 tournament. The USA and, potential co-hosts Canada, will both compete at Rugby World Cup 2027.

As noted by World Rugby, by this time next year the USA will be hosting baton. The year 2027 will see plenty of progress towards the staging of Rugby World Cup 2031. For example, host cities and venues will be processed ahead of an announcement in early 2028.

Organizers are presently in talks with NFL and MLS venues ahead of the 2028 announcement. The tournament dates of October 3-5 to November 14-16, 2031 mean that there will be a cross-over between the Rugby World Cup and the NFL season.

title: Gloucester-Hartpury boss Murphy exits on eve of new season
article_text:
Gloucester-Hartpury head of rugby Dan Murphy has left the club on the eve of the new Premiership Women's Rugby season.

Murphy took over last season, following the departure of Sean Lynn for the Wales head coach role, and had previously spent four years with the club as scrum coach.

Three-time champions Gloucester-Hartpury finished top of the regular-season table last term but failed to reach the PWR final for the first time in four years after being beaten by Saracens in the semi-finals.

They open their 2026-27 campaign on Saturday away to Sale Sharks.

"We recognise that the timing of this change, immediately before the start of the season, is not ideal," a club statement said., external

"However, this decision ensures stability for the squad ahead of an important first game."

The statement added the decision was made following a "review of the programme".

"The club believes the change is in Gloucester-Hartpury's best interests," it continued.

Murphy's departure follows the exit of backs and attack coach Matt Banahan at the end of last season.

The remaining coaching team will take charge for the upcoming match, with former London Irish captain Luke Narraway joining as consultant coach while the long-term structure of the team is decided.

Gloucester-Hartpury won 14 consecutive league games in 2025-26 to storm once again to the top of the table.

However, defeats in their final two games of the campaign, before a semi-final loss to Trailfinders, meant their season ended on a muted note after a run of three championship triumphs.

They have also lost a number of influential players over the summer, including mainstays of the club as it grew into the league's dominant force in recent seasons.

England captain Zoe Stratford and fellow Red Roses centre Tatyana Heard, back-row forward Sarah Beckett and Wales hooker Kelsey Jones have all joined Saturday's opponents Sale, while Wales back-row Bethan Lewis left for Bristol.

Murphy added in a statement: "I would like to place on record my thanks to the players, staff and loyal fans for their support throughout my time at Gloucester-Hartpury.

"I wish everyone at the club all the best for the future."

title: Scotland's £70,000 World Rugby fine explained
article_text:
Scottish Rugby were fined £70,000 in 2019 over comments made about World Rugby before their controversial Rugby World Cup clash against Japan.

The Pool A fixture was in doubt due to the approach of Typhoon Hagibis, with its cancellation potentially ending Scotland's hopes of reaching the quarter-finals.

Former SRU chief executive Mark Dodson, who stepped down in 2024, hit out at World Rugby's "rigidity" over the situation and hinted at legal action if the match was called off.

An independent disputes committee subsequently ruled that his comments amounted to misconduct and "brought the game into disrepute".

"Prior to its decision, the committee gave the parties ample time to resolve the dispute," it said in a statement.

"World Rugby made an open offer to the SRU, which required the SRU to apologise for its conduct and make a donation to the typhoon disaster relief fund in Japan.

"The SRU suggested alternative wording, which included a mutual expression of regret from both parties - and no apology."

Scottish Rugby was formally reprimanded, fined £70,000 and ordered to "issue in writing a meaningful apology to World Rugby and RWCL for its misconduct in terms approved by the committee".

The governing body had initially rejected World Rugby's proposed settlement, which included an apology and a donation towards typhoon relief efforts.

"World Rugby strongly believed the comments, which suggested an unfair and disorganised treatment of all teams, to be inappropriate and ill-judged at a time when Japan was preparing for the largest and most destructive typhoon in decades," a statement said.

"The international federation believed that such comments brought the game into disrepute, not only in relation to World Rugby's handling of an extraordinary situation but also in the message that it sent to the Japanese people."

The £70,000 fine was directed towards World Rugby's ChildFund Pass It Back programme, supporting communities affected by the typhoon.

The match eventually went ahead, with Scotland suffering a 28-21 defeat to Japan. The result saw them eliminated from the tournament before the quarter-finals.

Following the ruling, Scottish Rugby said: "we will now reflect on this outcome and further consider all our options, which may include arbitration".

The dispute was eventually resolved on 14 November 2019, with Scottish Rugby expressing regret and agreeing to make a £70,000 donation.

title: Steve Borthwick and Fabien Galthie underline importance of respect for officials after Rassie Erasmus comments
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

England head coach Steve Borthwick and France counterpart Fabien Galthie have emphasised the importance of upholding respect for match officials after South Africa’s Rassie Erasmus was banned for six matches.

Erasmus, who has led the Springboks to back-to-back World Cup wins, was suspended for a third time having made comments that questioned the integrity of officials earlier this week.

The 54-year-old, previously banned by World Rugby in 2021 and 2022, made reference to “match-fixing” in wide-ranging comments as he sought to draw attention to what he perceived as double standards within the sport after South Africa’s defeat to France and Ireland’s win over Fiji.

The Springboks take on Andy Farrell’s side on Dublin on Saturday evening, with Erasmus – banned from matchday involvement – intending to run a live stream from his hotel room of his reactions to the game.

While wishing not to directly comment on Erasmus’s remarks, both Borthwick and Galthie used their team announcement press conferences to underline the values of rugby they believe should be maintained.

“In the world of coaching, I have a duty of conscience towards the fans, towards the coaches, towards the players,” Galthie explained. “I have a duty and a responsibility towards the world of rugby, towards World Rugby. When you hold the position of head coach, you are responsible for your words, responsible for your behaviour.

“As a coach, I have to take care of the refereeing. If I don't take care of the referees, if I talk about referees, then I hurt rugby, I hurt the supporters, I hurt our opponents. The first thing we learn in our sport is fair play. We shake hands with the opponent and arrange to meet for the next match, for the next fight. There's always this idea of honour and fair play. That's how I learned it at rugby school, to say 'Mr referee’, shake his hand at the end of the match, take care of him.

"You have to be careful because rugby is a sport that is heavily refereed. More than half of the actions are stopped or whistled by an official. Without a referee, there is no rugby. There is no rugby among children, there is no education, since we have to respect a rule.”

Echoing a similar theme, Borthwick underscored the difficult role that referees have.

“What I will say is that match officials have a really tough job,” the England head coach stressed. “It's a really challenging job that match officials have.

“Number two, I have absolute 100 per cent confidence and faith that every match official in every game tries to do the very best they can. And, number three, I think they deserve enormous respect. And that's the way in rugby, you respect the match officials; any player or coach, we expect the same.

“In the values of our game, respect is clearly central to that. You call the referee ‘Sir’. And I still do now, it has been a habit for so many years, you call the referee ‘Sir’. It doesn’t mean we always agree but you get on with it. That is what you do in rugby.”

Erasmus has exercised his right to a full misconduct hearing after being handed the six-match ban.

title: New country welcomed into World Rugby fold as Oceania Rugby suspended
article_text:
Mali has been granted full World Rugby membership, while Oceania Rugby has been suspended from World Rugby Council membership pending an investigation into governance matters.

The decisions were among a series of outcomes announced following a World Rugby Council meeting in Dublin.

Mali’s application for full membership was unanimously approved by Council after a review process, completing a journey that began when the Malian Rugby Federation joined World Rugby as an associate member in 2004.

The promotion means Mali becomes World Rugby’s newest full member.

It takes the governing body’s total membership to 119 full members and 16 associate members.

World Rugby chair Brett Robinson said the decision reflected the progress made by the Malian Rugby Federation in developing and governing the game.

“Having been part of the World Rugby family since 2004, Mali’s progression to full membership represents an important step in the continued development of rugby in the country,” Robinson said.

Mali’s admission comes as World Rugby continues efforts to expand the game in emerging rugby markets, particularly across Africa. The federation has worked alongside Rugby Africa to grow participation and infrastructure within the country and has outlined ambitions to host major continental tournaments in the future.

The Council meeting also confirmed the reinstatement of Asia Rugby as a member of Council after meeting governance and administrative requirements.

Robinson said: “We are delighted to welcome back Asia Rugby, and their representatives Ada and Qais to Council, and look forward to working together to build a strong future for a region that will be represented by two nations – Japan and Hong Kong China – at a men’s Rugby World Cup for the first time next year. This will provide huge impetus for growth.”

Meanwhile, Oceania Rugby has been suspended from World Rugby Council membership while an investigation into governance matters takes place.

World Rugby stated that Oceania Rugby remains a member of the international federation and is cooperating fully with the process. Oceania Rugby is one of six regional associations of World Rugby, with 17 full member unions including the likes of Australia, New Zealand, Fiji, Samoa, and Tonga, as well as host of smaller Pacific island nations.

Samoa Rugby also remains self-suspended from Council membership while an ongoing review continues.

Further governance changes were confirmed with former Australia captain John Eales and ex-Argentina scrum-half Agustín Pichot elected to the World Rugby Executive Board as southern hemisphere high-performance union representatives.

The pair secured the highest number of votes from a ballot of 49 available votes and will replace SA Rugby president Mark Alexander and New Zealand representative Bart Campbell.

Under governance reforms approved in 2024, the Executive Board includes two northern hemisphere and two southern hemisphere high-performance union representatives alongside regional, performance, player and independent representatives.

Eales and Pichot take up their positions as World Rugby continues the rollout of its long-term strategic plan, which has included the introduction of new international competitions and a revised governance structure.

They succeed SA Rugby President Mark Alexander and New Zealand representative Bart Campbell.

“Congratulations to John and Agustín on their election to the Board,” said Robinson. “We are a year into implementation of our bold and ambitious new strategy, and John and Agustín will bring a new perspective and important insights as we continue to focus on making the business of rugby stronger, more resilient and impactful, while ensuring a game that is attractive and protects and supports our players on and off the field.”

title: Townsend makes 11 changes to Scotland side for Japan clash
article_text:
Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend has made 11 changes to the side that will face Japan in the Nations Championship on Saturday.

Only Zander Fagerson and captain Rory Darge, plus Darcy Graham and Tom Jordan - who shifts to fly-half - are retained in the starting line-up from the win over Australia last weekend.

Ollie Smith and Rory Hutchinson are involved for the first time and start at fullback and inside centre, with Stafford McDowall also handed a first start of the autumn at outside centre.

Kyle Rowe, who started the defeat to New Zealand, returns on the wing, alongside record try-scorer Graham, as Jamie Dobie starts at scrum-half.

Up front, Fagerson is joined by his Glasgow Warriors colleagues Nathan McBeth and Gregor Hiddleston, while Jonny Gray and Max Williamson form the second row partnership.

Liam McConnell has been handed a start at blindside flanker, while Ollie Leatherbarrow gets his first start after making his debut last weekend.

On the bench, Seb Stephen and Magnus Bradbury are set for their first involvements of the series with George Horne and Blair Kinghorn covering the back division on a 6:2 split.

title: Furbank leads returning England trio for All Blacks visit
article_text:
England have been boosted by the recovery and return of George Furbank, Seb Atkinson and Ollie Chessum to their starting line-up to face New Zealand on Saturday in the Nations Championship.

The trio, who all missed last weekend's win over Japan with knocks, are joined in the starting line-up by Will Joseph, who crossed for five tries against the Brave Blossoms.

Furbank held off the challenge of Freddie Steward, who impressed against Japan, to regain the full-back slot, while vice-captain Chessum brings ballast to a back row that is completed by Ben Curry and Ben Earl.

Fin Smith returns at fly-half to reprise a 10-12 combination with Atkinson that has started six of England's last seven Tests and dates back to their days as teenagers in Worcester Warriors academy.

Barring Joseph's inclusion for the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, England have named the same matchday 23 which combined excellently in the 45-12 victory over Australia a fortnight ago.

After last year's 33-19 success, England are aiming for successive wins over the All Blacks for the first time since beating them in November 2002 and June 2003 - five months before Rugby World Cup glory in Australia.

"There are few bigger occasions in international rugby than facing New Zealand," said head coach Steve Borthwick.

"It's a fixture that always carries a special significance, and one that the players are hugely looking forward to.

"We know the quality New Zealand have in their team. We've prepared for the very best version of them, knowing the challenge they will bring and the level we'll need to reach to get the result we want."

New Zealand, meanwhile, have also been bolstered by the return of big names.

Following their shock defeat by Wales in Cardiff last weekend, Jordie Barrett, Damian McKenzie and Cam Roigard are brought back in, while wing Will Jordan - his country's leading all-time try-scorer - has recovered from a hamstring issue to start.

Full-back Beauden Barrett, who skippered the side for the first time in Cardiff, will win his 150th Test cap, becoming only the fourth men's player - alongside Alun Wyn Jones, James Slipper and Sam Whitelock - to achieve the landmark.

Beauden and Jordie Barrett's brother Scott is in the second row, while Codie Taylor captains from hooker.

New Zealand lead the Nations Championship southern hemisphere standings by one point and any sort of victory over England is likely to be enough to book their place in the headline fixture of next weekend's play-off finals.

France, who lead the northern hemisphere table and play Argentina later on Saturday, would be their likeliest opponents.

A victory for England, however, could mean Borthwick's men forcing their way into the title play-off, while Ireland and South Africa, who meet in Dublin at 16:40 GMT, could also have a say in an intriguing finale to the group stage.

title: Ireland hooker Sheehan at number eight for Springboks game
article_text:
Ireland captain Dan Sheehan has been named at number eight for Saturday's highly anticipated Nations Championship match against world champions South Africa in Dublin.

Having won all 42 of his previous caps at hooker, the 28-year-old returns after recovering from a concussion to partner flankers Ryan Baird and Josh van der Flier in the back row.

Ireland head coach Andy Farrell has faced an injury crisis at number eight with regular skipper Caelan Doris, Jack Conan, Sean Jansen and recent debutant James McNabney all ruled out.

Nick Timoney, who was handed the jersey for last week's victory over Fiji, drops to the bench.

With Doris and Conan unavailable, Sheehan anchored the scrum in Leinster's United Rugby Championship win over Munster last month, but Saturday will be his first Test run-out in the back row.

"Most people would agree that he [Sheehan]'s a world-class player, not just good," said Farrell, who did not wish to comment on South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus' six-match ban for questioning the integrity of match officials.

"Throwing the ball in or scrummaging, his point of difference is in and around the field and how he plays the game with ball in hand or defensively, running lines and all of that.

"That's suited to number eight. He was training there all last week because he was on the 12-day return-to-play protocols, so we had a bit of a head start there, and he played there recently.

"He's very cool, calm and collected; there's no arrogance there whatsoever. Things don't bother him, so he takes it all in his stride, fully confident in his own ability."

Sheehan's move means that Ronan Kelleher keeps his place at hooker after starting the Fiji game, again joining props Andrew Porter and Tadhg Furlong in the front row.

After being rested last week, Joe McCarthy returns to the second row to partner Tadhg Beirne, with Van der Flier edging out Timoney for the number seven jersey.

Sam Prendergast starts at fly-half after being cleared to face the Springboks on Wednesday, with Jamison Gibson-Park retained at scrum-half.

Prendergast, 23, was cited for his hip-drop tackle on Fiji's Peceli Yato - which was not punished on the pitch - but an independent disciplinary panel ruled the challenge was not worthy of a red card.

"Nothing's changed for us all week," Farrell said when asked about the possibility of a Prendergast ban.

"There's always something going on, whether it's dealing with HIA (head injury assessment) injuries or incidents like we've had with Sam this week.

"It (the hearing) was late on Tuesday night; we trained Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday and Sam's done all of that so there's been no hiccups for us, let's say that."

Robbie Henshaw and Stuart McCloskey both return to midfield after Farrell opted to pair Jamie Osborne and Bundee Aki in a new-look centre partnership against Fiji.

However, Osborne was replaced by McCloskey in the third minute after sustaining a pectoral injury that has ruled him out of the South Africa game, while Aki drops to the bench.

With Hugo Keenan returning to full-back for his 50th cap after sitting out the Fiji game, Mack Hansen switches to the left wing with Robert Baloucoune retained on the right. Tommy O'Brien, who scored two tries from the left wing against Fiji, drops out of the squad.

Farrell has opted for a split of five forwards and three backs on the bench. Tom Stewart, Tom O'Toole, Sam Illo, James Ryan and Timoney provide pack cover with Craig Casey, Ciaran Frawley and Aki named as backline reinforcements.

South Africa, who named their team on Monday, make five changes with record cap holder Eben Etzebeth recalled to the second row.

Cameron Hanekom is named at number eight, replacing Jasper Wiese, who was handed a four-week suspension after being sent off for a dangerous clear-out in last week's defeat by France.

Ox Nche, Malcolm Marx and Wilco Louw are named as the starting front row.

Erasmus also named Nche, Marx and Louw to start the France game but swapped them out for Jan-Hendrik Wessels, Gerhard Steenekamp and Thomas du Toit shortly before kick-off at the Stade de France.

As part of the six-game ban handed down by World Rugby on Tuesday, Erasmus is not permitted to attend the Aviva Stadium encounter.

The 54-year-old has since announced he will be hosting an online watchalong of the match while he watches from his team's Dublin hotel.

South Africa sit second in the Nations Championship southern hemisphere standings, a point adrift of New Zealand.

A South Africa win over Ireland coupled with England beating the All Blacks (Saturday, 14:10 GMT) would be enough for Erasmus' side to seal a place in the 29 November final against the top-ranked northern hemisphere side at Twickenham.

Ireland must beat the Springboks and hope France and England falter against Argentina and New Zealand to finish top.

The Springboks won 24-13 at Aviva Stadium last year, their first victory over Ireland in Dublin since 2012.

Ireland: H Keenan; R Baloucoune, R Henshaw, S McCloskey, M Hansen; S Prendergast, J Gibson-Park; A Porter, R Kelleher, T Furlong, J McCarthy, T Beirne, R Baird, J van der Flier, D Sheehan (capt).

Replacements: T Stewart, T O'Toole, S Illo, J Ryan, N Timoney, C Casey, C Frawley, B Aki.

South Africa: Willemse; Arendse, Kriel, De Allende, Hooker; Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Van den Berg; Nche, Marx, Louw, Etzebeth, Nortje, Kolisi (capt), PS du Toit, Hanekom.

title: Scotland make 11 changes for Japan with yet another Lion forced to withdraw
article_text:
Scotland have retained just four starters from their victory over Australia as Gregor Townsend makes 11 changes for Saturday’s Nations Championship meeting with Japan at Scottish Gas Murrayfield.

Among those coming in is Newcastle Red Bulls back-row Ollie Leatherbarrow, who will make his first Test start at No.8 after making his debut from the bench in last weekend’s 15-12 victory over the Wallabies.

Darcy Graham, Tom Jordan, Zander Fagerson and captain Rory Darge are the only survivors from the XV that started against Australia, while British & Irish Lion Pierre Schoeman has become the latest player forced to withdraw through injury.

The loosehead has picked up a neck problem and has been replaced in the wider squad by Alec Hepburn. Schoeman joins fellow 2025 Lions Sione Tuipulotu, Ben White and Scott Cummings on the sidelines, with the trio already ruled out for the remainder of the Nations Championship earlier this week.

Leatherbarrow is joined in the back-row by Liam McConnell at blindside and Darge at openside, with the latter retaining the captaincy after his Player of the Match display against Australia.

Jonny Gray and Max Williamson form a new second-row pairing, while Nathan McBeth and Gregor Hiddleston come into the front row alongside Fagerson.

Jordan switches from inside centre to fly-half, with Jamie Dobie promoted from the bench to start at scrum-half. Stafford McDowall and Rory Hutchinson form a new midfield partnership.

Ollie Smith is named at full-back, with Graham moving to the right wing and Kyle Rowe coming in on the left.

Scotland have retained a six-two split among the replacements, where Seb Stephen and Magnus Bradbury could make their first appearances of the November campaign.

Scotland XV: 15 Ollie Smith, 14 Darcy Graham, 13 Stafford McDowall (vc), 12 Rory Hutchinson, 11 Kyle Rowe, 10 Tom Jordan, 9 Jamie Dobie, 1 Nathan McBeth, 2 Gregor Hiddleston, 3 Zander Fagerson, 4 Jonny Gray, 5 Max Williamson, 6 Liam McConnell, 7 Rory Darge (c), 8 Ollie Leatherbarrow.

Replacements: 16 Seb Stephen, 17 Rory Sutherland, 18 Will Hurd, 19 Gregor Brown, 20 Magnus Bradbury, 21 Matt Fagerson, 22 George Horne, 23 Blair Kinghorn.
