Replacements: 16 Mamoru Harada, 17 Yota Kamimori, 18 Taufa Latu, 19 Michael Stolberg, 20 Ruan Botha, 21 Tiennan Costley, 22 Shinobu Fujiwara, 23 Riku Kitahara.

title: Beauden Barrett to win 150th cap as All Blacks ring changes for England clash
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Beauden Barrett will make his 150th appearance for New Zealand as Dave Rennie brings back the big guns as the All Blacks look to bounce back against England.

Barrett captained the side in the shock defeat to Wales last week but retains his place at full-back in a heavily-changed backline, with younger brother Jordie Barrett and Will Jordan both passed fit to start.

Cam Roigard and Damian McKenzie return in the halves while Anton Lienert-Brown retains a starting spot following injury to Quinn Tupaea.

Up front, Codie Taylor captains the side from hooker, while Fabian Holland and Tupou Vaa’i are significant additions to the starting pack.

“It’s a great occasion for Beauden and his family. To wear the All Black Test jersey 150 times is an amazing achievement and testament to the impact he has had on this team over the past 15 seasons,” Rennie said. “He is a top man whose contribution off-field has been equally as impressive.

“England are a quality side and playing them at Allianz Stadium is always a big challenge. With the Hillary Shield and play-off spots for the Nations Championship Finals weekend all on the line, there is plenty to play for.”

England beat New Zealand last November in a defeat that precipitated the departure of head coach Scott Robertson.

Rennie was brought in as a replacement earlier this year but is facing fresh pressure after a first defeat to Wales in 73 years.

The eldest Barrett brother becomes the second All Black, after Sam Whitelock, and fourth player overall to reach 150 Test caps.

New Zealand XV: 1 Ethan de Groot, 2 Codie Taylor (capt.), 3 Fletcher Newell; 4 Scott Barrett, 5 Fabian Holland; 6 Tupou Vaa’i, 7 Peter Lakai, 8 Wallace Sititi; 9 Cam Roigard, 10 Damian McKenzie; 11 Josh Moorby, 12 Jordie Barrett, 13 Anton Lienert-Brown, 14 Will Jordan; 15 Beauden Barrett.

Replacements: 16 Asafo Aumua, 17 George Bower, 18 Pasilio Tosi, 19 Anton Segner, 20 Leicester Fainga’anuku; 21 Cortez Ratima, 22 Richie Mo’unga, 23 Rieko Ioane.

title: Botham 'disappointed' to be rested after starring against All Blacks
article_text:
Wales took the decision to take James Botham out of the side to face Australia for rugby reasons rather than paternity leave.

The blind-side flanker was named man of the match when he helped Steve Tandy's side create history by beating New Zealand at Principality Stadium.

The 28-year-old Cardiff forward made 30 tackles and got through a mountain of work.

Botham's partner is expecting their first child this week, but that was not the reason for club-mate Alex Mann's return in his place.

"We are obviously aware of it [the pregnancy] and for James, regardless of whether he was playing or not, that would be the primary focus, but it wasn't something that was part of selection," said head coach Tandy.

Mann has started in 12 of 14 Tests under Tandy and returns along with number eight Aaron Wainwright, who missed the All Blacks game because of a leg injury.

Botham and his Cardiff team-mate Taine Basham drop out of the matchday squad, with promising Exeter flanker Kane James set to win his second cap off the bench.

"James is disappointed not to play, but we have some amazing young men in our group," said Tandy about Botham.

"In training on Tuesday he was leading the charge and doing Australia things.

"We know if we want to be consistent in the long term then we need everyone going in the right way and providing competition.

"We have made changes in the back row because we feel it's an energy piece, Manny and Waino are pretty good players as well.

"Waino missed out through injury last week and Taine [Basham] stepped up, Manny played really well against Japan and will add energy."

Back-row forward Taine Plumtree made a big impact as a replacement in the final quarter against New Zealand.

He remains on the bench for the Wallabies and will also cover lock in the absence of Adam Beard, who is likely to be available for Nations Championship finals weekend after a shoulder injury.

title: CHIMP SPORT: Lady Cranes Set Sights on SVNS 2 Promotion in Dubai
article_text:
Uganda’s national women’s rugby sevens team, the Lady Cranes, have been flagged off for the HSBC SVNS 3 tournament scheduled for November 27–28 in Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

The 15-member contingent, comprising 12 players and three officials, was flagged off on Thursday at Cooper Chimney in Lugogo ahead of the two-day competition at The Sevens Stadium.

Uganda earned qualification for the Dubai event after winning their maiden Rugby Africa Women’s Sevens tournament in Nairobi, Kenya, earlier this month.

The victory secured the Lady Cranes a direct place in the third tier of World Rugby’s revamped sevens competition structure, where six nations will battle for promotion to HSBC SVNS 2.

Uganda will face China, Colombia, Poland, Samoa and Mexico in a round-robin format, with the top two teams securing qualification for the next tier, scheduled for early 2027 in Nairobi, São Paulo and Montevideo.

Head coach Onencan Charles believes the team can build on its recent success in Nairobi despite the limited preparation time.

“We’ve prepared quite well. It has been a very short time since we returned from Nairobi for the Rugby Africa tournament, but the girls are geared up because we still have the momentum from the recent competition,” Onencan said.

Captain Peace Lekuru also expressed confidence in the team’s readiness, identifying a top-two finish as their primary target.

“Our main goal is to finish in the top two and qualify for HSBC SVNS 2. Everyone is focused and prepared for the competition ahead. I feel so excited to lead the team again,” Lekuru said.

Players: Peace Lekuru (Captain), Adong Susan, Mufuwa Racheal, Namabiro Lydia, Nayiga Sarah Kirabo, Namukwaya Fazirah, Nabaggala Grace, Akello Tina Molly, Namutebi Bushira, Namboozo Matsula, Namulala Unity and Nandawula Juliet.

Management: Onencan Charles (Head Coach), Winnie Atyang (Team Manager) and Mayeku Nelson (Team Physiotherapist).

title: Scotland suffer Pierre Schoeman injury blow as Alec Hepburn gets Japan chance
article_text:
Scotland have suffered an injury blow with prop Pierre Schoeman ruled out of the clash with Japan due to a neck problem.

The experienced Edinburgh loosehead has left the Scotland camp and returned to his club for further assessment, leaving Gregor Townsend without one of his key forwards.

Schoeman’s absence has, however, opened the door for Alec Hepburn to join the squad as Scotland prepare for their final assignment of the campaign.

Townsend’s side will be aiming to finish on a high against Japan and build on their victory over Australia, having previously suffered defeat against New Zealand.

Read more: Scottish Rugby on how finances have taken step forward despite £1.4m loss

A convincing win could also prove significant as Scotland battle for the best possible finish in the standings.

Scotland and Wales appear locked in a fight for fourth place, with points difference potentially crucial depending on results elsewhere.

Ireland remain capable of being dragged into the equation, although that would require an almighty pasting against the Springboks combined with either Scotland or Wales running riot in their respective fixtures.

For Scotland, the focus will be on taking care of their own business against Japan despite losing Schoeman from the pack.

title: Wainwright and Adams back for Wales against Australia
article_text:
Wales have made four changes to the side that made history against New Zealand for the Nations Championship fixture against Australia.

Head coach Steve Tandy has tinkered with the starting line-up that beat the All Blacks for the first time in 73 years at Principality Stadium.

Wales go with the same XV that opened the Nations Championship with a 28-21 victory against Japan.

Alex Mann comes in for James Botham at blind-side flanker, Aaron Wainwright is back from a leg injury at number eight, lock Ben Carter returns for the injured Adam Beard and Josh Adams gets the nod on the wing.

Botham was man of the match against New Zealand but is not included after a huge defensive effort.

His partner is expecting their first child this week, but Wales say that is not the reason for the flanker sitting out the Wallabies game.

Exeter flanker Kane James is set to win his second cap from the bench after making his debut against Argentina in July.

Scarlets centre or fly-half Joe Hawkins also comes in for Ospreys playmaker Dan Edwards, who suffered an ankle injury in training that has led to Cardiff's Jarrod Evans being called into the Nations Championship squad.

Taine Plumtree will cover the second row in the absence of Beard, who suffered a shoulder injury against New Zealand.

Number eight Taine Basham and wing Gabriel Hamer-Webb drop out of the matchday squad after starting against the All Blacks.

Tandy says he had always intended to make changes.

"We made nearly 350 tackles, the ball in play time was one of the highest in Test rugby in the last three years and we have got competition," said the Wales head coach.

"The plan was always to freshen up and we are likely to do similar for the week after, because we need to find out about players.

"We have fresh and hungry players coming in, which will add the energy that we need at the weekend.

"The training environment is getting more competitive in certain positions we have the ability to put people in and feel confident about performance."

Eleven players will have started all three Tests - eight from English clubs and the Scarlets trio of full-back Blair Murray, centre Eddie James and fly-half Sam Costelow.

Wing Adams will win his 75th cap and returns after being left out against New Zealand despite scoring twice against Japan.

The 31-year-old Cardiff back has shown no signs of disappointment according to Tandy, despite missing out on history.

"He is a class rugby player but also a class man," he said.

"He is a big leader and is over the moon for the group. You saw him driving standards on the Tuesday and he knows where we need to go and how we need to keep building.

"He is an incredible person and did really well against Japan, but we need to have competition, to grow and keep pushing."

After beating Japan and the All Blacks, Wales are looking to complete a Cardiff hat-trick against the Wallabies.

They then travel to Twickenham's Allianz Stadium for finals weekend when they will play a southern hemisphere opponent, which could well be another fixture against the Japanese.

Tandy said: "It's our last home game of this competition. The support that fans give to the players and staff has been incredible and we can't wait to get back out at Principality Stadium."

The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has stated it has already sold more than 60,000 tickets for the fixture at Principality Stadium, which holds just under 74,000.

That figure exceeds the 55,152 that witnessed history against the All Blacks, despite the late kick-off time against the Wallabies.

Exeter's Tom Hooper has been named in the second row for Australia while flanker Carlo Tizzano starts in five forward changes from the team that lost to Scotland.

The front rows rotate roles for this Test with Isaac Kailea, Brandon Paenga-Amosa and Taniela Tupou selected as the starting combination, with Angus Bell, Billy Pollard and Allan Alaalatoa the replacements.

Lock Jeremy Williams and Fraser McReight are also on the bench as Australia contend with a six-day turnaround.

Wallabies head coach Les Kiss said: "We know we need to step up against a Welsh team full of confidence and momentum after their historic win against the All Blacks last weekend.

"Pulling on the gold jersey against Wales at Principality Stadium in Cardiff creates one of the great atmospheres in world rugby and we are focused on being up for the occasion."

Wales: Murray; Rees-Zammit, E James, Llewellyn, Adams; Costelow, T Williams; Smith, Lake (capt), Griffin, Jenkins, Carter, Mann, Morgan, Wainwright.

Replacements: Elias, G Thomas, Lewis, Plumtree, K James, Morgan-Williams, Hawkins, Hennessey.

Australia: Wright; Jorgensen, Suaalii, Ikitau, Potter; Gorden, Lonergan; Kailea, Paenga-Amosa, Tupou, Canham, Hooper, Valetini, Tizzano, Wilson (capt).

Replacements: Pollard, Bell, Alaalatoa, Williams, McReight, Thomas, Donaldson, Daugunu.

Assistant referees: Karl Dickson (England) & Jeremy Rozier (France).

title: Wales name team to face Australia as four come in and star to make home debut
article_text:
Wales have named their team to face Australia on Saturday, with Steve Tandy making four changes to the side that made history against New Zealand last week.

Last weekend’s starting XV wrote itself into Welsh rugby folklore by ending the 73-year wait for another win over the All Blacks. But that hasn’t stopped Tandy from making changes - with four new faces in his walk-on side for Saturday night.

It’s not a totally new combination - with Tandy reverting to the starting side that faced Japan at the start of the campaign.

In the backs, Josh Adams is brought back into the left wing - having been rested last week - with Gabriel Hamer-Webb missing out.

There’s three changes to the pack - with Aaron Wainwright back from injury to start at No. 8 ahead of Taine Basham.

Alex Mann replaces last week's player of the match James Botham in the back-row, while Ben Carter is in for Adam Beard.

On the bench, Kane James is set to win his first cap on home soil - having been named as a replacement.

Joe Hawkins is also in line for his first appearance of the autumn, being named on the bench - with Dan Edwards injured.

The Wallabies named their team for Saturday's match early on Thursday morning, with head coach Les Kiss making five changes to his pack.

"The focus this week has been on continuing to build and challenge our game in a short preparation week," said Kiss. “We know we need to step up against a Welsh team full of confidence and momentum after their historic win against the All Blacks last weekend.

“Pulling on the gold jersey against Wales at Principality Stadium in Cardiff creates one of the great atmospheres in world rugby and we are focused on being up for the occasion.”

Replacements: Ryan Elias, Gareth Thomas, Dillon Lewis, Taine Plumtree, Kane James, Reuben Morgan-Williams, Joe Hawkins, Louie Hennessey.

Replacements: Billy Pollard, Angus Bell, Allan Alaalatoa, Jeremy Williams, Fraser McReight, Kalani Thomas, Ben Donaldson, Filipo Daugunu.

title: PWR: RFU wants to 'protect Red Roses' with reduction in international players
article_text:
World rugby has endured a few shocks and upsets in 2026 - and England's women losing back-to-back Test matches to Canada was among the biggest.

But with 25 Canadians plying their trade on English soil in Premiership Women's Rugby (PWR) last season, their success on the international stage comes at a time when PWR has been in discussions with the Rugby Football Union (RFU) to review the numbers of overseas players in the league.

"We are keen to attract star talent into PWR to continue to make it the best league in the world," said RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney.

"But we've also got to protect England Red Roses' interests as well."

Changes have been planned for the 2027-28 PWR season around injury dispensation for foreign players, with the removal of club injury credit which helps to cover the cost of replacing an injured player.

Only players who sustain an injury while on international duty for one of England's representative teams will be eligible.

However, discussions have gone further around the numbers of English Qualified Players (EQP) required in matchday squads.

Speaking to BBC Sport, Sweeney said: "We're talking about it. Currently, there's 13 EQP in PWR. It's 15 in the [men's] Prem.

"We're always concerned about the amount of game time that's occurring for under-23 players coming through the system. Are they getting enough game time?

"We're having conversations with PWR in terms of how we can maximise that, so it is a live topic."

England had been on a 41-match unbeaten streak - dating back almost four years - before twice losing to Canada in the WXV Global Series last month.

It prompted a warning from head coach John Mitchell that too many overseas players in the PWR could be detrimental for future Red Roses sides.

The league has increasingly attracted the best global talent. In recent years, a majority of Scotland and Wales players have played in PWR and since the 2025 World Cup, more players have joined from New Zealand.

The highest-profile arrival last season was Black Ferns captain Ruahei Demant linking up with Bristol, while Ruby Tui has joined Trailfinders Women for the new campaign.

And while many neutrals believe Canada's growing success is good for the women's game, Sweeney says England must keep "raising the bar".

"It doesn't feel it's good for the game for us, we never want to lose - but it had to come at some stage," he said.

"Seeing the growth in the Canadian team, largely due to where they play in PWR - it's encouraging that the standards are rising.

"We're conscious that unions like Ireland are investing much more heavily now into the women's game as well, so it is good for the game.

"From our perspective, we just want to keep raising the bar and challenging people to catch us and challenge us."

Canada and Saracens scrum-half Olivia Apps was named PWR player of the season when her club lifted the 2025-26 trophy.

She says exposure to the PWR has massively benefited Canadian rugby.

"It's the best women's league right now to play in and the best quality competition," she told BBC Sport.

"We don't have a league back home, so to be able to come from the universities and play with and against the best players in the world is going to make us better for sure."

Asked if she was worried Canadian players would not get as much game time in the future, Apps said: "I would hope not. I think that would diminish the quality of the PWR.

"Internationals make this league what it is, and credit to the English players, but the internationals really do contribute in a great way.

"Any coach or team that has a Canadian on their side loves to have that Canadian because they work hard, they bring the physicality, the athleticism and a great style of rugby."

Reducing foreign imports would allow young English talent more PWR game time, but the move does not come without concerns.

"The league itself is to create Red Roses and to create English players for the future. If we are going to bring non-EQP players into the league, then they have to add to the league, so they have to be of a world-class standard," said Loughborough Lightning head coach Nathan Smith.

But Smith does envisage a problem if the league changes before investing in the pathways.

"There's a pinch point at the start of next season where we'll have Lions, England camp and a Premiership Cup. My simple question is, are there enough players to fulfil all three?" he said.

"England Under-20s and Under-18s aren't performing on the world stage, therefore what can we do to support that? We need a level of competition that sits below the PWR that fulfils their needs for development."

A PWR spokesperson said: "There is no difference of opinion between us and the RFU on this and developing the next generation of Red Roses is a specific, stated objective of the PWR.

"We will continue to work collaboratively with the RFU on EQP and any other matter which is important to the future of women's rugby in this country."

The new PWR season starts on Friday as Loughborough Lightning host Trailfinders.

For now, overseas stars will remain a key part of the league's success, but how many are allowed to feature in the future may define its next chapter.

title: Tamaiti Williams reaches major milestone in recovery from disc-eating infection
article_text:
Tamaiti Williams has reached a significant milestone in his recovery from the back infection that ended his 2026 season after just two games for the Crusaders: running.

The All Blacks prop has been sidelined since discovering that methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) had been eating a disc in his lower back, causing immense pain and putting more than just his rugby career in jeopardy.

Following a surgical procedure that included fusing two discs together, Williams has been slowly progressing through a lengthy rehab process as he eyes an eventual return to rugby.

The 26-year-old was named in the Crusaders’ 2027 squad, but with an injury replacement in Frenchman Clément Castets, signalling he is expected to miss at least part of the coming season.

One month later, Williams’ timeline remains uncertain, but the club shared a promising update to their social media channels on Thursday afternoon. The 27-Test All Black was shown jogging on a treadmill while attached to a load-sharing machine, which was holding 25 per cent of his body weight to ease the stress on his lower body and back.

“I feel fit. I feel light,” he said, grinning in the video. “It feels pretty foreign, though. I haven’t run since March, before all of the chaos happened. It feels good, though. No pain, which is good.”

Williams said his body “feels good” after his first run in eight months, adding: “We’ll get our recovery done and then we’ll go again.”

Crusaders physio John Roche was by Williams’ side for the milestone, and was thrilled to see it all go smoothly.

“This piece of kit is pretty amazing; it weighs the athlete, and then we can adjust the percentage of body weight so they can run at less than their full body weight. So, Tams is running at 75 per cent of his body weight at the moment.

“The treadmill can go up to 30 kilometres an hour, so you can run fast, but obviously he’s not going to do that for his first run. It’s just great to see the big man up and running.”

title: All Blacks to address mentality concerns ahead of decisive England Test
article_text:
All Blacks forwards coach Jason Ryan emerged from Saturday’s historic loss to Wales with questions over his team’s mentality in the match, questions he intends to answer ahead of a decisive Test against England at Twickenham this weekend.

New Zealand were beaten by a remarkable Welsh performance in the penultimate round of Nations Championship pool play that made more tackles than any team before them in Test history, but also came out of the gates firing on attack under the roof at Principality Stadium.

The All Blacks spent most of the final quarter of the Test pummeling the Welsh line, but were given no reward as Wales repelled their efforts and held them up any time they crossed the whitewash. The defensive display earned Ryan’s praise, but it was his side’s lack of energy that he kept coming back to in his immediate post-game reaction.

“It’s disappointing. It’s going to hurt for a while, that one,” Ryan told Jason Pine on Newstalk ZB shortly after the final whistle in Cardiff. “We just didn’t finish the opportunities we had, and they started the game with more intensity than us, and then started the second half with more intensity than us.

“And then, effectively, their defence, we just couldn’t break them down. Credit to them, and they deserve their win.”

Ryan said that after the slow start and Wales taking the lead, his players “went into their shells a little”, keeping Wales on top in the Test.

“We just didn’t come out of the blocks. We did the short kick-off and never regained that, and then they converted straight away and got momentum and bang. Teams score so fast now. But we were under pressure, and we couldn’t get ourselves out of it. And that’s probably the most disappointing thing.

“I’m just disappointed because we can’t hide from the fact that there are potentially parts in that game we’d have to question, mentally, if we were there. I think last week was a massive emotional week for us as a whole team and a whole group, and potentially we might have just been a little bit blasé of how we rolled up into Cardiff and got smacked for it.”

The team is still grieving the unexpected loss of their head of security, Logan Cadwallader, who had been with them for 10 years.

Ryan was adamant the All Blacks did not underestimate Wales’ quality, but admitted they did make life difficult for themselves with their selections. With an inaugural Nations Championship final now just two weeks away, the forwards coach was eager to rebound swiftly.

“Oh no, I don’t think it’s complacency. I just think they started and we just couldn’t pull them back, and that is what it is. We’ve got to move forward. We’ve got to move forward quickly.

“We also made a lot of changes; I think it was 10 that we made, and that’s cohesion. We gave a lot of fellas an opportunity, and there are some pretty good boys sitting in the stands, experience-wise, and potentially we lacked a bit of that at the end as well.

“I think we just have to have a look at it and just see where we were mentally; how we started the Test match.

“You’ve got to say that some of the defensive sets that Wales did were honestly quite unbelievable, and they were pretty spirited, and they hung in there and hung in there, and we just couldn’t break them down. So credit to them, they deserve that one.”

title: USA U20 star among four uncapped players in Australia’s Dubai Sevens squad
article_text:
USA Under-20s centre Dane Mitchell and former Moana Pasifika outside back Denzel Samoa are set to make their Australia Sevens debuts next week, with four uncapped players named to play at the HSBC SVNS Series season opener in Dubai.

Global Youth Sevens standout Bailey Roberts-Lintmeijer and ACT Brumbies prospect Chayse Geros have also been selected. Coach Liam Barry has otherwise gone with a fairly experienced group, which boasts a combined 235 SVNS events between them.

Mitchell made five appearances for the USA at the World Rugby Junior World Championship in Georgia, which included a few starts. But after returning to Australia, the university student got a chance to trial for the sevens side, which has opened the door to travelling the world.

Three-time Olympian Henry Hutchison is the most experienced member of the squad, having played at 68 tournaments, which Maurice Longbottom and James Turner bring more leadership to the national team.

Nathan Lawson is back with the sevens side after a stint in the NRL, having played a handful of matches for the St George Illawarra Dragons. Ben Dalton and Jayden Blake are others who have played in at least 10 events.

Australia will be without a few big-name players for the first stop of the season, with Henry Paterson still sidelined with a knee injury. Will Cartwright (knee) and Ben Dowling (foot) are also unavailable for selection.

“The squad has had a good few weeks in preparation and we are looking forward to our first tournament in Dubai,” Australia Men’s Sevens coach Liam Barry said.

“The 2026/2027 season has the added factor of Olympic qualification so we are well aware of the importance of getting off to a good start.”

Australia kick off their SVNS Series against the USA, South Africa and Argentina, If selected, Mitchell could potentially debut in the green and gold against the United States – who he was eligible for due to his mother.

The Aussies finished the 2025/26 SVNS Series strong with a drought-breaking title in Valladolid. SVNS Series action is stopping by the same destinations as last season, with Cape Town, Singapore, Perth, New York and Vancouver hosting regular season stops.

It’s a particularly important season with the top four teams securing automatic qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The World Championship heads to Hong Kong China, Valladolid and Bordeaux.

title: Wallaroos breakout star set for Australia Sevens debut in Dubai
article_text:
World Rugby Breakthrough Player of the Year nominee Amelia Whitaker will soon fly to Dubai as the only uncapped player in the Australia Women’s Sevens side, who are looking to win the HSBC SVNS Series event for the sixth time in seven years.

Whitaker was named the NSW Waratahs Player of the Year after a stellar Super Rugby Women’s campaign, and the winger was rewarded with higher Wallaroos honours. The 20-year-old rounded out a career-best 15s season with some stellar performances against Scotland.

Prolific Wallaroos try-scorers Desiree Miller and Maya Stewart were joined in the back three by Whitaker, who received Player of the Match honours after scoring two tries in a 56-12 win over Scotland at Sydney’s Accor Stadium.

The Wallaroos kicked off a historic quadruple header at Stadium Australia, with all four Teams in Gold taking the field. Australia faced arch-rivals the Black Ferns Sevens for the third time in less than 24 hours, while Whitaker celebrated with the Wallaroos.

Those SVNS Series players are now Whitaker’s teammates, with Isabella Nasser captaining a side that boasts World Championship-winning experience. Australia took out titles in Valladolid and Bordeaux earlier this year, as they pipped New Zealand in the race for the circuit’s top prize.

Maddison Levi is nearing the all-time try-scoring on the SVNS Series, with the recent Wallaroos debutant looking to chase down New Zealand’s Michalea Brake, who was named in the Black Ferns Sevens squad on Wednesday.

Tia Hinds, Heidi Dennis, Amahli Hala, Teagan Levi, Kaitlin Shave, Kahli Henwood, Bienne Terita, Ruby Nicholas, Kiiahla Duff and Alysia Lefau-Fakosilea have been named. MacKenzie Davis and Faith Nathan are unavailable due to injury.

“The team has had a strong preparation, with plenty of rugby played in different competitions and environments as well as two high-level tournaments together as a squad,” coach Reg Tayler said.

“We have benefited from these experiences and have been able to bring them back some learnings into our environment.

“We’ve got a good balance of youth and experience, and we’re heading to Dubai and Cape Town to set the standard.”

Australia started their SVNS Series matches against France, the USA and Spain in pool play. While New Zealand are the defending champions, the Aussies had won five straight titles at the event before that.

title: Springboks coach invites fans to watch party amid six-game ban
article_text:
Rassie Erasmus has issued an invite to Springboks fans to join a watch party he is hosting online for South Africa’s Nations Championship test against Ireland.

The coach is unable to attend the match due to a six-game ban he copped after a match-fixing rant following South Africa’s loss to France last week.

Under the rules of the ban, he will be unable to enter the stadium, communicate directly or indirectly with players or members of his staff during the match.

The ban will be in effect until a misconduct hearing is conducted per the request of South Africa Rugby. That will not happen before the Ireland game, though.

It is not the first time the outspoken coach has been hit with a ban for his explosive comments, but this time around he is taking a different approach to keep track of his team’s performance and also engage the fans.

The answer: a virtual watch party with the fans.

“Can sit and moan or make the best of it,” Erasmus wrote on X.

“I’ll be watching the match at the hotel, not keen to watch on my own. So let’s give it a go and hope I get the tech sorted – TV on, my laptop camera on and you’re welcome to join me.”

The website for the game-day watch along states the livestream is not an official Springbok or South Africa Rugby event.

Erasmus reiterated it is a “personal, not official” event on his social media pages, inviting fans over the age of 18 to join the stream.

The Springboks will face Ireland at 3.40am AEDT on Sunday, November 22.

title: Henry Pollock dropped as England team to face All Blacks is leaked
article_text:
Henry Pollock is set to drop to the bench as Steve Borthwick rings the changes for England’s blockbuster clash with the All Blacks on Saturday.

According to Telegraph Sport, Borthwick is expected to return to the bulk of the starting XV that defeated Australia 45-22 earlier this month.

Will Joseph is the notable exception, retaining his place on the wing following his sensational five-try performance against Japan.

The youngster replaces the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and is in line to win just his third England cap.

Fin Smith is expected to replace George Ford at fly-half, with Jack van Poortvliet making his sixth successive start at scrum-half.

Seb Atkinson and George Furbank have both recovered from injury and are tipped to return at inside centre and full-back respectively.

That means Max Ojomoh and Freddie Steward look set to miss out on starting spots despite impressing against Japan.

Borthwick is seemingly loading his bench with dynamite.

Pollock, Ellis Genge, Luke Cowan-Dickie, George Martin and Greg Fisilau are all expected to be named among the replacements, according to the Telegraph's team news.

Ollie Chessum returns at blindside flanker, with Ben Curry at openside and Ben Earl switching back to number eight.

Fin Baxter, Jamie George and Joe Heyes are expected to form the starting front row.

England will fancy their chances against an All Blacks side battling an injury crisis following their shock defeat to Wales.

Both teams will officially confirm their selections on Thursday.

Likely replacements: Luke Cowan-Dickie, Ellis Genge, George Martin, Henry Pollock and Greg Fisilau.

Asher Opoku-Fordjour and Will Stuart are competing for the replacement tighthead spot.

title: England Grand Slam winner set for Ireland debut this weekend
article_text:
An England Grand Slam winner has been included in Ireland XV's squad for their clash with Fijian Latui this weekend.

Head coach Mark Sexton has named his side for Friday night's fixture in Cork, with a mixture of experienced internationals and emerging players set to feature.

The match, which forms part of a double-header at Virgin Media Park alongside Ireland U20s' meeting with Scotland U20s, offers players an opportunity to showcase their ability in an environment close to the senior international set-up.

One of the biggest names in the squad is former England international Kieran Brookes, who has been selected at tighthead prop.

The 36-year-old is in line to make his first appearance in an Ireland shirt in more than 15 years, having previously represented the country at U18, U19 and U20 level.

Brookes has made an impressive start since joining Munster this summer and qualifies for Ireland through his grandparents, who were born in Belfast and Dublin.

Born in England, Brookes began his professional career with Newcastle Falcons before joining Leicester Tigers in 2011.

He later returned to Newcastle before signing for Northampton Saints in 2015, where he became a regular starter.

A move to Wasps followed in 2018, before he headed to France to join Toulon in 2021. Three years later, he signed for Perpignan to continue his career in the Top 14.

However, his spell in France ended earlier than planned this summer after he agreed to terminate his contract a year early to join Munster.

The move to Limerick has now opened the door to a potential return to international rugby, this time with Ireland.

He also featured in the 2016 Six Nations, returning from injury to play a part in England's Grand Slam-winning campaign.

His final appearance for England came in 2016, meaning he has long since completed World Rugby's three-year stand-down period required to switch international allegiance.

However, until his move to Munster, Brookes had never played his club rugby in Ireland, meaning he did not meet the necessary eligibility requirements.

His arrival at Munster has changed that, giving the experienced prop a route back into international rugby.

At 36, he could provide valuable depth and leadership to Ireland's front row if he makes a successful return to the Test international stage.

There is also a familiar face in the Irish coaching set-up.

Current head coach Andy Farrell was part of Stuart Lancaster's England coaching team during Brookes' international career, meaning the pair have previously worked together at Test level.

Former England international Dan Kelly has been named on the bench, although he has featured for Ireland A in the past, starting against Spain and England A last season.

Ireland XV: 15 Todd Lawlor, 14 Finn Treacy, 13 James Hume, 12 Cathal Forde, 11 Daniel Ryan, 10 Joey Carbery, 9 Fintan Gunne, 1 Alex Usanov, 2 Gus McCarthy (c), 3 Kieran Brookes, 4 Fineen Wycherley, 5 Edwin Edogbo, 6 David McCann, 7 Will Connors, 8 Brian Gleeson.

Replacements: 16 Eoin de Buitléar, 17 Jeremy Loughman, 18 Jack Aungier, 19 Conor O’Tighearnaigh, 20 Paul Boyle, 21 Matthew Devine, 22 Jack Murphy, 23 Dan Kelly.

title: Tonight's rugby news as South African government steps in after World Rugby ban
article_text:
These are your headlines on the evening of Wednesday, November 18.

Rassie Erasmus has received the backing of the South African minister of sport, arts and culture following his six-match ban from World Rugby.

The Springboks head coach has been suspended by the game's governing body following inflammatory remarks he made in a press conference in Dublin on Monday.

His comments centred on the match officials following the defeat to France last week; Erasmus questioned the officiating during the game, suggesting there could have been manipulation of the match after claiming French players had committed 17 knee-drop tackles without intervention from the television match official. He even asked the question: "Is that not match-fixing?"

That led to World Rugby taking swift action and banning the double World Cup winner for the next six matches. He's now requested a full hearing.

Gayton McKenzie has now weighed in on the matter, saying Erasmus "foolishly" said what others were thinking and that he has his "full support".

“@RassieRugby foolishly and openly said what most of us have been saying amongst friends, he is passionate about the game, he has my full support,” McKenzie wrote on X.

“I know he feels that he let us down but maybe just maybe fairness shall return because of his outburst. We love you to the moon and back or should I say six matches and back.”

South Africa said in their request to World Rugby: “SA Rugby is requesting a full misconduct hearing for Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus following his sanctioning by an independent World Rugby panel for comments made in a press conference in Dublin on Monday.

“A SA Rugby spokesperson said that the organisation respected the process but had requested an opportunity for its coach to contextualize his comments and assure the panel that it was not his intention to allege that any match official had acted with ulterior motives.

“SA Rugby trusted that such a hearing could be expedited considering the seriousness of the charge, and will not make any further comment until the hearing could be completed.”

Gareth Thomas admits he has spent the days since Wales' stunning victory over New Zealand watching supporters' reactions on social media, saying the scenes across the country made him "feel like a fan".

The loosehead was at the heart of a remarkable defensive effort as Steve Tandy's side held out for a famous 35-28 victory over the All Blacks in Cardiff, resulting in one of the most remarkable upsets in Welsh rugby history.

When Peter Lakai crossed with 53 minutes on the clock at the Principality Stadium, there was a sense of inevitability about what would follow.

The All Blacks would come and do what they have done so many times in Cardiff and pull away to add another year onto the 73-year undefeated streak against Wales.

One man at the heart of a resilient Welsh defence that ensured no more points were scored was Thomas.

Thomas says "he feels like a fan" after watching Welsh public reaction to the famous win.

"It's a very special feeling. I was sat in bed last night, just watching the videos of reactions in pubs and places around Wales," he said. "I love it how it made everyone feel, what it meant to people.

"I had a message saying how special it made their 92-year-old friend and he's happy to go to the grave now after that. So special to make people feel like that.

"We can't stop watching the reactions because it makes you feel like a fan. I would love to have been a fan watching it, shows what it means to see ex-players with tears in their eyes."

With the Wallabies next up in Cardiff this weekend, Thomas says there is belief within the squad and that "eyes are on" their next opponents.

"There's a lot of belief in this group and we feel that's the sort of performance we can put in," he added. "To get that result will probably put a bit of expectation on us now, but we look forward to carrying that in terms of a performance that we want to live up to

"We are very aware of another big test on Saturday. Eyes are on Australia and we are going full steam into that. Mentally I've been impressed with how quickly we've moved on to this next job and we really want to back it up come Saturday."

Jamie Dobie is relishing the prospect of seeing fellow Glasgow back Josh McKay make his Scotland debut against Japan this weekend.

The New Zealand-born full-back, 29, becomes eligible this week to represent his adopted nation after fulfilling the five-year residency rule.

McKay, a key player for Glasgow since joining in November 2021, has been training with Gregor Townsend’s squad this month in preparation for potential involvement in Saturday’s Nations Championship clash at Murrayfield.

“I think he can add a lot,” said Dobie, who has been a team-mate of McKay’s throughout his time at Warriors. “Everybody’s seen what he’s been capable of in a Glasgow jersey over the last few seasons and since he’s been in Scotland.

“Even just having him around the group, he’s brought a real fresh energy and he’s such a good bloke to have in the squad. The guys at Glasgow have appreciated that for a good few years now.

“It’s great to see him in this environment and being able to add that and everybody knows the threat that he is on the pitch with ball in hand.

title: Newcastle expect big recruitment drive after England breakthrough
article_text:
Calum MacRae admits that Max Hicks’ Nations Championship call-up to the England squad will prove a useful selling point when it comes to selling a move to Newcastle Red Bulls to homegrown talent.

New Zealand-born Hicks, who qualifies to play for England through his Cornish mother, made his England A debut in the 59-24 home win over an Argentina XV in Bath a couple of weeks ago.

The Red Bulls summer signing from Perpignan, who was a second-half replacement in the West Country, was called up for training before last weekend’s win over Japan, and MacRae says it is useful to have examples of what can be achieved when speaking to players.

“It’s ultimately in these situations you need examples of it living and breathing, because it’s easy to say those things, but right from the get-go in the first block, we’ve got players who are in the conversation for international stuff, having just come in.

“So when you’re having those conversations in recruitment, it’s far easier to say what you’ve done rather than what you would like to do, and Max is a great example of that. There are a number of other guys in the conversation.

“Obviously, Ollie Leatherbarrow has been at the club for a period of time, but he has got an international cap with Scotland. Yes, it’s the other side of the border. But ultimately, it does show the quality of the programme that the club are putting together.

“It validates that if you come to Newcastle, not only can you perform and play well for the club, but that’s not a limiting factor if you’ve got aspirations to play international rugby,” said MacRae.

Red Bulls defence coach MacRae, who himself was a summer arrival in the North-East from Benetton, isn’t surprised that Hicks has hit the ground running and so quickly forced his way into Steve Borthwick’s thinking.

“As you’re coming to a new club, you do obviously do a bit of background, and everybody I touched base with spoke very, very highly about him and about his rugby ability.

“You can see he’s a real full-court player, both in attack and defence. He’s shown some brilliant work, ball in hand, soft skills on the offload, but also physically; he’s really shown in the last few weeks that he can impose himself physically. And also, he’s got an engine in some of the scramble efforts and some of the games where we’ve been put under pressure.

“He’s one of those guys that’s like a Duracell bunny that appears in situations where you need him when you’re put under pressure. So I think it’s fully deserved that he’s in the conversation for next-level honours.

“It has come quickly, but I think it’s merited because his performances suggest that he should be in those conversations. And it’s really positive from an England point of view that they’re prepared to actually pick players on form from the domestic competition,” he added.

title: Carlos Alcaraz: Seven-time Grand Slam champion sinks Ben Shelton to reach championship match at ATP Finals
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz made it a lucky 13 wins in a row against Ben Shelton to reach Sunday's showpiece of the ATP Finals in Turin.

Alcaraz, who eased concerns about a hamstring injury by completing an unbeaten group-stage campaign, defeated American third seed Shelton 3-6 6-3 7-6 (7-1) despite heavy strapping on his upper left leg.

The Spaniard was beaten by Jannik Sinner in last year's final in Turin but will be determined to go one better this time around and claim his first year-end title. He will face either Alexander Zverev or Daniil Medvedev in Sunday's championship match.

title: Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton’s ranking points & prize money after ATP Finals semi-final
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz prevailed in a deciding set tiebreak to defeat Ben Shelton in a pulsating semi-final at the 2026 ATP Finals.

World No 3 Alcaraz fought back to earn a 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1) victory over fourth-ranked Shelton in the last four at the Inalpi Arena in Turin.

The Spanish star produced a stunning level to seal the win as he dominated the third set tiebreak by winning the last seven points of the match.

Alcaraz, who is chasing his maiden ATP Finals title, is through to his second final at the season-ending championships, having lost to Jannik Sinner in last year’s title match.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion dismantled Frances Tiafoe, Daniil Medvedev and Flavio Cobolli in the round robin stage in Turin, and he has extended his overall winning streak to 13 matches.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Shelton was playing his first semi-final at the ATP Finals in what was his second appearance at the prestigious indoor hard-court event after he made his debut in 2025.

The American progressed to the last four after winning two of his three matches in the group stage.

Alcaraz has earned 400 ATP ranking points for his semi-final win against Shelton, having already collected 600 points for his three round robin wins.

Shelton defeated Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar in his first and third matches in the John McEnroe Group either side of a loss to Alexander Zverev.

The US Open finalist secured 400 ranking points for his two victories in Turin.

Alcaraz has collected a $2,759,000 for his unbeaten run to the final in Turin, and he could take his prize money haul to $5,171,000 if he lifts the trophy.

Shelton has earned $1,148,000 for his campaign at the ATP Finals.

title: Men’s tennis is changing in 2028. From money to the calendar, here’s what to know
Arevalo/Pavic reach title match at Nitto ATP Finals
Lakshya Sen's title hat-trick bid ends as Satwik-Chirag also crash out, India draw blank at Hong Kong Ope
article_text:
suffered straight-game defeats in their respective semifinals.

Lakshya's bid for a third consecutive title was halted by Denmark's Anders Antonsen, who produced a commanding 21-13, 21-13 victory. Earlier, Satwik and Chirag, the world No. 6 pair, went down 18-21, 19-21 against Malaysia's eighth-seeded combination of Man Wei Chong and Tee Kai Wun.

The defeats meant India finished the tournament without a finalist, despite Lakshya arriving in Hong Kong on the back of consecutive titles at the Hylo Open and Kumamoto Masters Japan over the last two weeks.

Satwik and Chirag began their semifinal with a 4-1 head-to-head advantage over Man and Tee, but the Malaysians proved more effective in the crucial moments.

The Indians made an encouraging start, racing to a 3-0 lead, before their opponents fought back in an attacking contest featuring sharp returns, angled shots and powerful smashes.

The scores remained close through the opening exchanges, but Man and Tee edged ahead 11-10 at the interval.

Tee then raised his intensity as the Malaysians opened up a 16-12 lead.

Satwik and Chirag fought back from 16-19 to level at 19-19 in the second game after trailing 15-18, but the Malaysians held their nerve. They targeted Chirag to earn match point before sealing the contest with a precise push into the corner.

The defeat ended another impressive season for the Indian pair, who had won titles in Singapore and China this year.

Lakshya, meanwhile, struggled to find his rhythm against Antonsen, who controlled the rallies with accurate placement and clever angles.

The Danish shuttler established an early 3-0 lead before Lakshya fought back to make it 8-8. However, Antonsen moved ahead at the interval and gradually took control, closing out the opening game 21-13.

The second game followed a similar pattern. Antonsen moved ahead 5-2 after the change of ends and carried an 11-6 advantage into the interval.

Lakshya produced occasional moments of resistance but remained inconsistent, allowing Antonsen to extend his lead to 18-9. The Dane eventually converted his third match point to complete a comfortable victory.

Lakshya's movement and reactions appeared a fraction slower, with the accumulated workload of his recent title-winning run possibly catching up with him.

title: Hong Kong Open 2026 badminton: Lakshya Sen's 13-match winning streak ends in semi-finals
Hong Kong Open: ‘We Will Come Back Stronger’
article_text:
Goh Soon Huat and Lai Shevon Jemie came to LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 needing a miracle – and very nearly pulled it off.

Having suffered three first-round exits in their previous four tournaments, the Malaysian husband-and-wife duo hauled themselves off the canvas and back into the race for the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2026 with a gritty semifinal run. Standing between them and the final ticket to Hangzhou next month were top seeds Feng Yan Zhe and Huang Dong Ping.

On Saturday, Goh and Lai pushed the Chinese powerhouse to the brink before falling 21-17 21-18 – a result that officially wrapped up the mixed doubles qualification race and handed the last berth to Japanese pair Yuta Watanabe/Maya Taguchi.

Yet, despite the heartbreak of falling short of a season-finale appearance, there were no hung heads in the mixed zone. Instead, there was a quiet, hard-earned relief their spark had returned.

“It wasn’t a perfect match but both of us gave the best we had,” said Lai. “Coming in from quite a rollercoaster of results and performances, today was one of our steadier matches. Although we didn’t manage to get the win, we did quite well.”

They certainly made Feng and Huang sweat, clawing back in the second game to snatch a 16-15 lead before the world No.1s slammed the door shut.

“Against the Chinese pairs, even if you lead by quite a few points, it’s still not much of an advantage because they have the ability to catch right back up,” Lai admitted.

Goh echoed that sentiment, confessing that the weight of the occasion briefly got the better of his footwork. “At the start, I quite enjoyed the match. But once we reached a more crucial point, I began to put more pressure on myself and lost my pacing – my speed got too fast and broke my rhythm.”

Still, as their 2026 campaign ends, the detour to Hong Kong proved invaluable.

“The good thing is we have regained our momentum, our rhythm and most importantly, our confidence,” Goh noted.

For Lai, who openly admitted she had been battling self-doubt, the semifinal run was the exact validation she needed.

“I can see the results of my training showing up on court this time,” she said. “That has given me a good push to know I’m heading in the right direction.”

Hangzhou will have to wait, then – but with their mojo firmly back in their kit bags, Goh and Lai are already looking forward to what 2027 brings.

title: 2026 WTA Rankings Winners & Losers: Elena Rybakina +4, Iga Swiatek -7, Alex Eala +38, Emma Raducanu -79
article_text:
The 2026 WTA Tour season has wrapped up and there is a new No 1 as Elena Rybakina finished at the top of a different-looking top-20 in the WTA Rankings compared to the start of the year.

Rybakina started the 2026 campaign at No 5 in the rankings, but she took over at No 1 after the US Open in September and confirmed her position as year-end No 1 during the Asian swing, bringing an end to Aryna Sabalenka’s long reign.

And there is also a new No 2 with teenager Mirra Andreeva finishing at a career-high on the back of her French Open and WTA Finals titles this year, up from No 9 last year.

Sabalenka – who started the year at No 1 and spent 99 consecutive weeks at the top – finishes at No 3.

The Sabalenka-Iga Swiatek days of dominance ended this year as the latter was No 2 on January 1, but she slipped to No 9 with neither winning a Grand Slam in 2026 although the Belarusian finished runner-up to Rybakina at the Australian Open and US Open.

Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula are still firmly part of the top 10, but the likes of Madison Keys (-12), Amanda Anisimova and Jasmine Paolini (-27) have dropped off.

Elina Svitolina (+8), Linda Noskova (+6), Karolina Muchova (+11) and Marta Kostyuk (+16) have moved into the top 10.

In terms of those who finished between No 11 and No 20 in 2026, Maja Chwalinska was at No 150 on 1 January and finds herself 138 places higher at No 12 with her rise coming on the back of her runners-up finish at Roland Garros and her maiden WTA 1000 title at the Wuhan Open.

No 13 Iva Jovic is +22 thanks to a run to the quarter-finals at the Australian Open and the successful defence of her WTA 500 trophy at the Guadalajara Open.

Fellow rising star Alex Eala sits two places behind the American as she climbed 38 places from No 53 with her jump coming on the back of her maiden WTA Tour title at the WTA 500 Washington DC Open while she also finished runner-up at the Hong Kong WTA 250 event.

Sorana Cirstea is up from No 43 to No 16 as she finished her final year as a professional with the Transylvania Open title and a quarter-final appearance at Roland Garros.

*Although the WTA Tour season is over, there are still a few WTA 125K and ITF events taking place, but no one in the top 20 will feature so the above top 20 will remain unchanged, while there could be one or two changes lower down the list.

Kristina Liutova started the 2025 season at No 714, but the 16-year-old surged up the rankings on the back of her maiden title at the Memphis Classic as she became the second youngest player to win a WTA Tour title on debut.

The Russian teenager is currently at No 103, 611 places better off than on 1 January.

Sara Bejlek, Lilli Tagger, Diane Parry, Claire Liu and Hariet Dart also won their maiden titles this year and also earned big jumps.

Czech Bejlek sits at No 33, having started the year at No 92, Parry is one place behind her after surging 90 spots from No 124, Tagger won her maiden title at the age of 18 and she rose from No 159 to No 54, while Liu is +140 from No 207 to No 67 and Dart is +87 from No 172 to No 85.

Dart is currently the British No 3 behind Katie Boulter – who started 2026 at No 106, but is currently No 50 – and Sonay Kartal (No 68 to No 54).

Former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin’s struggles continued in 2026 as she started at No 28, but has dropped 161 places to no 189.

Emma Raducanu finished the 2025 season as the British No 1 as she was No 29 and she reached No 23 in March, but injury ruined her year as she didn’t play any matches during the second half of the campaign and has slumped 79 places to No 108.

title: Iga Swiatek makes huge schedule change as first event of 2027 season confirmed
article_text:
Iga Swiatek will not line up at the 2027 United Cup as she has opted not to compete at the annual team tournament for the first time since its launch, instead signing up for a regular WTA Tour event.

Since the inaugural United Cup in 2023, Swiatek has been an ever-present member of Team Poland and steered them to back-to-back runners-up titles in 2024 and 2025 before they finally got their hands on the coveted winner’s trophy last year.

But the six-time Grand Slam winner won’t be part of Poland’s title defence in January 2027 as she has decided to swap the team environment for the individual competition of the Tour by entering the Brisbane International.

Swiatek will make her debut at the WTA 500 event that will also feature world No 1 Elena Rybakina – who won the title in 2024 – and four-time Grand Slam winner Naomi Osaka.

Aryna Sabalenka won the tournament the past two years, but organisers are yet to confirm if she will return to seek a third consecutive trophy at the season opener.

For Swiatek, it is certainly a big shift in her calendar following a disappointing 2026 season that saw her fail to win a Grand Slam for the first time since 2021. Her best run at the majors was at the Australian Open where she reached the quarter-finals.

Although she won two titles – the United Cup and the Canadian Open – she finished a disappointing ninth in the WTA Rankings, having started the year at No 2 behind Sabalenka, as she failed to qualify for the season-ending WTA Finals in Indian Wells.

The last time the former world No 1 finished that lowly was back in 2021.

There is no doubt that she and her team, with coach Francisco Roig leading the way, hopes this change will lead to a better 2027 season, especially with several high-quality opponents set to test her in Brisbane ahead of the first Grand Slam of the year.

Before signing up for the United Cup, Swiatek competed at the 2022 Adelaide International and reached the semi-final before losing against then world No 1 Ashleigh Barty. That, though, gave her confidence ahead of the Australian Open as she also reached the last four in Melbourne, but lost against Danielle Collins.

In 2021, she started at the Gippsland Trophy and made it to the quarter-finals, while in 2020 and 2019 she kicked off her season at the Australian Open.

Andy Murray: Great Britain's outgoing Davis Cup captain Leon Smith hopes Scot will one day take the role
article_text:
Great Britain's outgoing Davis Cup captain Leon Smith hopes "standout candidate" Andy Murray will one day take the role he is vacating after more than 16 years.

Smith took over from John Lloyd in 2010 following a humiliating loss to Lithuania that left Britain facing relegation to the bottom level of the historic competition.

Harnessing the talents and commitment of Murray, who he coached as a junior, Smith led Britain back to the top tier and, only five years later, to a first title since 1936 when they defeated Belgium in 2015.

Murray won all 11 singles and doubles rubbers he contested in 2015, as well as 33 out of 36 in singles in the competition overall.

The 39-year-old, who is currently head coach to Jack Draper, paid tribute to Smith, saying: "Winning the Davis Cup in 2015 with Leon as captain was one of the proudest moments of my career.

"He did a great job of bringing everyone together and making sure we all felt we had a part to play.

"I've obviously known Leon a long time, since he coached me as a kid. I think the most fun we had together was when I was playing Davis Cup and Leon was on the bench.

"I wish Leon all the best as he steps down, and good luck to the new captain."

Smith, whose final tournament will be next week's Finals in Bologna, where Great Britain face Germany in the quarter-finals, hopes Murray will one day take the role.

"I think it is timing for him, he's busy with his life," Smith said. "He obviously is the standout candidate, isn't he? For all the attributes and more.

"Hopefully it's something he's interested in the future.

"The Davis Cup, it's not just the ties itself. It's being at the events. It's supporting the players and their personal coaches on their journeys.

"And it's also the Olympics and his history in the Olympics is second to none.

"So I do hope it's something he does in the future, but I respect that it's not for him right now, and I can understand it.

"But I really hope at some point in the future that he does take it on."

Speaking on Sky Sports Tennis, Andy's older brother Jamie discussed the role with Gigi Salmon and Tim Henman.

The seven-time Grand Slam doubles champion said: "I think that's an interesting way to see how they're going to go about it. I think there's probably quite a few people that would quite fancy it.

"I think Greg [Rusedski] as well, with everything that he's done in his career, would definitely deserve to be in that conversation.

"I'm sure Andy will get asked about his interest levels. He certainly should be given everything that he's done for tennis in our country."

Henman reflected on Smith's tenure by saying: "A big part of that role was making sure that Andy turned up to play and then giving him the environment to go out and perform as well as he could.

"Andy at that time was loving playing Davis Cup, representing his country and the team went from strength to strength.

"When Leon started, they were at the bottom of professional tennis, but they worked their way up to lifting the trophy in Belgium."

title: Wang Zhiyi and Tomoka Miyazaki vie for Hong Kong Open title without Ahn
article_text:
A showdown between the top players from China and Japan will decide who takes the crown at the Hong Kong Open, with badminton world No. 1 Ahn Se-young (24, Samsung Life Insurance) absent.

World No. 3 Wang Zhiyi and No. 7 Tomoka Miyazaki will meet in the Hong Kong Open semifinals. Both are set for a must-win battle as they pursue a place in the final and the title.

Wang Zhiyi and Miyazaki both won their women's singles quarterfinals on the 20th at the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Hong Kong Open (Super 500) at Kai Tak Arena in Hong Kong, securing places in the semifinals.

Wang Zhiyi was first to reach the semifinals after a hard-fought match. She beat Indonesia's Putri Kusuma Wardani, ranked No. 9 in the world, 2-0 (22-20, 22-20). Both games went to deuce at 20-20, but Wang stayed focused at the decisive moments and closed out the match with consecutive points.

The win was also significant because Wang was the last Chinese woman left in the singles draw. Tokyo Olympic gold medalist Chen Yufei, ranked No. 4 in the world, lost to India's Santoshi Ramraj, while Han Yue and Su Wenjing were also eliminated. Wang was the only Chinese player left, preserving her country's pride.

Miyazaki also secured a semifinal berth with a dominant performance. She routed fellow Japanese player Hina Akechi, ranked No. 14 in the world, 2-0 (21-11, 21-9). After coming back from an early deficit in the first game, she extended her lead with a run of points. She then put Akechi under pressure from the start of the second game and won comfortably.

The victory also served as revenge for Miyazaki. She put behind her a painful 2-1 comeback loss to Akechi in the Korea Open quarterfinals on the 6th in Yeosu, South Jeolla province.

The two players will now face off for a place in the final. Wang remains China's only hope in women's singles, while Miyazaki has an opportunity to prove herself as the next ace of Japanese women's badminton.

The title race has become more competitive with world No. 1 Ahn Se-young (Samsung Life Insurance), No. 2 Akane Yamaguchi of Japan and No. 5 Pusarla Venkata Sindhu of India all absent from the tournament. With the dominant favorite out, Wang and Miyazaki have emerged as title contenders.

Wang has shown her determination to reclaim the title, surviving to the semifinals as the only Chinese player left in the tournament. Miyazaki has already secured a spot in the 2026 BWF World Tour Finals and is determined to keep her momentum going with a title win ahead of the season-ending event.

If both players win their semifinals, they will advance to the final, where they will be just one match away from the title. With Ahn absent from the Hong Kong Open, attention is focused on whether China's Wang will challenge for the title or Japan's Miyazaki will emerge as the new queen.

title: Alcaraz puts aside injury concerns to take apart Cobolli
article_text:
A ruthless Carlos Alcaraz put aside his injury concerns to dismantle Flavio Cobolli and ensure a perfect record in the ATP Finals group stages.

Spain's Alcaraz hurt his left hamstring in his previous match against Daniil Medvedev and had a scan on the injury on Thursday.

He arrived for his match against Cobolli with strapping on his upper-left leg - as well as tape on his right knee and a sleeve on his right arm - but was brutally efficient in a 6-4 6-1 win.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion did not face a break point and bludgeoned 29 winners in a 65-minute victory.

"I tried not to move that much. I tried to be aggressive, to dominate the match as much as I can," the 23-year-old said.

"I'm just really happy that I am getting more confident, the way I'm hitting the ball and seeing what's going on in the match.

"The challenge now is not on the court, it's off the court, to do whatever it takes to be in a good shape and feel physically ready for a battle tomorrow."

Alcaraz is now on a 12-match winning streak and will face Ben Shelton, who he beat in the Paris Masters final last month, in Saturday's semi-finals.

The winner of Friday's last match between Medvedev and Frances Tiafoe will face Alexander Zverev in the other semi-final.

Alcaraz was conservative in his movement, trying to avoid sliding in and out of the corners - but rather than diminishing his game, it allowed him to produce some astonishing shot-making.

Cobolli never looked as though he had the belief that he could challenge Alcaraz, and was broken in the first game of the match by a thumping return winner.

Alcaraz kept the points short, hammering his forehand and backhand to all corners, and targeted Cobolli's second serve in particular.

An astonishing whipped 110mph forehand winner was the highlight of the first set, which Alcaraz wrapped up with a strong service hold.

Cobolli again lost his serve in the opening game of the second set and Alcaraz claimed five of the final six games to secure victory.

After converting match point with another return winner, Alcaraz embraced Cobolli at the net and offered the crushed Italian a few words of support.

Alcaraz has not had his serve broken once in his three group matches as he bids for a first title at the season-ending event.

He and world number one Zverev have both made it through the group stages without dropping a set, while Alcaraz has not lost more than four games in a set.

In the doubles, Britain's Neal Skupski and American partner Christian Harrison reached the semi-finals with a 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 victory over Marcel Granollers and Horacio Zeballos.

The US Open champions will face fourth seeds Marcelo Arevalo and Mate Pavic for a place in Sunday's final.

title: Disappointing early exit for top seed Julien Carraggi
article_text:
It was a disappointing start to the Scottish Open for Belgium's Julien Carraggi, who entered this week's International Challenge tournament as the top seed but suffered a first-round defeat.

The charismatic Belgian was hoping for a strong run in Scotland, but his campaign came to an early end against South Korea's Hyeon Woo Cho, ranked world number 117.

Cho secured the victory in straight games, winning 21-13, 24-22, despite a much closer battle in the second game.

The result brings Carraggi's Scottish Open campaign to an end after just one match, while Cho continues his impressive form on the European circuit.

The Korean arrived in Scotland following an impressive performance at last week's Irish Open, where he reached the men's singles final.

title: ATP increases player compensation to $350m & delays doubles cuts decision
article_text:
The men's ATP Tour is promising its players rewards of at least $350m in 2028 - but the board has delayed a decision on hotly disputed changes to doubles until next month.

The bonus pool will increase from the current $21.5m to $50m in 2028, with payments offered to players ranked in the world's top 30 at the start of each Masters 1000 event.

The world number one will receive the highest bonus of $2m for each of the Masters events they play.

A total of $25m will also be shared out between the world's top 250 players at the end of each season, with the goal for everyone to receive $100,000.

That would make a significant difference to the finances of lower-ranked players.

Players will also no longer be penalised so directly for missing tournaments through injury.

World number two Jannik Sinner, for example, won five Masters events in a row between March and May, but may only qualify for 25% of his bonus as he has not been able to play since Wimbledon.

Proposed changes to the doubles - which includes halving draw sizes and reducing the percentage of prize money from 20% to 10% - have received fierce opposition from the players.

In October, more than 150 men's doubles players wrote an open letter to the ATP Tour urging them to reconsider "drastic" changes to the format.

Chairman Andrea Gaudenzi told BBC Sport the governing body of men's tennis needed "a bit more time to reach consensus".

"I hope we find the right balance between the players' and the tournaments' demands, and I truly hope we reach a compromise."

The proposals will now be voted on next month.

Doubles players have said the changes would make it "effectively impossible" for anyone outside the top 30 to make a living from the sport.

There may be a hint of compromise in the air, but Gaudenzi still believes at least some of the doubles money needs to be redirected towards singles players.

"It's impossible to make everyone happy. It's something we do not take lightly, but we also cannot ignore the fans and the broadcasters - [just] like any entertainment business," he said.

"Whether you are a musician or an actor, it needs to be rewarded as a function of the entertainment you provide to the fans."

Gaudenzi told Britain's Henry Patten, who was unhappy he and CEO Eno Polo were not present when Patten and Harri Heliovaara received the year-end number one trophy, that he had no intention of undermining their achievement.

"I understand his disappointment and he's obviously also driven by what we are discussing, and I do understand it's quite emotional their side," Gaudenzi added.

"But I was here in the hotel together with Eno - we were actually fighting and negotiating twelve hours a day to get this deal done - so we were really in the trenches all day long."

The ATP Board has also approved the formation of ATP Ventures, which will bring all the Tour's media, data and central sponsorship rights under the same roof. This could improve the chances of the ATP and the WTA agreeing to pool their resources and create a 'Tennis Ventures'.

Probably the trickiest issue to resolve is the length of the season - there are just 33 days between this year's Davis Cup Finals and the start of the 2027 season in Australia.

The ATP schedule for 2028 is likely to be released in late January, but Gaudenzi warned not to expect "big changes".

"That's going to be difficult," Gaudenzi added.

"The off-season, I think, will improve, but ultimately it will take time.

"But we have a plan, we have shared that plan conceptually with the players and I think it will take a few years to execute, but we are going in the right direction.

"Don't expect big changes regarding the off-season in 2028. They are a work in progress."

title: How sustainability is shaping the Nitto ATP Finals
article_text:
The Nitto ATP Finals is about more than just the on-court action.

As well as bringing together the world's best players for the prestigious year-end tournament, the event provides an opportunity to make a positive impact beyond tennis, with sustainability and community engagement central to its wider ambitions.

At the 2026 edition in Turin, title partner Nitto is continuing its work with the ATP, the Italian Tennis and Padel Federation (FITP) and the City of Turin through the Torino Green Project, while introducing new measures to reduce the tournament's environmental footprint.

For this year's event, a hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO) fuel blend is being used in the on-site generators in place of conventional diesel. The generators accounted for 36 per cent of the tournament's emissions in 2025, making this an important step towards the event's goal of reducing carbon emissions by 30 per cent by 2030, compared with 2024 levels. Nitto is supporting that ambition through a five-year commitment.

The initiative builds on the Torino Green Project, launched in 2023 by Nitto, FITP, the City of Turin and the ATP. Its first projects included planting 50 trees near the arena, installing green roofs on selected bus stops and donating €100,000 to the city.

The project has continued to evolve. In 2024, a living Green Wall was installed in the Fan Village and later relocated elsewhere in Turin. In 2025, a Green Art Wall, created using air-purifying Airlite paint, was installed at Leone Sinigaglia primary school.

Other measures supporting the tournament's sustainability efforts include electricity from 100 per cent renewable sources, an electrified Lexus fleet for player and staff transport, discounted Frecciarossa train tickets for fans and free travel on selected tram lines for ticket holders.

Sustainability is also reflected in the tournament's community work. Children and families supported by Turin charity U.G.I. ODV are invited to attend matches, while children have the opportunity to walk on court alongside players as mascots. The Nitto ATP Finals Innovation Summit also brings together representatives from the City of Turin, academia and industry to discuss sustainability challenges.

The tournament's environmental progress is measured by FITP, with support from Enovation Consulting, through carbon-footprint assessments and an annual ESG report. The 2025 edition was also certified to the ISO 20121:2024 sustainable event management standard by Bureau Veritas.

With Nitto's title partnership running through 2030, the host city will continue working with its partners and the to make progress towards its emissions-reduction goal.

title: Zi Yu-Noraqilah reach first Super 500 semi-final in World Tour
article_text:
KUALA LUMPUR: Women's pair Low Zi Yu-Noraqilah Maisarah Ramdan celebrated a major milestone after reaching their first Super 500 semi-final at the Hong Kong Open on Friday.

The world No. 41 upset American world No. 25 Francesca Corbett-Jennie Gai 21-19, 16-21, 21-16 in the quarter-finals at the Kai Tak Arena.

The victory came a day after Zi Yu-Noraqilah upset Taiwan's world No. 6 Hsu Yin Hui-Lin Jhih Yun 21-19, 21-18 in the second round.

"I'm very happy because this is our first Super 500 semi-final," said Zi Yu.

Noraqilah felt the pair had produced their best performance of the week against the Americans.

"I think today we played quite well compared with the two previous matches," she said.

Their creditable run has come despite Noraqilah still working her way back to full fitness following a left ankle injury.

The 19-year-old, who withdrew from last week's Kumamoto Masters, said she was currently at 70 per cent fitness.

Noraqilah said preparation for the Hong Kong Open had been demanding, with Zi Yu returning from junior tournament commitments while she was recovering from injury.

They will face either seniors Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah or another American pair, Lauren Lam-Allison Lee, for a place in the final.

title: Carlos Alcaraz injury update: Spaniard cancels ATP Finals warmup before Flavio Cobolli match
article_text:

World No 3 Alcaraz sustained a left hamstring injury during his 6-2, 6-4 victory over Daniil Medvedev on Wednesday afternoon in Turin.

Early in the second set of the match, Alcaraz took a medical timeout and had his left thigh area strapped.

In his post-match press conference, Alcaraz confirmed he had felt a “little problem” in his hamstring.

“Well, I feel it a little bit. I’m not gonna lie,” said the 23-year-old.

“But unfortunately I was, you know, I was playing great, and suddenly, I felt a little problem of my hamstring.”
