title: GB's Davis Cup-winning captain ends 17-year stint
article_text:
Great Britain's Davis Cup-winning captain Leon Smith says it is the "right time" for a change after announcing he will end his 17-year stint in the role.

Smith guided the British men's team to Davis Cup victory in 2015 - the nation's first win in the event since 1936.

The 50-year-old Scot said he had been mulling over his future for "most of this year" before deciding to step down after next week's Finals in Bologna.

Smith's successor has not yet been appointed, but the Lawn Tennis Association (LTA) has spoken to potential candidates and hopes to announce the new captain as soon as possible.

Former world number one Andy Murray, who was instrumental in Britain's 2015 triumph, is not believed to be interested in the role at this time.

"There comes a time whether it is personally you need a change, or it is good for the team to have something else," said Smith, who seemed emotional in a video call with reporters.

"I've done it for a very long time and I think there are others who will enjoy the role and can bring something different to the role."

"I love the role and haven't lost any passion for it. But it feels like the right time for me personally and the guys moving forwards."

With Smith picking the team and creating a tight bond between the group, Murray was the driving force on the court as he won all eight of his singles matches in the victorious campaign.

Murray was coached by Smith as a child and said winning the Davis Cup together was "one of the proudest moments" of his career.

"He did a great job of bringing everyone together and making sure we all felt we had a part to play. He got the best out of us that year," three-time Grand Slam champion Murray said.

"I've obviously known Leon a long time, I think the most fun we had together was when I was playing Davis Cup and Leon was on the bench. I'm really glad we got to share those moments.

"I wish Leon all the best as he steps down, and good luck to the new captain."

Smith, who will continue in his role as head of British men's tennis, took over in 2010 with the team in danger of being relegated to the lowest tier of the Davis Cup.

Within three years they were back in the top tier and just two years later Murray inspired them to the trophy.

Smith also guided the team to the semi-finals in 2016 and 2019.

While he can no longer rely on a superstar of Murray's ilk, Smith is hoping this year's crop can ensure his captaincy ends on another high.

Britain will rely on Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery and former world number eight Cameron Norrie in the singles, with world number one Henry Patten and three-time major champion Neal Skupski pairing up in the doubles.

Smith's side faces Germany - led by singles world number one Alexander Zverev - in the last eight on Thursday.

"I'm focused and really looking forward to captaining Great Britain for one more week in Bologna next week and hopefully creating a few more special memories together," Smith added.

Smith has won 70% of his ties since taking over as captain in the summer of 2010.

The venues and the crowds for many of the early ties were on the low side, until Britain moved through the divisions and Andy Murray returned to the team.

The travelling support surged, and the team celebrated their return to the World Group with a stunning win over the United States in a baseball stadium in San Diego in January 2014.

Less than two years later the Davis Cup was back in Britain as thrilling wins in Glasgow and the Queen's Club were followed by Murray's famous lob to seal victory over Belgium.

Great attention to detail has contributed to Britain's success; and far more often than not, Smith got the marginal selection calls right.

He will be an extremely hard act to follow, but will inevitably work closely with his successor given his ongoing role as the head of men's tennis.

title: Leon Smith: Great Britain's Davis Cup-winning captain stepping down after 17 years
article_text:
Great Britain's Davis Cup-winning captain Leon Smith says it is the "right time" for a change after announcing he will end his 17-year stint in the role.

Smith guided the British men's team to Davis Cup victory in 2015 - the nation's first win in the event since 1936.

The 50-year-old Scot said he had been mulling over his future for "most of this year" before deciding to step down after next week's Finals in Bologna.

Smith's successor has not yet been appointed, but the Lawn Tennis Association (LTA) has spoken to potential candidates and hopes to announce the new captain as soon as possible.

Former world number one Andy Murray, who was instrumental in Britain's 2015 triumph, is not believed to be interested in the role at this time.

"There comes a time whether it is personally you need a change, or it is good for the team to have something else," said Smith, who seemed emotional in a video call with reporters.

"I've done it for a very long time and I think there are others who will enjoy the role and can bring something different to the role."

"I love the role and haven't lost any passion for it. But it feels like the right time for me personally and the guys moving forwards."

With Smith picking the team and creating a tight bond between the group, Murray was the driving force on the court as he won all eight of his singles matches in the victorious campaign.

Murray was coached by Smith as a child and said winning the Davis Cup together was "one of the proudest moments" of his career.

title: Hong Kong Open: Evergreen Intanon Books Record Trip
article_text:
Ratchanok Intanon punched her ticket to the season finale for a women’s singles record 11th time after beating Michelle Li 21-19 21-16 in the LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 quarterfinals on Friday.

Needing a victory to secure the ranking points required for next month’s HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2026 in Hangzhou, the Thai star showed trademark composure to reach her first Hong Kong Open semifinal since finishing runner-up to Chen Yu Fei in 2019.

“I felt like she had some pain or some injury,” Intanon said of Li. “Still, I tried not to think about anything outside the court and just focus on the game. I had to stay calm on every shot because I felt she was slower than me, though her hands were still better than mine on some shots.”

For Intanon, the milestone is a testament to resilience following her own injury battles.

“First of all, I want to thank myself because I never give up through injuries,” she reflected. “Coming back takes time and I’ve tried to take it slowly and manage it with my coach. Even here, I’m still not 100 per cent, so I just wanted to do what I could in the moment.”

Next up is an all-Thai semifinal against compatriot Pornpawee Chochuwong, who defeated Rakshitha Sree Santhosh Ramraj by the exact same scoreline moments later. Chochuwong also clinched the final women’s singles berth for Hangzhou after her sole rival, Putri Kusuma Wardani, fell 22-20 22-20 to Wang Zhi Yi.

Despite making 10 prior appearances at the season finale, a title has remained elusive for Intanon.

Her first appearance back in 2012 – at the Super Series Finals – saw her reach the last four, where she lost to Wang Shi Xian.

“I’ve played so many times now. I’m always very grateful and though I’ve never won it, every time I go I hope to at least make that semifinal mark,” she said. “I’m going to take care of my body after this tournament and try to get stronger.”

Asked if she is setting a bigger target this year, her answer was simple: “Winning.”

Amallia Cahaya Pratiwi/Siti Fadia Silva Ramadhanti completed their remarkable rise by claiming a women’spot at the Finals, beating top seeds Yuki Fukushima/Mayu Matsumoto 21-16 21-15.

Languishing in 23rd position just last month, the Indonesians, who only paired up this year, surged into the women’s doubles top eight off the back of a HYLO Open title, deep runs at the French Open and Kumamoto Masters and Friday’s upset. Minutes later, Americans Lauren Lam/Allison Lee’s 21-18 21-11 defeat to Pearly Tan/Thinaah Muralitharan officially sealed Hangzhou berths for both Pratiwi/Ramadhanti and Bulgarian sisters Gabriela Stoeva/Stefani Stoeva.

Pratiwi put their qualification into perspective: “Opportunities truly come from anywhere; we didn’t expect to make it this far.”

Ramadhanti added: “Going through a difficult period and missing out on the Asian Games really served as a wake-up call for us.”

title: Arthur Fils & Rafael Jodar’s ATP Finals ranking points & prize money after round robin exits
article_text:
Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar have both been eliminated from the 2026 ATP Finals, but how many ranking points and how much prize money did they earn?

Jodar had to beat Ben Shelton on Thursday to keep his hopes of progressing to the semi-finals alive, but his 7-6(8), 7-5 defeat to the American meant he finished bottom of the John McEnroe Group.

The Spanish star’s loss to Shelton saw him finish with a 0-3 record after he was beaten by Alexander Zverev and Arthur Fils in his first two matches.

After Shelton’s victory over Jodar, Fils required a straight-set win over Zverev in the final match in the John McEnroe Group on Thursday evening to qualify for the last four.

However, Fils was eliminated as he suffered a 6-4, 7-6(4) defeat to the world No 1.

The Frenchman lost to Shelton in his opening match before defeating Jodar in his second.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Both Jodar and Fils were making their debuts at the ATP Finals.

Zverev won the John McEnroe Group with a 3-0 record, while Shelton finished in second place after winning two of his three matches.

Fils collected 200 ATP ranking points for his round robin win against Jodar. He has overtaken Flavio Cobolli to climb to a projected new career-high position of world No 6 in the ATP Live Rankings.

Jodar, meanwhile, did not add to his points tally after losing all three of his matches in Turin. He remains 10th in the rankings.

Both Fils and Jodar earned a participation fee of $338,000 for playing all of their round robin matches.

Fils earned an additional $405,000 for his victory.

title: BWF World Senior Circuit Hosting Opportunity – 2027
article_text:
Building on the initial circuit tournaments in 2026, and after consultation with key stakeholders, the BWF has confirmed a framework for the BWF World Senior Circuit and welcomes applications from interested Member Associations to host tournaments in 2027.

The establishment of the World Senior Circuit is a key strategic opportunity to engage senior players on a global level to continue to play badminton and to invest in a circuit of sustainable tournaments which culminate in the BWF World Senior Championships as the pinnacle senior badminton tournament.

The following summarises the established framework and application process.

- As a standalone World Senior Circuit tournament or as a joint Continental Confederation Senior Circuit and BWF Senior Circuit tournament.

- The BWF to sanction/confirm World Senior Circuit tournaments.

- Host responsible for delivery of tournament and related costs.

Same as World Senior Championships starting with 35+ up to 75+ with host option to hold more categories (e.g. 80+).

Additional strength categories can be offered (e.g. recreational or a “waterfall” tournament); however, the elite category only counts for the World Senior Ranking.

Player Age Eligibility: Players must fulfil the age requirement before 1 January of the year of the tournament.

- Manual entry process to start (or tournament-specific online entry if applicable).

- Entry fees can be charged to ensure operational sustainability.

- Maximum three events per player (per age group or across varying age groups).

- Group > Knockout if entry size requires (group only if entry size requires) following, where applicable, BWF General Competition Regulations (GCR).

Scoring System: Best of three games to 15 points.

Length of competition up to host based on entry size and other local factors, with last day (finals) on Sunday.

- Prospectus Publication: At least 120 days in advance of tournament.

- Entry deadline: Four weeks in advance of tournament.

- Draws: One week in advance of tournament.

- Based on World Senior Ranking, where applicable, following GCR.

- Substitutions: Allowed for doubles events only, as per BWF World Senior Championships regulations.

- Minimum national level but Continental Level recommended.

- Minimum national level but Continental Level recommended.

- Line Judges: Recruited and provided by host.

Transportation Services: Determined by host, based on entry fees charged.

Accommodation: Determined by host, but at minimum, host to provide list of hotel options for individual player bookings.

Visa Support: Hosting MA to provide visa support letter / other documentation as required.

- Tournament doctor / nurse / paramedics for field of play.

- Medical care for players provided back of house as needed but can be charged to players.

Practice: Where feasible, provide access to competition courts (and practice court(s), if available), but not required.

A set of formalised regulations will be confirmed and published based on the above framework in due course.

The BWF is accepting applications from Member Associations to host World Senior Circuit tournaments in 2027 (with the option to confirm continued hosting in 2028) through submission of a Sanction Request by 31 December 2026 via the following form.

Please note that for 2027 tournaments, the earliest hosting opportunity would be March 2027.

The BWF to confirm hosts by January 2027 and establish a calendar of tournaments.

The BWF to provide further guidance to hosting Member Associations in January or February 2027.

title: Miyazaki avenges Akechi and faces Wang in Hong Kong Open semifinals
article_text:
Tomoka Miyazaki, Japan's next-generation women's badminton star and the world No. 7, swept past compatriot Hina Akechi, ranked No. 14, to avenge her loss at the Korea Open and reach the Hong Kong Open semifinals.

Miyazaki beat Akechi 2-0 (21-11, 21-9) in the women's singles quarterfinals of the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Hong Kong Open (Super 500) on the 20th at Kai Tak Arena in Hong Kong.

It was a dominant victory. Miyazaki trailed 4-2 early in the first game but reeled off five straight points to take a 7-4 lead. She extended it to 10-5, and when Akechi began to close the gap, Miyazaki scored five consecutive points again to go ahead 15-6. She eventually took the first game 21-11.

The second game followed a similar pattern. Leading 2-1 early on, Miyazaki won seven points in a row to go up 9-1. Akechi fought back to 13-8, but Miyazaki won five straight points to seal the momentum. She closed out the match 21-9.

The victory means more than simply reaching the semifinals. On the 6th, Miyazaki lost to Akechi in the Korea Open women's singles quarterfinals in Yeosu, South Jeolla province, falling 2-1 (13-21, 23-21, 21-8) after taking the first game.

The Hong Kong Open is a good opportunity for Miyazaki to contend for the title. The top three in the women's singles rankings — world No. 1 Ahn Se-young, No. 2 Akane Yamaguchi of Japan and No. 5 Pusarla Venkata Sindhu of India — are all absent.

Miyazaki has already secured a spot in the 2026 BWF World Tour Finals. If she wins her first title of the season at this tournament, she can build her confidence ahead of the season-ending finals next month.

Miyazaki will face Wang Zhiyi in the semifinals. Wang beat Indonesia's Putri Kusuma Wardani 2-0 (22-20, 22-20) in an earlier quarterfinal.

After avenging her Korea Open loss to Akechi, Miyazaki now has a chance to get back at Wang Zhiyi, who eliminated her at the Kumamoto Masters. She is just two wins away from her first title of the season.

title: Hong Kong Open 2026: Lakshya Sen overcomes Loh Kean Yew in three games to enter semis
article_text:
Lakshya Sen beat Singapore’s Loh Kean Yew 21-17, 10-21, 21-13 to advance to the semifinals at the Hong Kong Open on Friday.

Lakshya made a brisk start to take an 11-7 lead into the interval, but Loh fought back strongly to draw level at 14-14. The two traded points in a tense finish before Lakshya found another gear to take the opening game 21-17.

Loh seized control early in the second game, racing to a 7-2 lead and carrying a comfortable 11-6 advantage into the interval. He continued to dominate after the break, stretching the lead to 19-10 before closing out the game 21-10 to force a decider.

Lakshya bounced back emphatically in the decider, racing to an 11-5 lead at the interval. He maintained his grip on the contest after the break, stretching the advantage to 19-10 before sealing the game 21-13 to complete a hard-fought victory.

Earlier, Lakshya, who is now assured of a spot at BWF Tour Finals 2026, beat Denmark’s Rasmus Gemke in straight games in the round of 16.

Lakshya revived his season in emphatic fashion, winning back-to-back titles at the Hylo Open and Japan Masters to emerge as a strong contender for the BWF World Tour Finals. His triumph in Japan, where he defeated Koki Watanabe in the final, proved crucial to his qualification bid, as he closed in on becoming only the second Indian after P. V. Sindhu (women’s singles) to make the cut for this year’s season-ending tournament.

Lakshya last featured in the BWF World Tour Finals in 2021, reaching the semifinals.

title: De Minaur to headline major Australian tournament amid form slump
article_text:
Alex de Minaur will take part in the Brisbane International for the first time in eight years, announcing he will play the Australian Open lead-up tournament in January.

In doing so, he becomes the biggest marquee player to sign up for the event since Rafael Nadal, Novak Djokovic and Andy Murray did so across the early 2020s.

It is also the event where Nick Kyrgios made his fleeting attempt at a singles return in 2026, before opting out of an Australian Open wildcard spot.

The tournament gets underway in the first week of January and de Minaur is excited to build into what will be a crucial calendar year for him.

“I love playing on Pat Rafter Arena and have so many fond memories of competing in Brisbane. The support is always awesome, and I can’t wait to get back out there,” de Minaur said.

“There’s nothing better than playing at home in Australia. The first week of the year is a great opportunity to get the season off to a strong start, and Brisbane is the perfect place to do that.

“It’ll be a strong field, as always, but you can’t beat winning at home, so I’ll be doing everything I can to lift the trophy in Brisbane.”

It marks the starting point of what the 27-year-old hopes will be a form turning point, after a difficult 2026 season.

De Minaur will enter 2027 as the No.11 ranked player in the world, after being as high as fifth in July.

A second round exit at the US Open coupled with poor performances on the ATP Tour in the second half of the year ultimately cost him from a ranking perspective.

The Aussie admits he has to change his mindset going forward and learn from what has turned into a form slump.

“It’s the first time that I’ve felt the inconsistency,” de Minaur told the Associated Press.

“I went through a six-month period where I kind of went walkabout. I wasn’t myself. I wasn’t playing the type of tennis that I know I could and I missed out on a lot of opportunities.

“I’ve been spoiled in a way that I’ve been able to bring that level week in and week out and for the longest time I almost expected those wins.

“I’ve got to be a little bit nicer to myself and appreciative of winning any sort of match.

“I was still worried about the level I was playing and I wasn’t content with myself.

“That carried on to the whole clay season and then it became a little bit of a snowball effect.”

Performance on the big stage in Grand Slams has also come into focus for de Minaur.

Despite sitting in-and-around the top 10 since 2023, he has had a tendency to stumble when it matters most.

De Minaur is yet to advance beyond a Grand Slam quarter-final at any of the four majors to this point of his career.

He made the quarter-final in the 2026 Australian Open before losing to Carlos Alcaraz, and stumbled in early phases of the other three Slams, missing out on golden opportunities to advance deep while Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner missed time with injuries.

“That’s one of the key things I want to focus on and try to go deep at the Slams,” he said.

“Really try to prioritise that a little bit more to make sure that all my energy goes towards those events.”

He has made the last two Australian Open quarter-finals, and will be hoping 2027 is the year he pushes deeper on his home turf.

title: Alexander Zverev suffers injury scare as Carlos Alcaraz discovers his fate at ATP Finals
article_text:
Alexander Zverev cleared some of the fog around the group phase of the ATP Finals as he powered to a third successive straight sets win by seeing off the challenge of Arthur Fils in Turin.

Zverev highlighted his impressive record against top ten rivals who are not Jannik Sinner or Carlos Alcaraz in a press conference earlier this week and he has backed up those words by adding another three wins to his record this week.

Zverev has seen off Rafael Jodar, Ben Shelton and now Fils in convincing fashion, with his latest win ensuring Shelton will progress to a potential semi-final clash against Alcaraz on Saturday.

There are doubts over whether Alcaraz will compete in the latter stages of the ATP Finals after he injured his hamstring in his win against Daniil Medvedev on Wednesday, but he now knows another match against Shelton awaits if he is fit enough to compete.

Alcaraz went for a scan on his hamstring on Thursday morning and it has been decided that he will try to compete in the rest of the tournament, but that position could change if his condition worsens.

Zverev also suffered an injury scare in his win against Fils, as he admitted a long-standing ankle problem was giving him some concern.

The pain he feels is linked to the huge injury he suffered in his 2022 French Open semi-final against Rafael Nadal, as he conceded it still gives him pain.

“Unfortunately I started feeling my ankle again,” Zverev said after his 6-4, 7-6(6) victory.

“I’ll probably feel my ankle sometimes until the end of my career. Unfortunately, the injury that I had was quite big. I’m going to do everything that I can to be pain-free on Saturday, but this is something I have to live with nowadays.”

Zverev also admitted some of his intensity was lacking against Fils as he knew his place in the semi-finals was already secured.

“I thought the first two matches were very high level,” he added.

“Today I thought I played a little bit worse from the baseline, but I’m very happy to have won all three matches, against three very difficult opponents.

“Arthur, for me personally, is a very difficult opponent because of how much power he has, but I’m happy to be through in straight sets.”

Zverev is set to play Daniil Medvedev in the last four on Saturday, with Alcaraz taking on Shelton if he can manage his hamstring problem.

title: ATP Finals 2026 Day 5 Recap
article_text:
Day 5 of the 2026 ATP Finals saw Alexander Zverev complete a perfect round-robin campaign, while Ben Shelton booked his place in the semi-finals after a hard-fought victory over Rafael Jodar.

Shelton survived two set points in a tight opening-set tiebreak before eventually seeing off the Spaniard in straight sets, although he had to wait for the evening result to confirm his qualification.

Zverev then defeated Arthur Fils 6-4, 7-6(6), despite the Frenchman saving five consecutive match points in a dramatic second-set tiebreak. The German tops the John McEnroe Group with three wins from three and hasn’t dropped a service game all week.

The result sets up a semi-final between Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz, while Zverev will face the winner of Friday’s clash between Daniil Medvedev and Frances Tiafoe.

Both Zverev and Alcaraz look a level above the rest so far, although a few physical concerns remain heading into the knockout stages, with Alcaraz nursing a hamstring issue and Zverev also appearing uncomfortable towards the end of his match.

Ben Shelton (3) def. Rafael Jodar (8) 7-6(8), 7-5

Ben Shelton kept his ATP Finals semi-final hopes alive on Thursday afternoon, defeating Rafael Jodar 7-6(8), 7-5 in a hard-fought encounter.

The American, who lost to Alexander Zverev on Tuesday, had to work considerably harder than expected against the 20-year-old Spaniard, eventually coming through in two hours and seven minutes.

The opening set was closely contested, with Jodar putting Shelton under pressure on serve and creating break opportunities. However, the American escaped trouble with his usual big serving, and the pair eventually headed to a tiebreak.

Jodar had two set points in the breaker, but Shelton saved both before finally taking it 10-8 when the Spaniard framed a forehand long.

The second set was another tight affair, though Shelton looked to have taken control after moving up to 4-2. However, Jodar refused to go away, fighting back to level at 5-5 with aggressive baseline hitting.

At that point, it looked like we might be heading for another tiebreak, but Shelton produced one of his better return games to break at 5-5, moving Jodar from corner to corner before serving out the match.

It wasn’t really a convincing display from Shelton from the baseline, and he basically relied heavily on his serve to get himself out of trouble.

Jodar had plenty of opportunities and probably should have taken the opening set, but he looked a bit leggy, especially when moving forward to track down Shelton’s shorter slices.

Jodar finishes his ATP Finals debut with three defeats, but his rise from No. 168 at the start of the year to the world’s top ten is one of the season’s stories, and he’s certainly one to watch next year.

Shelton, meanwhile, finishes the round-robin stage at 2-1 and must now wait for the result of Alexander Zverev’s match against Arthur Fils.

If Fils wins in straight sets, the Frenchman will progress alongside Zverev. Any other result will see Shelton qualify for the semi-finals in second place.

Alexander Zverev (1) def. Arthur Fils 6-4 7-6(6)

Alexander Zverev completed a perfect round-robin campaign at the 2026 ATP Finals on Thursday evening, defeating Arthur Fils 6-4, 7-6(6) to finish top of the John McEnroe Group without dropping a set.

The World No. 1, who had already secured his semi-final spot with victories over Rafael Jodar and Ben Shelton, made a solid start against the Frenchman, relying on his excellent serving and consistent baseline game.

Fils played some decent tennis in the opening set, but a sloppy service game at 3-3 proved costly. Zverev converted his third break point to move 4-3 ahead and comfortably served out the set 6-4 in around 35 minutes, ending Fils’ hopes of reaching the semi-finals and confirming Shelton’s qualification.

However, I liked how Fils tried to play, and he wasn’t about to roll over as the second set proved far more competitive.

The Frenchman raised his level, going toe-to-toe with Zverev from the baseline (who I thought didn’t hit his forehand as well), and showing the aggressive tennis that has propelled him into the Top 8 despite posting a woeful Grand Slam record.

Neither player could find the breakthrough until Fils earned two set points on Zverev’s serve at 6-5. However, Sascha produced some huge serves to escape trouble and force a tiebreak.

Zverev then won six consecutive points to lead 6-1, seemingly putting the match to bed, but Fils remarkably saved five straight match points to level at 6-6.

However, Sascha eventually got the job done, taking the breaker 8-6 to seal another straight-sets victory.

Fils put in a decent effort, and if he’d been a little wiser on some points, he’d have taken a set, but he ultimately couldn’t get past Zverev when it mattered.

For the German, it’s been an excellent group stage. Three matches, three victories, and six sets won without dropping a single one. He’s also gone through all three matches without losing a service game, which is pretty impressive given the opposition, but not so surprising given he’s bombing down 185 km/h second serves, on average.

Zverev advances to the semi-finals as the John McEnroe Group winner and will face either Daniil Medvedev or Frances Tiafoe, who meet on Friday to decide the second qualifying spot from the Ivan Lendl Group.

Shelton also advances despite his Tuesday defeat to Zverev and will face Carlos Alcaraz in the other semi-final.

title: A 15-year ATP Tour streak has just been broken by Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner, and Alexander Zverev
article_text:
Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, and Jannik Sinner have comfortably been the best three players on the ATP Tour this year.

Zverev has managed to claim the first two Grand Slam titles of his career, which subsequently helped him become world No 1 for the first time too.

Alcaraz, meanwhile, began the year with an Australian Open victory, before ending the year on a high with wins in Vienna and Paris after a four and a half month injury absence.

Sinner, too, has suffered with injuries, but he was still able to win the first five Masters titles of the season, as well as his fifth Grand Slam at Wimbledon.

The pair are far and away the top three ranked players on the ATP Tour, as they have been for the past three seasons.

Zverev, Alcaraz, and Sinner have become the first trio of players in 11 years to keep their place in the top three of the rankings for three consecutive seasons.

The last trio to do so was, unsurprisingly, Novak Djokovic, Roger Federer, and Rafael Nadal, who stayed top three for five years in a row between 2007 and 2011.

Zverev, Alcaraz, and Sinner have become just the third trio in men’s tennis history to earn the accolade, also joining Jimmy Connors, Ivan Lendl, and John McEnroe.

Those three tennis legends stayed in the top three between the 1981 and 1984 season, so the current best three players in the world are in very good company.

There is little reason to believe that they will not continue that form into the 2027 season either, particularly with how this season has gone.

Sinner has missed six months of action and Alcaraz has missed four and a half months and yet neither came anywhere near close to losing their position in the top three of the ATP Tour rankings.

As things stand, Alcaraz, who is the current world No 3, sits 1200 ranking points above Ben Shelton in the rankings, and that looks destined to increase at the ATP Finals.

A potential hamstring injury aside, Alcaraz is one of the major favourites to win the ATP Finals and it would be a big surprise to not see him make the final.

The Spaniard could create yet more distance between world No 3 and world No 4 as the 2026 season draws to a close.

It’s hard to see anyone having the consistency to dislodge Zverev, Sinner, and Alcaraz from the rankings, despite the likes of Shelton, Arthur Fils, and Flavio Cobolli making giant strides in the rankings this season.

title: Alcaraz Cleared to Continue ATP Finals, But Risk Remains
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz has reportedly received encouraging news regarding his left hamstring injury and has decided to continue competing at the ATP Finals in Turin.

According to reports from Spanish media, including Punto de Break, Cadena COPE and RTVE, an MRI conducted on Thursday ruled out structural damage to the Spaniard’s left hamstring, clearing the way for him to face Flavio Cobolli on Friday.

Note: Alcaraz has already qualified for the semifinals, so the stakes of Friday’s match aren’t as high as they might have been had he been preparing to play for qualifying for the semifinals.

It doesn’t necessarily mean the 23-year-old, who cancelled today’s practice with junior No.1 Guto Miguel of Brazil, is out of the woods.

Cadena SER reports that Alcaraz’s team is taking a cautious, match-by-match approach, with the seven-time Grand Slam champion expected to evaluate his physical condition following Friday’s encounter before making any decisions about the semifinals.

Friday’s match with Cobolli should give him the information he needs to decide whether or not he feels good enough to make a run at winning the title in Turin.

There is also the matter of Alcaraz’s right knee, which had been troubling him ahead of the tournament. RTVE reported that Thursday’s medical examinations also addressed the knee, but no specific findings have been made public.

It all adds up to a delicate situation for Alcaraz, who has plenty at stake beyond this week’s competition in Turin. The Spaniard is expected to represent his country at the Davis Cup Finals later this month, and the pressure to compete for his nation will undoubtedly weigh heavily on him.

There is also the bigger picture to consider.

With the 2027 season fast approaching, Alcaraz will have a relatively short offseason to recover, rebuild and prepare for his Australian Open title defense.

But the combination of hamstring discomfort and an ongoing knee concern makes this an especially important moment for the Spaniard. Tempted by winning the ATP Finals and then representing Spain at Davis Cup could come at a cost. He’ll have to listen closely to his body, and make a decision that balances the present and the future.

title: Jannik Sinner’s latest decision sparks concern as new injury update emerges
article_text:
It is unclear when Jannik Sinner will return from the right knee injury that has sidelined him since July, and a new update has now emerged.

Sinner has not played since he defeated Alexander Zverev in the 2026 Wimbledon final to defend his title at the grass-court major.

While Sinner has not shared details about the specific nature of his knee injury, Sky Sport Italy have reported that the issue he is dealing with is iliotibial band syndrome (ITBS).

Last week, Sinner divulged he is hoping to make his comeback before the 2027 Australian Open.

“The goal is to go to Australia; I hope to get there, and perhaps play a few tournaments beforehand,” said the world No 2.

“Right now, I need to follow the protocols without rushing things. I have a lot of faith in the process, and I’m working toward that objective.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

“Initially, we had an impossible goal for my return in mind, so we took a different path. I’m a tennis player, not a doctor, so my only option is to trust them.

“I miss playing tennis. Right now, however, it is crucial that I take care of my body, because I want to keep playing for another 10 to 15 years.”

The 25-year-old Italian added: “I’m fine. We’re doing everything we can — and more — to get back on the court as soon as possible.

“I have a great team with many experts to help us come back stronger.”

Vanity Fair Italia has reported Sinner is set to fly to America “to consult another specialist and determine the best course of action to return to the field without risking a relapse.”

The report added: “After meeting with Professor Alberto Zangrillo and a team from the San Raffaele Hospital in Milan, Jannik wants a further opinion before making any decisions.”

The revelation that Sinner will speak to another specialist has sparked some concern among fans about the condition of his knee.

It seems far from certain that the five-time Grand Slam champion will be fit for the start of the 2027 season.

title: ATP Finals 2026: Draw and schedule as Carlos Alcaraz, Alexander Zverev qualify for semifinals
ATP Finals: Ben Shelton beats Rafael Jodar to move within touching distance of semi-finals
article_text:
Ben Shelton battled past Rafael Jodar to move within touching distance of a place in the ATP Finals last four.

US Open runner-up Shelton only lost his serve once but still had to fight for just over two hours to beat the fast-rising Spaniard 7-6 (10-8) 7-5.

American Shelton closed out the match with three aces in a row and then wrote "I'll be watching, Arthur" on the camera lens - a reference to the final game in the group.

Shelton will progress to the semi-finals if world number one Alexander Zverev beats France's Arthur Fils later on Thursday.

Fils would need to beat Zverev in straight sets if he is to qualify instead of Shelton.

"I think if he takes Sascha [Zverev] out in straights, I'll say too good and go on holidays," Shelton joked of his good friend Fils.

"I'm always rooting for him [Arthur] and I think he and Sascha will have a great match.

"I'd love to make the semi-finals for the first time. I'll definitely be watching."

Germany's Zverev, unbeaten so far at the season-ending event, is assured of top place in the John McEnroe Group, and will play either Daniil Medvedev or Frances Tiafoe in Saturday's semi-finals.

Shelton did not win a match on his ATP Finals debut last year, but arrived in Turin with a Masters 1000 title and a first Grand Slam final under his belt.

He beat Fils in three entertaining sets in his opening match before being swept aside by Zverev on Tuesday.

Shelton was under pressure against Jodar in the first set, saving two break points and missing a series of routine shots when his opponent was struggling.

However, after taking a tight tie-break, Shelton quickly broke to take control of the third set.

Jodar, competing in his first professional season on the ATP Tour, was strong defensively and wrestled the break back to level at 4-4.

However, he was visibly fatigued and unable to keep Shelton at bay in a series of lengthy rallies, with Shelton breaking for 6-5.

Shelton slipped at the back of court as he served for the match, but recovered quickly to close out victory. He finished with 14 aces to one double fault, having dropped only 11 points behind his first serve.

In the doubles, Britain's Henry Patten and Finnish partner Harri Heliovaara will need to beat French pair Theo Arribage and Albano Olivetti if they are to keep their title defence alive.

Wimbledon champions Patten and Heliovaara have won one and lost one of their three group matches.

title: WTA names Jamie Baker chief tour officer
article_text:
- Former British No. 2 and Wimbledon Tournament Director brings extensive experience across professional tennis, tournament operations and player relations

The WTA (Women's Tennis Association) on Thursday announced the appointment of Jamie Baker as Chief Tour Officer. A former professional player and most recently Associate Director of Professional Tennis and Tournament Director at Wimbledon, Baker brings a distinctive combination of experience as a competitor, tournament leader, and business professional to the WTA. He will join the organization during the first quarter of 2027.

In his new role, Baker will oversee Tour operations, player and tournament relations, and performance health, working closely with players, tournaments, and colleagues across the organization. His appointment adds significant tennis and operational expertise to the WTA's leadership team as the organization builds on its recent success delivering the WTA Finals back in the U.S.

"Jamie brings an exceptional combination of experience as a professional player and a leader at one of the world's most prestigious tournaments," said Valerie Camillo, Chair and CEO of the WTA. "He understands the sport from multiple perspectives, from the player experience to the operational demands of running a major international event. His expertise and judgment will be invaluable as we continue to grow the Tour and deliver enhanced services to our players and tournaments."

"Jamie has a deep understanding of what it takes to deliver professional tennis at the highest level, and he brings a valuable perspective on the needs of players and tournaments," said Adam Barrett, WTA Tournament Council Chair and Tournament Board Representative. "His experience and collaborative approach will be an asset to the WTA and to the broader tennis community. We look forward to working with him in this new role."

"I'm delighted to be joining the WTA at such an important moment of opportunity. The WTA has an extraordinary legacy and has played a defining role in shaping the future of women's sport. As women's sports continue to grow and attract new audiences and investment, the WTA is uniquely positioned to help lead that next chapter, drawing on its rich history, its athletes, and the global reach of the sport. I'm honored to be part of that work and look forward to contributing to the future of the Tour," said Baker.

Baker joins the WTA from The All England Lawn Tennis Club (AELTC), where he served as Associate Director of Professional Tennis and Tournament Director. In that role, he led tennis matters for The Championships, overseeing key aspects of tournament operations, including officiating, scheduling, player services, and practice facilities. He was also responsible for the player experience, grass court strategy, and relationships with the ATP, WTA, and World Tennis.

His experience at Wimbledon follows a career that spans both sides of professional tennis. Prior to tournament leadership, Baker competed on the ATP Tour, where he was ranked as high as British No. 2 before retiring from professional tennis in 2013.

Following his playing career, Baker spent nearly five years in corporate banking at Santander before joining The AELTC as Head of Tennis Relations in 2018. He was promoted to Head of Professional Tennis and Tournament Director in 2020 and became Associate Director of Professional Tennis in 2024.

At the WTA, Baker will bring this combination of competitive, operational, and business experience to the work of supporting players and tournaments and managing the Tour. His experience managing a world-class tournament will be instrumental in the WTA's new approach to self-operating the WTA Finals and the work to build out the event in Charlotte.

With the addition of the Chief Tour Officer role, Valerie Camillo will be CEO of the WTA in addition to her role as Chair. Camillo will partner with Marina Storti in her role as CEO of WTA Ventures, the commercial arm of the WTA.

title: American tennis player receives two-year ban after testing positive for same substance as Jannik Sinner
article_text:
Jessica Eudovic has been handed a two-year ban by the International Tennis Intregrity Agency after testing positive for clostebol in the 2025 season.

The star had been provisionally suspended for over a year since testing positive at a World Tennis Tour event in Santa Tecla, El Salvador, on the 1st October 2025.

The process was drawn out due to Eudovic challenging the suspension, which caused the case to be moved to a independent tribunal.

Following a two-day hearing in October, Eudovic has still received the ban, which she will now need to serve a year of after already missing 12 months of action.

According to the ITIA, “the tribunal found that while Eudovic did not establish how clostebol entered her system, the breach was not intentional.

“In reaching its decision, the tribunal considered the scientific evidence, including the very low level of clostebol detected in Eudovic’s sample, the circumstances of the case, and Eudovic’s evidence.

“As Eudovic was unable to establish how the prohibited substance entered her system, despite accessing the ITIA’s support fund for product testing, the tribunal could not consider a further reduction of the sanction. Eudovic was therefore suspended for two years.

“Time served under provisional suspension is credited against the sanction. As such, Eudovic’s suspension ends on 20 November 2027. Eudovic’s results from the event in Santa Tecla are also disqualified, with the associated ranking points and prize money forfeited.

“While suspended, Eudovic is not allowed to play in, coach at, or attend any events organised or sanctioned by World Tennis, WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams, or any national association.”

This is, of course, not the first time a player has tested positive for clostebol, which is banned synthetic anabolic–androgenic steroid.

Jannik Sinner is perhaps the most high-profile player to receive a ban after testing positive for clostebol, as he missed three months of action after a settlement with the International Tennis Integrity Agency.

Lower down the tennis rankings, and the likes of Karlis Ozolins and Daniil Kakhniuk have also been suspended due to testing positive for clostebol.

As for Eudovic, the star’s early career has been rocked by the case and the suspension.

She has not played competitively since appearing at a WTT W35 tournament in Boca Raton, United States in November of last year.

By the time she will return to action she will be 20 years old, so there is plenty of time for her to hit the ground running and bounce back from the ban.

She has been ranked as high as world No 1104 in the rankings.

title: Iconic tennis tournament faces being axed and two more replaced at crunch ATP meeting
article_text:
An iconic tournament on the ATP Tour is at risk of being axed, with two more also on the chopping block, as per reports. It comes as the Tour's chiefs meet in Turin at the end of the 2026 tennis season.

And on the table at that crunch meeting, according to Cor Sport, is the future of the Mexican Open. The tournament, which has been held in Acapulco since 2001, is potentially getting the chop from the 2028 season onwards.

Meanwhile, the other two at-risk tournaments are Doha and Dubai, with talk that they could be scrapped from the schedule as early as 2027. That's due to ongoing unrest in the Middle East, with tournaments in the region disrupted earlier this year.

The leadership at the ATP are said to be deep in discussions about how to handle the geopolitical crisis, with suggestions that the two ATP 500 events could be moved or even replaced. The governing body is wary of mid-season disruption again and therefore wants to act with foresight.

The two tournaments are currently scheduled for February, with Doha taking place the week before the tour rolls into Dubai. There has been a suggestion that the Tour is keen for one ATP 500 event to host two tournaments in consecutive weeks. But both Rotterdam and Dallas and Delray Beach have already communicated their inability to do this.

By contrast, organisers in Rio de Janeiro have proposed a back-to-back tournament in Brazil, but the drawback is that it would be on clay. The ATP isn't convinced by that proposal and therefore it's been mooted that they could just create a brand new tournament in a location that is yet to be decided.

There is talk that Rio, along with Gstaad, Kitzbuhel, Umago and Bastad could all switch to hard courts. However, that wouldn't happen until 2029 at the earliest. Also on the agenda was a discussion about the distribution of ranking points and the future of doubles on tour.

On court, the season-ending ATP Finals are ongoing, with top two seeds Alexander Zverev and Carlos Alcaraz both qualified for the semi-finals.

title: Alcaraz undergoes MRI on hamstring and cancels training, his ATP Finals in the balance (report)
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz had scans on his left hamstring and right knee in Turin around midday and called off his 1 pm training session. With no result released, Friday’s dead rubber against Cobolli and Saturday’s semi-final now hang on his condition.

Carlos Alcaraz had an MRI scan on his left hamstring and his right knee around midday on Thursday in Turin, then pulled out of his training session. It comes a day after he needed treatment during his 6-2, 6-4 win over Daniil Medvedev. The result had not been made public at the time of writing, and neither the ATP nor his team has made a statement.

The scan took place at the Istituto di Medicina dello Sport, close to the Inalpi Arena, according to Sky Sport Italia and EFE. Sky Sport Italia says he arrived at 12:08 and left at around 1:15 pm. He was accompanied by his doctor Juanjo López, his physio Juanjo Moreno and his fitness coach Alberto Lledó, according to El Español.

His training session, planned for 1 pm with the Brazilian junior Guto Miguel, was cancelled. He was taken off the schedule a minute before it was due to start, according to EFE, as a precaution. A first check on Wednesday evening had shown nothing conclusive, the injury being too recent.

On Wednesday, Alcaraz had played the problem down without closing the door. “I feel it a little bit. I’m not gonna lie,” he said in his press conference. “Right now I’m just feeling okay.” He added: “We will see with my team, with my physio, but I think the rest of the day and tomorrow is really going to be important days ahead of me.”

He had already secured first place in Group Lendl that evening, when Frances Tiafoe beat Flavio Cobolli 7-6(6), 6-0. The right knee is not a new subject: he had already been protecting it in training before the tournament.

Alcaraz is due to face Cobolli on Friday, at 2 pm according to the Spanish press, in a match with nothing at stake in the standings: Alcaraz is first and Cobolli is eliminated. For Alcaraz, though, the rule makes it decisive. A player who withdraws from a round-robin match after the first round cannot play the knockout stage, so if he does not play Cobolli, he is out.

If he starts the match and retires, he can still play Saturday’s semi-final against the runner-up of the McEnroe Group, subject to a favourable medical opinion, according to Sky Sport Italia and EFE. His replacement would be Alex de Minaur, the first alternate according to the Italian press (Sky Sport Italia, Adnkronos).

The Davis Cup is also in view. Alcaraz is in Spain’s team for the Final 8 in Bologna, from 24 to 29 November, with a quarter-final against Austria on 26 November according to Sky Sport Italia. There is a precedent: in 2025, after losing the ATP Finals final to Jannik Sinner, an oedema of the right hamstring, detected on MRI, kept him out of the Davis Cup. His withdrawal was announced on 18 November 2025.

His Davis Cup teammate Rafael Jodar, speaking in Spanish after his defeat to Ben Shelton on Thursday, said he has not yet spoken to Alcaraz. “I haven’t had time to talk to either Carlos or the captain yet,” he said. “I see Carlos very motivated to play this competition and to give everything for his country.” He added: “If he is physically and mentally well, which I believe is the case, he will be with us, but obviously it is a decision for his team and for him.”

title: An Se-young and Yamaguchi both absent, China suffers 'massive humiliation' as women's singles players eliminated one after another... Wang Zhiyi is already the sole survivor
article_text:
*This content was translated by AI.View Original

Neither Korea's badminton "queen" An Se-young (24, Samsung Life) nor Japan's star Yamaguchi Akane (29) are present. However, China suffered humiliation as its women's singles players were eliminated one after another. Wang Zhiyi (26) is already the only one left standing.

World No. 3 Wang Zhiyi defeated Nidaara Natuki (Japan) 2-0 (21-13, 21-15) in the women's singles round of 16 at the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Hong Kong Open (Super 500), held on the 19th (Korean time) at the Kai Tak Arena in Hong Kong. Among the four Chinese players who entered the women's singles event at this tournament, Wang Zhiyi is the only one to advance to the quarterfinals.

From China's perspective, this tournament was an opportunity they absolutely did not want to miss. This is because world No. 1 An Se-young and No. 2 Yamaguchi were both absent.

An Se-young has been combining rest and treatment since winning the Korea Open on the 8th of last month. She is in the process of getting her body in shape ahead of the BWF World Tour Finals, which will be held in Hangzhou, China, next month.

At the "Yonex Podium Day with Badminton National Team" event held at The Hyundai Seoul in Yeongdeungpo-gu, Seoul on the 16th of last month, An Se-young shared her recent status, saying, "I have been running without rest for three months, so my body has broken down quite a bit and I am receiving treatment."

An Se-young's absence was a huge opportunity for other players. This season, An Se-young recorded 71 wins and one loss in 72 matches, and she had run up a streak of 55 consecutive victories since her defeat in the All England Open final in March of last year. She has already collected 11 championship trophies.

On top of that, Yamaguchi also did not participate in this tournament. Yamaguchi is a powerhouse who won the Kumamoto Masters on the 15th of last month by consecutively defeating Chinese players.

At the time, Chen Yufei withdrew due to a foot injury during the final game of the semifinal against Yamaguchi. Wang Zhiyi, who advanced to the final, also lost to Yamaguchi 0-2 (14-21, 20-22). China had aimed for victory in a tournament where An Se-young was absent, but they were blocked by another wall.

At this Hong Kong Open, both players were avoided, but China's challenge is not unfolding as expected. Sina.com explained, "China sent out all its main women's singles players, but rivals An Se-young and Yamaguchi did not participate," adding, "Wang Zhiyi and Chen Yufei received the No. 1 and No. 2 seeds respectively, so the outlook for winning was very bright."

However, contrary to expectations, Chinese players packed their bags one after another. The media pointed out, "Only Wang Zhiyi remains in China's women's singles."

The biggest shock was the elimination of world No. 4 Chen Yufei. Chen Yufei lost to Lakshita Ramraj (India), ranked 47th in the world, 0-2 (18-21, 22-24) in the round of 16 on the same day. The Tokyo Olympics women's singles gold medalist failed to win a single game against the 19th-year-old promising player.

Just one day earlier, she had shown confidence. According to China's Xinhua News Agency, Chen Yufei was asked about the drought in Chinese women's singles titles after defeating Amalie Schulz (Denmark) on the 18th of last month.

In response, Chen Yufei said, "I think this tournament will be fine." However, her own challenge ended in her second match.

Her foot injury, which is still recovering, and a tight schedule were also variables. Sina.com assessed, "Chen Yufei looked relatively tired throughout the match, and her movement on the court was not agile enough."

It further analyzed, "The previous injury and this tight schedule appear to have had some impact on Chen Yufei." Chen Yufei played her first-round match the previous evening and then returned to the court somewhat earlier than other players on that day.

Another Chinese player, Han We, also could not continue the tournament to the end. She withdrew in the round of 16 against Michelle Li (Canada) due to physical condition issues. She had lost the first game 14-21 and was trailing 5-11 in the second game.

Shi Wenjing had already been eliminated after losing to Akechi Hina (Japan) in the first round. With Chen Yufei and Han We also withdrawing in the round of 16, the challenge for a Chinese women's singles title has fallen solely on Wang Zhiyi.

Victory is desperately needed in Chinese women's singles. They have not been able to lift a trophy for a full eight months. Wang Zhiyi has not reached the top since the All England Open in March of last year, and Chen Yufei's only win this year was at the Indonesia Masters in January of this year. The shoulders of Wang Zhiyi, who is left alone, are inevitably even heavier.

Wang Zhiyi will face Putri Kusuma Wardani (Indonesia) in the quarterfinals on the 20th. As the sole survivor in Chinese women's singles, she will challenge for a spot in the semifinals.

title: Hong Kong Open: Teen Santhosh Ramraj Shocks Idol Chen
article_text:
Never meet your heroes, unless you are 19-year-old Rakshitha Sree Santhosh Ramraj, in which case you might just knock them out of a Super 500 tournament.

The Indian world No.47 delivered the shock of LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 on Thursday, toppling pre-tournament favourite and world No.4 Chen Yu Fei 21-18 24-22 in the second round.

Just 24 hours after banking her maiden top 20 scalp against Mia Blichfeldt, Santhosh Ramraj bagged her first top 10 victory – becoming the first player outside the top 30 to beat Chen since Gregoria Mariska Tunjung in 2017.

“She’s my biggest idol and I still can’t believe I won against her,” Santhosh Ramraj admitted afterward, visibly awestruck. “This will be one of the most memorable days in my playing career.”

The win was no fluke. Combining fearless aggression with stubborn defence, Santhosh Ramraj refused to blink even when staring down a 15-5 deficit in the second game. Ironically, her secret weapon was simply mentally clocking in for a decider.

“Actually, I was preparing for the third game,” she laughed. “I just didn’t want to give up so easily. Since she’s so senior, I had nothing to lose, so I kept on trying. It worked out really well that I was able to close the gap.”

Behind the giantkilling performance lies a quiet story of family sacrifice. Six years ago, her family uprooted their lives in Coimbatore and moved to Hyderabad so she could train at the Gopichand Academy – a leap of faith now paying dividends. Having reached the Korea Masters semifinals in August, she is now into her first Super 500 quarterfinal of the season.

“I think I’m not less than anyone,” she said, the awe quickly giving way to conviction. “I’m very thankful to all my coaches for supporting me throughout this journey.”

Her reward for slaying her idol? A maiden clash with Thailand’s Pornpawee Chochuwong, who swept Lin Hsiang Ti 21-11 21-12 to keep her HSBC BWF World Tour Finals hopes alive.

If Thursday proved anything, Chochuwong shouldn’t expect the teenager to show too much respect.

title: Satwik-Chirag cruise into Hong Kong Open quarterfinals
article_text:
Hong Kong Open: Rakshitha Ramraj stuns world No.4 Chen Yufei to reach quarterfinals

Meanwhile, the fifth seed Satwik-Chirag beat the Malaysian pair in straight games to reach the men's doubles last eight.

Rakshitha Ramraj continued her impressive run as she stunned world No. 4 Chen Yufei to storm into the quarterfinals of the Hong Kong Open Super 500 on Thursday.

The 19-year-old Indian secured a straight-games victory (21-18, 24-22) over the former Olympic champion and five-time world medallist in 45 minutes.

“This is the biggest win of my career. She is my biggest idol, and I still can’t believe I beat her. This will be the most memorable day of my career,” Ramraj said in her post-match interview.

“I’m very happy that whatever I played worked out really well. My attack was really good today, and that was the key. I believe I can do even better in the future,” she added.

After taking the opening game, Ramraj produced a remarkable fightback in the second, recovering from 5-15 down to close it out 24-22, and setting up a quarterfinal clash with Thailand's Pornpawee Chochuwong.

“I was actually preparing for a third game, but I didn’t want to give up so easily. I kept trying, and in the end it worked really well to cover the deficit,” she said.

This is the biggest win of Ramraj’s career so far. She had earlier caused another upset in the first round by defeating world No. 20 Mia Blichfeldt of Denmark.

Meanwhile, Indian men's doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty also moved to the quarter-finals with a straight-game win over Malaysia’s Nur Mohd Azriyn Ayub and Tan Wee Kiong.

The fifth-seeded Indians, who won two Super 750 titles this year at Singapore and China, put up a clinical show during their 21-19, 21-16 win over Nur and Tan in 42 minutes.

Satwik and Chirag will next face China’s Hu Ke Yuan and Lin Xiang Yi on Friday, who beat Japan’s Kakeru Kumagai and Hiroki Nishi 21-19, 21-17.

Earlier, the Indian duo needed three games to get past Chinese Taipei’s Lee Jhe-Huei and Yang Po-Hsuan in the opening round.

In the women’s doubles, the world bronze medalists Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand lost to the American pair of Lauren Lam and Allison Lee 20-22, 13-21 in the pre-quarterfinals to end their campaign.

Lakshya Sen, who has sealed his place in the season-ending BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou, also reached the last eight with a 21-11, 21-18 win over Denmark’s Rasmus Gemke in the men’s singles pre-quarterfinals.

title: ‘I see comments every day’: Sonay Kartal’s fightback against injury and online abuse
article_text:
Sonay Kartal believes the vitriolic abuse and threats that she and her fellow players receive after every match have become an unavoidable part of her job.

“Unfortunately, it’s something that comes with the sport,” the British No 2 says. “I don’t really have a choice to not deal with it. Obviously, it’s not a good thing to have and as a player, win or lose, you’re seeing those things.

“You can try and take yourself away from it as much as you can and you can do different things to your [social media] account to try and hide it, but it’s a shame that it is something we have to deal with and hopefully it can change. But we’ve all been there, we know what it’s like when you have a loss and you see your social media flooded with not very nice comments.”

Social media abuse has been a constant theme for players in recent years, particularly due to the prevalence of sports betting, and many have spoken out. Most recently, her compatriot Jodie Burrage reposted some of the barrage of abuse received on her Instagram account earlier this month.

While the governing bodies have developed some tools to monitor it, and limit the comments that players see, Kartal notes that most of those initiatives come at the cost of privacy, making them a less than ideal solution. “I see those comments every day, it’s hard to avoid them,” she says.

“You look at a post, you look at your Instagram, and they’re there. At the start, it was not very nice to read but unfortunately I’m used to it now so it’s just another one. You just deal with it. It is what it is.”

Kartal was speaking from the comfort of the National Tennis Centre, her home away from home, at the end of perhaps the most challenging season of her career. In March, she defeated the 2025 Australian Open champion, Madison Keys, to reach the last 16 at Indian Wells, an excellent result. At No 54 in the world rankings, she sat 10 spots away from her career-high No 44 and it seemed she would keep on moving forward. Instead, she would not compete for another six months after being diagnosed with a stress fracture in her back.

As she reflects on months of long rehab and the frustration of working through her injury at Roehampton while surrounded by players sweeping in and out between tournaments, Kartal describes the first month as the most painful. “It was just very uncomfortable,” she says. “I had a lot of nerve pain, too. I wouldn’t wish sciatica pain upon anyone. Back pain and nerve pain is not fun.

“I would just be doing normal things like brushing my teeth or putting my shoes on and I’m in quite a lot of pain, which is not fun. For a 24-year-old it was not something I really wanted to deal with, which is another reason why I just had to let this get better. I couldn’t really rush it because it’s six months of my time now versus maybe it’s post-Sonay’s tennis life constantly having back pain.”

Her response was spectacular. While some players naturally take time to find their timing or match instincts after such a long time out, Kartal hit the ground running immediately. In just her third tournament back at the Wuhan Open in October, she defeated Belinda Bencic, Jasmine Paolini, Elina Svitolina and Jelena Ostapenko, four former top-five players, consecutively to reach her first WTA 1000 final – and led Maja Chwalinska in the final before being beaten in three sets.

Having tumbled to No 170 in the world that week due to her extended absence, that result allowed her ranking to skyrocket, and she is now at No 53 as she prepares for the new season. She also briefly became the British No 1 – Katie Boulter has since leapfrogged her once more – for the first time.

Kartal’s next goal is to be seeded at the major tournaments and, having dragged herself so quickly back to where she was before the injury, to keep on pushing forward: “I didn’t worry about ever getting back to that level,” she says, shrugging. “I just wasn’t sure how long it would take me.”

Ash Barty and Shingo Kunieda to be Inducted Into International Tennis Hall of Fame
article_text:
Major moments inspired all-court conviction in Ashleigh Barty.

Former world No. 1 Barty brought her best in Grand Slam finals posting a 3-0 record in Slam showdowns winning six of the seven sets she played in those finals.

Now, the 30-year-old Barty will receive tennis ultimate honor: Induction into the International Tennis Hall of Fame.

Barty and Shingo Kunieda, the most decorated men’s wheelchair tennis player in history, winning a record 28 Grand Slam singles titles and 50 major titles overall, form the International Tennis Hall of Fame’s Class of 2027, the Hall announced today.

The Class of 2027 will be inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame during Hall of Fame weekend August 26–28, 2027 in Newport, Rhode Island.

The Barty Party peaked in a homecoming crescendo in January of 2022 as the top-seeded Aussie’s 6-3, 7-6 win over feisty American Danielle Collins snapped a 44-year home singles drought at the Australian Open and captivated Aussies.

Barty’s triumph drew a peak viewership of 4.26 million TV viewers Down Under making it the most widely-viewed Australian Open women’s final in Australia in history.

“I’m so grateful. Tennis has given me everything and more,” Barty said. “In my career, I’ve been introduced and connect with so many amazing people around the world. And it’s also given me the opportunity to have some of my dreams after tennis: Starting a family…

One of the greatest sub 5’8″ servers in tennis history, Barty was a highly-skilled all-court player who excelled on all surfaces.

Barty owns three Grand Slam titles on three different surfaces: 2022 Australian Open on hard court, 2021 Wimbledon on grass and 2019 Roland Garros on clay. Barty’s 114 consecutive weeks as world No. 1 is fourth on the all-time list behind only Serena Williams and Steffi Graf (186 consecutive weeks apiece) and Martina Navratilova (156 consecutive weeks).

When Barty won the 2021 Wimbledon, she joined Ann Jones, Martina Hingis and Amelie Mauresmo as the fourth junior champion to raise the Rosewater Dish. Barty was such a gifted athlete she played two sports professionally: Cricket and tennis. Barty took the entire 2015 season off and played pro cricket for the Brisbane Heat during her time away from tennis.

“To be able to win Wimbledon which was my dream, my one true dream that I wanted in tennis, really changed my perspective,” Barty said when she announced her 2022 retirement. “I just had that gut feeling after Wimbledon. I had spoken to my team quite a lot about it and there was just a little part of me that wasn’t quite fulfilled.

“Then came the challenge of the Australian Open. That for me just feels like my perfect way to celebrate what an amazing journey my tennis career has been. As a person, this is what I want.”

Alexander Zverev notified of lawsuit by former partner in abuse case during middle of ATP Finals
article_text:
World No 1 Alexander Zverev was officially notified of a lawsuit filed by his former partner during the middle of the season-ending ATP Finals on Wednesday.

The latest legal case brought by the mother of Zverev's former partner alleges the tennis player violated the terms of an out-of-court settlement between the pair after the woman accused him of assaulting her.

The lawsuit brought by Brenda Patea in Germany takes issue with Zverev reportedly saying in an interview with French sports news outlet L'Equipe earlier this year that "it has been proven that the accusations were false" and "my innocence has been proven."

Zverev's Berlin-based lawyers, Christian Schertz and Anna Sophie Heuchemer, confirmed in a statement shared with The Associated Press that they were formally served with Patea's lawsuit on Wednesday.

"Our client will defend himself against the lawsuit," Zverev's lawyers said. "If the statement attributed to him was indeed made in the form alleged, we consider it to be a permissible expression of opinion" protected by the German constitution.

They said there had been no breach of any contractual obligations.

Patea's lawyer, Michael Scheele, told The Associated Press that Zverev's claim over his innocence "triggered a veritable storm of criticism against our client."

He said the backlash was damaging to her business as an influencer and that she also felt her honour had been violated.

"Quite apart from the fact that Zverev's claim is false, he was not permitted to make any public statements whatsoever, in any form," he said. "Both Brenda Patea and Alexander Zverev had agreed to this in a settlement."

Patea is seeking that Zverev be ordered not to repeat such comments and that he be fined up to £208,484 €250,000 euros every time if he does.

Zverev faced a charge of causing bodily harm to Patea during an argument in Berlin in May 2020. He always denied any wrongdoing.

The case ended in a district court in Berlin in 2024 after the settlement. Zverev agreed to pay fines to the state and charitable organisations.

Zverev this month ascended to the No 1 ranking for the first time. He also won his first two Grand Slam titles this year and is competing this week at the ATP Finals in Turin.

Zverev has not commented on the lawsuit.

He previously denied abuse allegations from another former girlfriend, Olga Sharypova, who first made the accusations in 2020 and followed up in 2021 with a detailed account in a Slate.com article that was taken down because of a preliminary injunction issued by a German court. Slate said it stood by the article.

The allegations prompted the men's professional tennis tour, the ATP, to investigate her claims. It ended 15 months later, in January 2023, with the ATP saying there was "insufficient evidence" to substantiate the claims.

title: Alcaraz gives injury update at Nitto ATP Finals
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz made it two wins from two on Wednesday at this year’s Nitto ATP Finals but walked off court with heavy strapping on his left leg following his victory against Daniil Medvedev.

The Spaniard received treatment on his upper left leg from the tournament physio when leading by a break at 2-1 in the second set. The 23-year-old did not appear hindered by the issue, and afterward gave an update on his condition.

“I feel it a little bit,” Alcaraz said in his post-match press conference when asked about his left leg. “I'm not going to lie. But, you know, unfortunately I was playing great, and suddenly I felt a little problem of my hamstring. But just a little bit.

“I could play really good tennis since that moment until the end of the match. I was really focused on other things. I was trying to stay relaxed, to move not too aggressive, let's say. I'm thinking about being aggressive and thinking about my shots all the time. So right now, I'm just feeling okay. We will see with my team, with my physio, but I think the rest of the day and tomorrow is really going to be important days ahead of me.”

Alcaraz knows all too well how quickly an injury can change a player's perspective. The Spaniard spent more than four months sidelined earlier this year after sustaining a wrist injury at the ATP 500 event in Barcelona. The No. 3 player in the PIF ATP Rankings eventually returned at the US Open in August, reaching the quarter-finals.

Since then, Alcaraz has lifted trophies in Paris, Vienna and Tokyo to arrive in Turin in outstanding form. But the time away from the court also left him with a renewed appreciation for the opportunity to compete, a perspective that came into focus again after Wednesday's hamstring concern.

“The injury made me realise what's important, what's really important,” Alcaraz said. “It's not winning, it's not winning or losing finals of tournaments. It's just about playing tennis. That's what I realise, that it is a gift every time that I can step on the court and compete healthy.

“When you realise that, everything comes easier for me, because I enjoy and I don't feel stressful on a tennis court, or most of the time I don't feel stressful on a tennis court, which means I could face the problems in a different way. More calm, relaxed, and I'm thinking, ‘OK, I'm going to still try my best tennis, I'm going to still try what I have to do.’”

Alcaraz will face Flavio Cobolli in his final round-robin match in Turin. The 29-time tour-level titlist is aiming to lift the trophy at the prestigious year-end event for the first time this week.

title: Sponsor Invite Admits To 'Extremely Poor Decision' In Wake Of LPGA Tour Disqualification
article_text:
University of Miami golfer Scarlett Schremmer has admitted she made an "extremely poor decision" by initially denying using an illegal green-reading book during her LPGA Tour debut.

The sponsor invite was disqualified from The Annika at Pelican Golf Club after using a green-reading book that was apparently permitted in college golf but not on the LPGA Tour.

Per Golfweek's Beth Ann Nichols, who broke the original story, the LPGA Tour learned of the potential violation after her playing partners reported the issue following the first round, but officials failed to take action until the weekend.

Schremmer, who missed the cut after rounds of 69 and 74, was disqualified on Saturday after officials received photo evidence.

In a statement confirming Schremmer’s disqualification, the LPGA Tour said: "Schremmer violated Model Local Rule G-11, which, per the LPGA Rules of Play Card, is in effect during all LPGA Tour competitions, except at off-site local qualifying events.

"This Model Local Rule requires that players are limited throughout their round to using only the yardage book that has been approved for use in the competition."

Schremmer has now addressed her initial denial in a statement published on Instagram Stories and shared on X by Golfweek's Cameron Jourdan.

Subscribe to the Golf Monthly newsletter to stay up to date with all the latest tour news, equipment news, reviews, head-to-heads and buyer’s guides from our team of experienced experts.

She wrote: “Over the past few days, I've spent a lot of time reflecting on what happened last week and, more importantly, how I handled the situation.

“I had no idea that I had a yardage book with illegal Information. When I was approached about it, I was scared, embarrassed, and made an extremely poor decision in saying it was not in use.

“I deeply regret that, I always will, and I want to own that mistake.”

She concluded: “This experience has given me a lot to think about, both as a golfer and as a person.

“I understand that trust is earned through actions rather than words, and I know that rebuilding it takes time.

“I am committed to learning from this, growing through it, and demonstrating through my actions that I can move forward with greater honesty, maturity, and accountability.”

Miami sophomore Schremmer is 51st in the World Amateur Golf Ranking.

She has won twice this fall and is also a member of the USGA’s 2026 Elite Amateur Program. She has also twice competed in the prestigious Augusta National Women's Amateur.

title: Rick Shiels hits back after catching strays from LIV Golf’s Chief Restructuring Officer
article_text:
Rick Shiels has hit back after finding himself on the receiving end of criticism from LIV Golf’s Chief Restructuring Officer David Orlofsky amid the collapse of LIV Golf.

Shiels is one of the most recognisable figures in golf content creation, with over 3 million subscribers to his YouTube channel.

Such is his influence in the game, Shiels took part in the Internet Invitational this year which featured 64 content creators competing for $4m.

It appeared, however, according to Front Office Sports' David Rumsey, that Orlofsky didn’t know who Shiels was when discussing those that are owed money by LIV Golf.

“As I understand it, Rick Shiels is some sort of golf influencer, but I have never heard of him,” he said when asked why he Englishman was owed $1.4m.

“So I couldn’t tell you much about him, but apparently his job was to write stuff and publicise stuff about the events. And because he has supposedly a following, people were supposed to – there’s supposed to be some value he added there. I couldn’t pick him out of a lineup.”

The $1.4m figure is what Shiels is due from the league after signing up in January 2025 on a multi-year strategic partnership as an official ambassador and content creator.

Those comments from Orlofsky are particular tone deaf, especially considering Shiels wasn’t hired to write content.

The Englishman has finally responded, however.

Shiels has established himself over the years as one of golf’s biggest and most influential content creators, especially on this side of the Atlantic.

He has played with the likes of Sir Nick Faldo and Tom Watson, while interviewing countless names in the world of professional golf through his YouTube channel.

The 40-year-old was unwilling to let the comments from Orlofsky pass though as he took to Instagram to offer his own thoughts.

“Unbelievable” replied Shiels on Ziregolf’s Instagram page stating that Orlofsky didn’t know who Shiels was, adding in a laughing face emoji.

“David who?” the Englishman also stated and it shows just how much of a fallout the collapse of LIV Golf has caused, as it isn’t just Shiels who is owed money.

Indeed, the BBC reports that the R&A are still due £500k from the Saudi-backed league, whole smaller business are also waiting on money.

“This consultancy support will help elevate conditions across the league’s 14-event season, spanning ten countries and five continents.” read an R&A statement at the time.

Elsewhere, Global Infusion Group is still due £321,671 for catering services provided at the LIV Golf UK event back in July, while cleaning company BD365 Clean are owed £75,225 for providing 108 members of staff.

Overall, creditors have submitted more than £100m in unsecured claims throughout the bankruptcy process, yet LIV has put aside just £2m to deal with those recoveries.

The numbers simply don't add up and it remains to be seen whether Shiels, or any other person/company due money by LIV will ever see a penny.

Shiels’ role during his time with LIV Golf was to spend time with each team, filming videos while bringing back his old ‘break 75’ series to showcase the league and its players.

He did previously withdraw a claim for $7,040,700 against LIV Golf Incorporated, which is separate from the $1.4m he is currently owed.

There will surely be plenty more twists and turns in this ongoing saga, no doubt about that. For Shiels, though, it is clear he isn’t one to back down from a fight given his recent replies to Orlofsky.

title: YouTube Star Peter Finch Confirmed For DP World Tour Debut
article_text:
